The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands. Juvenile polyps are a specific type of hamartomatous polyps.

name: Malrotation of colon
definition: An anatomical anomaly that results from an abnormal rotation of the gut as it returns to the abdominal cavity during embryogenesis.

name: Fulminant hepatitis
definition: Acute hepatitis complicated by acute liver failure with hepatic encephalopathy occurring less than 8 weeks after the onset of jaundice.
comments: Note that different definitions of fulminant hepatitis are used in the medical literature.

name: Intestinal lymphedema
definition: Fluid retention and edema in the intestine caused by a compromised lymphatic system.

name: Lactose intolerance
definition: An inability to digest lactose.

name: Hypoplasia of the small intestine
definition: Underdevelopment of the small intestine.

name: Esophageal ulceration
definition: Defect in the epithelium of the esophagus, essentially an open sore in the lining of the esophagus.

name: Rectoperineal fistula
definition: The presence of a fistula between the perineum and the rectum.

name: Malrotation of small bowel
definition: A deviation from the normal rotation of the midgut during embryologic development with mislocalization of the small bowel.
comments: Malrotation results not only in the malposition of the bowel but also in the malfixation of the mesentery. The normally broad mesenteric attachment is shortened to a narrow pedicle that predisposes the patient to the complication of midgut volvulus.

name: Hamartomatous stomach polyps
definition: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas located in the stomach.

name: Multiple small bowel atresias
definition: The presence of multiple areas of atresia affecting the small intestine.

name: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
definition: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract.

synonyms.text: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Recurrent infection of the GI tract

name: Episodic hemolytic anemia
definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that occurs in repeated episodes.

name: Congenital hemolytic anemia
definition: A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.

name: Acute myeloid leukemia
definition: A form of leukemia characterized by overproduction of an early myeloid cell.

name: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia
definition: Low platelet count associated with maternal platelet-specific alloantibodies.
comments: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia occurs following fetomaternal transfusions leading to generation of alloreactive antiplatelet antibodies.

name: Congenital hypoplastic anemia
definition: A type of hypoplastic anemia with congenital onset.
comments: In this condition, hematopoiesis must have been inadequate in fetal life. Affected infant have marked pallor and reticulocytopenia or absence of red blood cell precursors in an otherwise normally cellular bone marrow. This term does not refer to a particular diagnosis or etiology (or which several are known) but to the phenotypic feature.

name: B Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
definition: A type of ALL characterized by elevated levels of B-cell lymphoblasts in the bone marrow and the blood.

name: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia
definition: Sudden onset of thrombocytopenia (reduced platelet count) within 5-10 days of the transfusion of blood products. The clinical presentation is post-transfusion purpura (PTP), wigth severe thrmbocytopenia, epistaxis, and hemorrhages.
comments: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia is thought to be related to platelet-specific alloantibody from prior transfusion/pregnancy.

name: Fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia
definition: A kind of hemolytic anemia that is induced by the ingestion of fava beans.

synonyms.text: Hemolytic anaemia following ingestion of fava beans
Hemolytic anemia following ingestion of fava beans

comments: Persons with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency are susceptible to fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia because of the oxidative stress induced by compounds in Fava beans (thought to be vicine and isouramil). The same underlying defect can make affected persons susceptible to hemolysis induced by a number of mediciations.

name: Drug-sensitive hemolytic anemia
definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that is triggered by ingestion of certain drugs.

name: Normocytic hypoplastic anemia
definition: A type of hypoplastic anemia in which the erythrocytes have a normal cell volume (the mean corpuscular volume is within normal limits).

name: Acute myelomonocytic leukemia
definition: An acute leukemia characterized by the proliferation of both neutrophil and monocyte precursors.

name: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
definition: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil.

synonyms.text: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

comments: Neutrophils usually display 3-4 nuclear lobes. Hypersegmented neutrophile nuclei display 5 or more lobes. This feature can be seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency or with other etiologies.

name: Anisopoikilocytosis
definition: A type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence in the blood of erythrocytes of varying sizes and abnormal shapes.

name: Increased hemoglobin oxygen affinity
definition: An abnormal increase in the binding affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

name: Folate-unresponsive megaloblastic anemia
definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia that does not improve upon administration of folate. Since vitamin B12 acts by promoting recycling of folate, administration of vitamin B12 also does not improve this type of anemia.

name: Refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts
definition: A type of myelodysplastic syndrome characterized by less than 5% myeloblasts in the bone marrow, but with 15% or greater red cell precursors in the marrow being abnormal iron-stuffed cells called ringed sideroblasts.

name: Recurrent thromboembolism
definition: Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.

name: Microspherocytosis
definition: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.

name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
definition: A type of acute myeloid leukemia in which abnormal promyelocytes predominate.

name: Pyropoikilocytosis
definition: A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.

name: Hypochromic microcytic anemia
definition: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

name: Reduced factor XII activity
definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.

name: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia
definition: A type of hemolytic anemia in which the Coombs test is positive.
comments: The Coombs test measures a coating of immunoglobulin or complement on the red cell surface.

name: Acute monocytic leukemia
definition: The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.

name: Prolonged bleeding after surgery
definition: Bleeding that persists longer than the normal time following a surgical procedure.

name: Ph-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia
definition: A subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that results from a reciprocal translocation between the ABL-1 oncogene and a breakpoint cluster region (BCR), resulting in a fusion gene, BCR-ABL, that encodes an oncogenic protein with constitutively active tyrosine kinase activity.

name: Recurrent deep vein thrombosis
definition: Repeated episodes of the formation of a blot clot in a deep vein.

name: Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia
definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of folate.

name: Reduced leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
definition: Decreased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.

name: Intermittent thrombocytopenia
definition: Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.

name: Reduced protein S activity
definition: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.
comments: Protein S functions as a cofactor to Protein C in the inactivation of Factors Va and VIIIa in the coagulation pathway. Therefore, a defect in protein S is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

name: Normochromic microcytic anemia
definition: A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

name: Hyperchromic macrocytic anemia
definition: A type of anemia characterized by abnormally large erythrocytes with abnormally high amounts of hemoglobin.

name: Amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia
definition: Thrombocytopenia related to lack of or severe reduction in the count of megakaryocytes.

name: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.

name: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count
definition: Count of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow above the upper limit of normal. Ring sideroblasts are nucleated erythroblasts with a pathologic accumulation of iron granules in the mitochondrial matrix. They can be detected by Prussian blue staining as blue perinuclear aggregates in bone marrow aspirate erythroblasts.
comments: Sideroblastic anemia includes a group of inherited and acquired anemias of ineffective erythropoiesis characterized by an accumulation of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow and decreased production of mature red blood cells. Additionally, refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts is a type of myelodysplastic syndrome that is characterized by anemia and the presence of at least 15 percent ring sideroblasts in the marrow.

name: Impaired ADP-induced platelet aggregation
definition: Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.

name: Chronic hemolytic anemia
definition: An chronic form of hemolytic anemia.

name: Perineal fistula
definition: The presence of a fistula between the bowel and the perineum.
comments: The perineum is the diamond-shaped region of the body between the pubic arch and the anus.

name: Incisional hernia
definition: An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.

name: Spontaneous neonatal pneumothorax
definition: Pneumothorax occurring neonatally without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

name: Intercostal muscle weakness
definition: Lack of strength of the intercostal muscles, i.e., of the muscle groups running along the ribs that create and move the chest wall.

name: Intermittent hyperventilation
definition: Episodic hyperventilation.

name: Respiratory infections in early life
definition: Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections in early life, as manifested by recurrent episodes of respiratory infections.

name: Respiratory failure requiring assisted ventilation
definition: A state of respiratory distress that requires a life saving intervention in the form of gaining airway access and instituting positive pressure ventilation.

name: Intermittent episodes of respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
Elevated pulmonary artery pressure
definition: An abnormally elevated blood pressure in the circulation of the pulmonary artery.

name: Recurrent infections due to aspiration
definition: Increased susceptibility to infections due to aspiration, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infections due to aspiration.

name: Stress/infection-induced lactic acidosis
definition: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs in relation to stress or infection.

name: Persistent lactic acidosis
definition: A continuous form of lactic acidemia.

name: Severe lactic acidosis
definition: A severe form of lactic acidemia.

name: Exercise-induced lactic acidemia
definition: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs following exercise or exertion.

name: Congenital lactic acidosis
definition: A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

name: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young
definition: The term Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) was initially used for patients diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia that could be treated without insulin for more than two years, where the initial diagnosis was made at a young age (under 25 years). Thus, MODY combines characteristics of type 1 diabetes (young age at diagnosis) and type 2 diabetes (less insulin dependence than type 1 diabetes). The term MODY is now most often used to refer to a group of monogenic diseases with these characteristics. Here, the term is used to describe hyperglycemia diagnosed at a young age with no or minor insulin dependency, no evidence of insulin resistance, and lack of evidence of autoimmune destruction of the beta cells.

synonyms.text: Maturity onset diabetes of the young

name: Reduced circulating vitamin A concentration
definition: Concentration of vitamin A below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

name: Episodic metabolic acidosis
definition: Repeated transient episodes of metabolic acidosis, that is, of the buildup of acid or depletion of base due to accumulation of metabolic acids.

name: Intermittent lactic acidemia
definition: An intermittent (discontinuous) form of lactic acidemia.

name: Recurrent infantile hypoglycemia
definition: Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood occurring during the infantile period.

synonyms.text: Recurrent low blood sugar in infant

name: Impairment of galactose metabolism
definition: An impairment of galactose metabolism.

name: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis
definition: A form of metabolic acidosis with increased serum chloride levels.

name: Abnormal circulating magnesium concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of magnesium in the blood circulation.

name: Hyperphenylalaninemia
definition: The concentration of L-phenylalanine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Abnormal oral glucose tolerance
definition: An abnormal resistance to glucose, i.e., a reduction in the ability to maintain glucose levels in the blood stream within normal limits following oral administration of glucose.

name: Chronic lactic acidosis
definition: A chronic form of lactic acidemia.

name: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction
Pulmonary artery dilatation
definition: An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of the lung blood vessels

name: Arteriosclerosis of small cerebral arteries
definition: Arteriosclerosis (increased thickness, increased stiffness, loss of elasticity) of the small arteries of the brain.

synonyms.text: Hardened artery wall in small cerebral arteries

name: Ascending aortic dissection
definition: A separation of the layers within the wall of the ascending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.
comments: According to the Stanford classification, type A aortic dissection affects the ascending aorta and arch.

name: Vascular calcification
definition: Abnormal calcification of the vasculature.

name: Pulmonary artery atresia
definition: A congenital anomaly with a narrowing or complete absence of the opening between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.
comments: Pulmonary artery atresia means that unoxygenated blood in the right ventricle can not be effectively pumped into the lung for oxygenation.

name: Venous thrombosis
definition: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

name: Pulmonary artery aneurysm
definition: An aneurysm (severe localized balloon-like outward bulging) in the pulmonary artery.

name: Tortuous cerebral arteries
definition: Excessive bending, twisting, and winding of a cerebral artery.

name: Generalized arterial calcification
definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts, affecting arteries distributed throughout the body.

name: Extrahepatic portal hypertension
definition: Increased pressure in the pre-hepatic portal vein.
comments: Hypertension in the portal venous tree proper. previous def: 'has part' some ('increased pressure' and ('inheres in' some ('arterial blood' and ('part of' some 'Pre-hepatic portal vein (adult human)'))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

name: Aortic aneurysm
definition: Aortic dilatation refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted (ratio of observed to expected diameter 1.5 or more). Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.

synonyms.text: Bulge in wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe (pathological) form of dilatation of a segment of a blood vessel. In clinical practice, dilatation and aneurysm are occasionally used interchangeably. In this subhierarchy, we therefore use aneurysm as the primary label and list dilatation as a broad synonym.

name: Accelerated atherosclerosis
definition: Atherosclerosis which occurs in a person with certain risk factors (e.g., SLE, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of early heart disease) at an earlier age than would occur in another person without those risk factors.

name: Dilatation of the cerebral artery
definition: The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.
comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

name: Extracranial internal carotid artery dissection
definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.

name: Arteriovenous fistula
definition: An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.

name: Vascular tortuosity
definition: Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

name: Peripheral arterial stenosis
definition: Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.
comments: The ankle-brachial index (ABI; the ratio of systolic blood pressure in the ankle to that in the arm), is a measure of occlusion of peripheral arteries in the leg. Peripheral arterial stenosis may be observed with atherosclerosis and with increased intima media thickness as seen in diseases such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The most common cause of peripheral arterial stenosis in patients over 40 years of age is atherosclerosis. Cerebral and coronary arteries are by definition not included in peripheral artery disease.

name: Pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas
definition: A rare vascular anomaly with a direct communication between pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed.

name: obsolete Dilatation of the descending aorta
Generalized arterial tortuosity
definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.

name: Descending thoracic aorta aneurysm
definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta.

synonyms.text: Dilatation of the descending thoracic aorta

name: Absent pulmonary artery
definition: A congenital defect with aplasia (absence) of one of the right or left pulmonary artery.
comments: This is a rare feature that has been observed in recessive lethal osteogenesis imperfecta with mutation in CRTAP.

name: Pulmonary artery sling
definition: An anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery, such that it arises from the posterior aspect of the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and esophagus to reach the left hilum.

name: Thoracic aorta calcification
definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the thoracic aorta.

name: Calcification of the aorta
definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.
comments: Note that the phrase "aortic calcification" is mainly used to describe calcification of the aortic valve rather than of the aorta itself.

name: Pulmonary arterial medial hypertrophy
definition: Increase in mass of the tunica media of the arteries in the pulmonary circulation.

synonyms.text: Hypertrophy of the pulmonary artery wall

name: Medial calcification of large arteries
definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large (conduit) arteries.
comments: GitHub issue: https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/6877

name: Recurrent cerebral hemorrhage
definition: Recurrent bleeding into the parenchyma of the brain.

name: Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis
definition: Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.

name: Ascending tubular aorta aneurysm
definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.

synonyms.text: Aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
Bulging of wall of large artery located above heart

comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

name: Pulmonary artery hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the pulmonary artery.

name: Elevated mean arterial pressure
definition: An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.

name: Coarctation of abdominal aorta
definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the abdominal aorta.

name: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of the femurs
definition: Flaring of distal femur.

synonyms.text: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of distal femur

name: Bilateral radial aplasia
definition: Missing radius bone on both sides associated with congenital failure of development.

name: Metaphyseal sclerosis
definition: Abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.

synonyms.text: Increased bone density in wide portion of long bone

name: Metaphyseal rarefaction
definition: Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.

name: Mesomelic leg shortening
definition: Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

name: Rhizomelic arm shortening
definition: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).
comments: This term implies that the ulna and radius are not substantially shortened.

name: Slender long bones with narrow diaphyses
definition: Reduced diameter of a long bone with a more pronounced reduction of the diameter of the diaphysis of the long bones.

synonyms.text: Slender long bones with narrow shaft

name: Multicentric ossification of proximal humeral epiphyses
Recurrent patellar dislocation
definition: Patellar dislocation occurring repeated times.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

synonyms.text: Absent/small end part of innermost thighbone
Absent/underdeveloped end part of innermost thighbone

name: Flattened proximal radial epiphyses
definition: An abnormally flat form of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

name: Femoral bowing present at birth, straightening with time
definition: Congenital onset bending or abnormal curvature of the femur that normalizes with age.

synonyms.text: Bowing of thighbone at birth, straightening with time

comments: This feature can be diagnosed based on the medical history of congenital femoral bowing with spontaneous improvement.

name: Dumbbell-shaped humerus
definition: The humerus is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.

synonyms.text: Dumbbell-shaped long bone in upper arm

name: Osteomyelitis leading to amputation due to slow healing fractures
Mesomelic arm shortening
definition: Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

name: Dysplastic distal radial epiphyses
definition: Abnormally developed (dysplastic) distal epiphysis of the radius.

name: Diaphyseal undertubulation
definition: Tubulation refers to the size and shape of tubular bones. In children and adolescents, the modeling process regulates normal bone growth. Final shaft (tube) diameter depends on appositional bone growth and the equilibrium between periosteal and endosteal bone resorption and formation. Undertubulation refers to a broad, widened form of the shafts (diaphyses) of long bones.

synonyms.text: Thickening of shaft or central part of long bones

name: Hypoplastic distal humeri
definition: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the humerus.

synonyms.text: Wide innermost wide portion of shankbone bone
Wide innermost wide portion of shinbone bone

name: Distal ulnar hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the ulna.

name: Shortening of all phalanges of the toes
definition: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of all phalanges of the foot.

name: Unilateral ulnar hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the ulna on only one side.

name: Proximal radio-ulnar synostosis
definition: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the proximal portions of the radius and the ulna.

name: Multiple long-bone exostoses
definition: Multiple exostoses originating in long bones.

synonyms.text: Multiple exostoses of long tubular bones

name: Irregular capital femoral epiphysis
definition: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth capital femoral epiphysis.

synonyms.text: Irregular end part of innermost thighbone

name: Proximal humeral metaphyseal irregularity
definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the proximal end of the humerus (at the shoulder).

name: Diaphyseal cortical sclerosis
definition: An elevation in bone density of the cortex of one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

name: Anterolateral radial head dislocation
definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterolateral direction.

name: Metaphyseal spurs
definition: Bony outgrowths that extend laterally from the margin of the metaphysis.

synonyms.text: Fragmented, irregular end part of bone

name: Cone-shaped epiphyses fused within their metaphyses

synonyms.text: Cone-shaped end part of long bone fused within their wide portion of wide bone

name: Proximal fibular overgrowth
definition: Overgrowth of the proximal part of the fibula.

synonyms.text: Overgrowth of innermost part of calf bone

name: Proximal radial head dislocation
definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an proximal direction.

name: Wrist hypermobility
definition: The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

name: Anterior radial head dislocation
definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterior direction.

name: Limited knee flexion/extension
definition: A limited ability of the knee joint to perform extension and flexion.

name: Abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
definition: An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.

name: Lateral femoral bowing
definition: A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.

name: Streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
definition: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.

synonyms.text: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

name: Absent proximal radial epiphyses
definition: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.

name: Distal femoral bowing
definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

name: Premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes

synonyms.text: Premature birth following premature rupture of foetal membranes

name: High-frequency hearing impairment
definition: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).
comments: High frequency hearing impairment often involves loss of ability to hear consonants such as s, f, t, and z, even though vowels can be heard normally.

name: Cochlear degeneration
definition: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.

name: Calcification of the auricular cartilage
definition: Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.

name: Hypoplastic nasal septum
definition: Underdevelopment of the nasal septum.

synonyms.text: Decreased size of septum of nose

name: Abnormal nasal morphology
comments: This is a category for overall abnormal morphology that may be replaced later with more exact descriptions.

name: Abnormality of the vertebral endplates
definition: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral disks.

name: Abnormal sacrum morphology
definition: An abnormality of the sacral bone.
comments: The sacrum is the large, roughly triangular bone at the base of the verterbal column that is formed by fusion of the five sacral vertebrae S1 to S5.

name: Abnormal intervertebral disk morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of the intervertebral disk.
comments: Any abnormality of the fibrocartilaginous structures that are located between adjacent vertebral bodies.

name: Abnormal Achilles tendon morphology
definition: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

name: Atrial fibrillation
definition: An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.

synonyms.text: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

comments: The ventricular response to atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular because of the large number of atrial impulses that transit the atrioventricular node, making the ventricle partially refractory to further impulses. Atrial fibrillation can cause a number of manifestations including excessive ventricular response with angina pectoris or hypotension in susceptible individuals, syncope, systemic embolization, fatigue, or anxiety. These features should be coded separately.

name: obsolete Dilatation of the ascending aorta
Abdominal aortic aneurysm
definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.

name: Aortic arch aneurysm
definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

name: obsolete Abnormalities of the peripheral arteries
Supraventricular arrhythmia
definition: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.
comments: Supraventricular arrhythmia includes atrial arrhythmias (atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, junctional ectopic tachycardia, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (Wolf-Parkinson-White Syndrome), orthodromic or antidromic. Supraventricular arrhythmia is distinct from ventricular tachycardia, which originates in the ventricles.

name: Arterial tortuosity
definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

name: Elevated diastolic blood pressure
definition: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.
comments: Normal diastolic blood pressure is less than 80 mmHg.

name: Abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

name: Posterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
definition: An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
comments: The posterior vertebral scalloping sign appears on a lateral radiograph of the spine as an exaggeration of the normal concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies. Neurofibromatosis may be associated with marked scalloping of the posterior borders of the vertebral bodies resulting from intraspinal tumors.

name: Pericardial constriction
definition: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

name: Right ventricular dilatation
definition: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle, which can be defined echocardiographically as a right ventricular to left ventricular ratio greater than 1:1.
comments: Ventricular dilatation is to be distinguished from ventricular aneurysm, which refers to a diastolic as well as systolic outpouching of the ventricle containing endocardium, epicardium, and thin-wall non-contractile scarred myocardium, which mainly develop in the setting of a full-thickness infarct, replaced by fibrous tissue because of myocardial infarction.

name: Absence of the pulmonary valve
definition: Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.
comments: The distinctive feature of APVS is the airway obstruction caused by tracheobronchial compression that results from massive dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (PA) and its first- and second-order branches. Consequential tracheomalacia and bronchomalacia determine the timing and severity of respiratory compromise, as well as the morbidity and mortality of these patients.

name: Abnormal T-wave
definition: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.

name: Mitral annular calcification
definition: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.
comments: MAC is a common degenerative process involving the fibrous annulus of the mitral valve, and is generally an incidental finding associated with aging. This term applies if MAC occurs at a substantially younger age than usual.

name: Anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
definition: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

name: Ventricular septal hypertrophy
definition: The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.

name: Coronary artery stenosis
definition: Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.

name: Cardiac valve calcification
definition: Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.

name: Pulmonary valve defects
definition: Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.

name: Abnormal atrioventricular conduction
definition: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

name: Preductal coarctation of the aorta
definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.
comments: Blood flow to the aorta distal to the coarctation may be dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus, and hence closure of the ductus arteriosus can lead to serious ischemia of the affected tissues.

name: Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
definition: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.
comments: This HPO term intends to refer to the histological changes that characterize histiocytoid cardiomyopthy. The disease entity Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by incessant ventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, and often sudden death by age 2 years.

name: Ventricular escape rhythm
definition: A ventricular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).

name: Hypoplastic left atrium
definition: Underdeveloped, small left heart atrium

name: Concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

name: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
definition: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.
comments: Pulmonary veins drain through abnormal connections to the right atrium.

name: Abnormal left ventricular function
definition: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.

name: Dysplastic pulmonary valve
definition: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

name: Shortened PR interval
definition: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

name: Elevated right atrial pressure
definition: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.
comments: Elevated mean right atrial pressure (RAP) can be measured by cardiac catheterization.

name: Complete heart block with broad QRS complexes
definition: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.

name: Left posterior fascicular block
definition: Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

name: Membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
definition: Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.
comments: An important feature in the differential diagnosis between valvular and subvalvular aortic stenosis is the fact that no ejection sound is present in the latter.

name: Dysplastic aortic valve
definition: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

name: Premature arteriosclerosis
definition: Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

name: Complete heart block with narrow QRS complexes
definition: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.

name: Tricuspid regurgitation
definition: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.
comments: This term should not be applied to Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve (see HP:0010316).

name: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
definition: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

name: Bicuspid pulmonary valve
definition: The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.
comments: The pulmonary valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid.

name: Pericardial lymphangiectasia
definition: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

name: Prolonged QTc interval
definition: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

name: Global systolic dysfunction
definition: A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.

name: Synovial lining hyperplasia
definition: Synovial hyperplasia involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.
comments: Synovial hyperplasia is a frequent clinical finding in patients with joint injury and other joint disorders.

name: Flattened metatarsal heads
definition: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.

synonyms.text: Flattened head of long bone of foot

comments: The metatarsal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the toes.

name: Generalized morning stiffness
definition: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.

name: Stiff interphalangeal joints
definition: Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

name: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
definition: Absence of the abdominal musculature.

name: Helicobacter pylori infection
definition: A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.
comments: The bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori has co-evolved with humans and colonizes approximately half of the human population, but only causes overt gastric disease in a subset of infected hosts.

name: Spontaneous esophageal perforation
definition: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.
comments: Esophageal perforation can lead to retained gastric contents, saliva, bile, and other substances entering the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinitis, which in turn may lead to sepsis.

name: Pancreatic pseudocyst
definition: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

name: Gastric hypertrophy
definition: Hypertrophy of the stomach.

name: Secretory diarrhea
definition: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

name: Intrahepatic bile duct cysts
definition: The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.

name: Hypoplastic colon
definition: Underdevelopment of the colon.

name: Anal mucosal leukoplakia
definition: Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.

name: Pancreatic calcification
definition: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.

name: Intestinal obstruction
definition: Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.

name: Frequent Giardia lamblia infestation
definition: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.

name: Impaired mastication
definition: An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.
comments: Chewing and swallowing are interrelated. The act of chewing plays a fundamental role in the process of swallowing food. Mastication prepares food for swallowing by breaking it into small particles. Accordingly, loss of teeth has been associated with swallowing difficulties. Chewing difficulties may be caused by loss of teeth, partial dentures, or by tooth pain. Swallowing difficulties, in contrast, are often characterized by difficulties swallowing liquids, reflux, throat spasms, choking on dry food, or dysphagia.

name: Abdominal organ duplication
definition: A congenital malformation characterized by the development of an additional organ or organ-like structure, i.e., an extra copy of the organ normally located in the abdomen.

name: Anoperineal fistula
definition: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.

name: Absence of intrinsic factor
definition: Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.

synonyms.text: Intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

comments: This feature can be ascertained by immunoassay of gastric juices.

name: Bowel diverticulosis
definition: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.

name: Rectal abscess
definition: A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.

name: Intestinal edema
definition: Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.
comments: This finding can be observed upon abdominal radiography. The bowel lumen may be slightly dilated. Secondary to the fluid accumulation, there are anatomic and motor alterations in the intestine which are reflected in the roentgenogram.

name: Adenomatous colonic polyposis
definition: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.

name: Biliary tract obstruction
definition: Obstruction affecting the biliary tree.

name: Chronic gastritis
definition: A chronic form of gastritis.

name: Pancreatic dysplasia
definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.
comments: Dysplasia is defined in MPATH as a distortion or deficiency of the tissue or cellular architecture.

name: Hypoplasia of the gallbladder
definition: The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.

name: Jejunal atresia
definition: A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.

name: Chronic calcifying pancreatitis
definition: A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.

name: Degenerative liver disease
definition: The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.

name: Total intestinal aganglionosis
definition: A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.

name: Extrahepatic biliary duct atresia
definition: Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.

name: Partial abdominal muscle agenesis
definition: Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

synonyms.text: Death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

name: Intestinal hypoplasia
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the intestine.

name: Giant hypertrophic gastritis
definition: A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

name: Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
definition: Underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.

name: Intrahepatic biliary atresia
definition: Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.

name: Absence of pectoralis minor muscle
definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor.

name: Unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle
definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.

synonyms.text: Unilateral aplasia of pectoralis major muscle

name: Abnormal facility in opposing the shoulders
definition: Increased range of shoulder movement related to aplasia or hypoplasia of the clavicles that results in the ability to approximate the shoulders in front of the chest.
comments: This feature is characteristic of cleidocranial dysplasia. See Figure 2 of PMID:23289840

name: Joint hemorrhage
definition: Hemorrhage occurring within a joint.

name: Abnormal synovial membrane morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the synovium, which is a membrane that lines the cavity of synovial joints and consists of a lining layer of macrophage-like synoviocytes and fibroblast-like synoviocytes, as well as a sublining of connective tissue. Synovial cells are thought to contribute to joint homeostasis by secreting various factors such as hyaluronic acid and lubricin important for joint lubrication and function, as well as disposing of the waste products.

name: Gastritis
definition: The presence of inflammation of the gastric mucous membrane.

name: Abnormality of the gallbladder
definition: An abnormality of the gallbladder.

name: Abnormal jejunum morphology
definition: An abnormality of the jejunum, i.e., of the middle section of the small intestine.

name: Intestinal polyp
definition: A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

name: Premature delivery because of cervical insufficiency or membrane fragility
Miscarriage
definition: A pregnancy that ends at a stage in which the fetus is incapable of surviving on its own, defined as the spontaneous loss of a fetus before the 22th week of pregnancy.
comments: The age at which fetal demise is legally classified asa a miscarriage varies between countries with the US being 20 gestational weeks and the UK being 24 gestational weeks. The HPO chooses the average of these age ranges.

name: Prominent nasolabial fold
definition: Exaggerated bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion, or commissure).

name: Absent nasal septal cartilage
definition: Lack of the cartilage of the nasal septum.

synonyms.text: Failure of development of nasal septal cartilage
Decreased size of tip of nose

name: Depressed nasal bridge
definition: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.
comments: The adjective "depressed" here does not indicate an active process but a status. A depressed nasal bridge can occur irrespective of the width of the nasal bridge, and the width should be assessed independently. In infancy, the nasal bridge is relatively more posterior than in the older person. The term depressed nasal bridge should only be used when the bridge is more posterior than is typical for age and ethnic background.

synonyms.text: Decreased size of bridge of nose

name: Abnormal nostril morphology
definition: Abnormality of the nostril.

synonyms.text: Decreased size of internal carotid artery

name: Intimal thickening in the coronary arteries
Arterial dissection
definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of an artery.

name: Pseudocoarctation of the aorta
definition: Pseudocoarctation is a congenital anomaly of kinking, or buckling, of the aorta without a pressure gradient across the lesion. It is characterized by elongation and kinking of the aorta at the level of the ligamentum arteriosum.
comments: Note that the ligamentum arteriosum, which develops from the ductus arteriosus, is attached to the superior surface of the pulmonary artery and the inferior surface of the aortic arch.

name: Premature occlusive vascular stenosis
definition: Peripheral arterial stenosis with onset before the age of 50 years.

name: obsolete Atrioventricular canal defect with right ventricle aorta and pulmonary atresia
Persistent left superior vena cava
definition: A rare congenital vascular anomaly that results when the left superior cardinal vein caudal to the innominate vein fails to regress.

name: Carotid artery tortuosity
definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the carotid arteries.

name: Aortic arch calcification
definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the arch of aorta.

name: Cerebral venous thrombosis
definition: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a cerebral vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

name: Capillary hemangioma
definition: The presence of a capillary hemangioma, which are hemangiomas with small endothelial spaces.

name: Large vessel vasculitis
definition: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) affecting large arteries such as the aorta and branches of the aorta.

name: Agenesis of pulmonary vessels
definition: A developmental defect characterized by the lack of formation of the pulmonary blood vessels.

name: Pulmonary aterial intimal fibrosis
definition: Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
comments: Some causes of intimal fibrosis are hypertension, intimal fibroplasia, arterial atheroma, and CADASIL syndrome.

name: Arterial fibromuscular dysplasia
definition: An arterial lesion that is characterized by either intimal fibroplasia, with neointimal lesions of cells and matrix deposition, or medial fibroplasia, in which there is loss of smooth muscle cells and increased deposition of collagen and proteoglycans in the medial layer.
comments: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is distinct from atherosclerotic lesions in that FMD lesions do not contain inflammatory cells or lipids. Instead, the pathology of FMD. FMD can result in arterial stenosis or occlusion, and less commonly, arterial dissection or aneurysm formation. FMD can affect almost any artery but most commonly affects the renal arteries, presenting as hypertension, and the carotid and vertebral arteries, leading to ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attacks, headaches, and pulsatile tinnitus.

name: Anomalous branches of internal carotid artery
Increased pulmonary vascular resistance
definition: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) more than 3 wood units, as defined by the current definition of pulmonary hypertension. 95% of individuals have a PVR of less than 2.4 wood units.

name: Cerebral vasculitis
definition: Inflammation of the blood vessels within the brain.

synonyms.text: Lack of facial fat below the skin

name: Mandibulofacial dysostosis
definition: A type of craniofacial dysostosis associated with abnormalities of the external ears, mirognathia, macrostomia, coloboma of the lower eyelid, and cleft palate. This is a bundled term that is left in the HPO now for convenience with legacy annotations but should not be used for new annotations.

name: Hemifacial hypertrophy
definition: Unilateral overgrowth of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.

synonyms.text: Increase in size of half of face

name: Disturbance of facial expression
definition: An abnormality of the gestures or movements executed with the facial muscles with which emotions such as fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and disgust can be expressed.

name: Extension of hair growth on temples to lateral eyebrow
definition: A pattern of hair growth in which there is hair extending from the temples to the lateral eyebrows.

synonyms.text: Unusual hairline with hair growth on temples extending to lateral eyebrow

name: Hypoplastic philtrum
definition: Underdevelopment of the philtrum.

name: Progeroid facial appearance
definition: A degree of wrinkling of the facial skin that is more than expected for the age of the individual, leading to a prematurely aged appearance.

name: Recurrent mandibular subluxations
definition: Recurrent partial dislocations of the mandible.

name: Sparse lateral eyebrow
definition: Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of lateral eyebrow hairs.

synonyms.text: Limited hair on end of eyebrow

comments: Abnormal sparseness of the eyebrows laterally.

name: Abnormality of complement system
definition: An abnormality of the complement system.
comments: The complement system represents a family of over 25 serum proteins and cell surface receptors that act in a cascade manner leading to innate functions such as inflammation and enhancement of adaptive immunity. Three general pathways, i.e. classical, lectin and alternative, activate the complement system.

name: Autonomic bladder dysfunction
definition: Abnormal bladder function (increased urge or frequency of urination or urge incontinence) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

name: Hypoplasia of the bladder
definition: Underdevelopment of the urinary bladder.

name: Abnormal carotid artery morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of the carotid arteries, including the common carotid artery and its' arterial branches.

name: Abnormal vena cava morphology
definition: An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

name: Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve
definition: Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve (TCS) is a rare congenital airway malformation in which distinct tracheal rings are replaced by a continuous cartilaginous segment. Vertically fused C- or O-shaped cartilaginous rings can extend from the subglottis to the carina or bronchus with little to no pars membranacea posteriorly. Comment:Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve has been associated with various craniosynostosis syndromes.

name: Inspiratory stridor
definition: Inspiratory stridor is a high pitched sound upon inspiration that is generally related to laryngeal abnormalities.

name: Hypoplasia of the epiglottis
definition: Hypoplasia of the epiglottis.

name: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency
definition: A primary immune deficiency that is characterized by defects or deficiencies of T-lymphocytes that causes specific susceptibility to intracellular micro-organisms.
comments: Several diseases are classified as severe T cell immunodeficiencies: severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID), reticular dysgenesis, thymic dysplasia (Nezelof syndrome), combined immunodeficiency disease (CID), and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS).

name: Recurrent herpes
definition: Increased susceptibility to herpesvirus, as manifested by recurrent episodes of herpesvirus.

name: Decreased circulating complement factor I concentration
definition: Concentration of the complement component factor I in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: Defective B cell differentiation
definition: Reduced functionality of the process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a B cell. A B cell is a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.

name: Aplasia of the thymus
definition: Absence of the thymus. This feature may be appreciated by the lack of a thymic shadow upon radiographic examination.

name: Susceptibility to chickenpox
definition: Increased susceptibility to chicken pox, as manifested by recurrent episodes of chicken pox.

name: Humoral immunodeficiency
definition: A general term referring to a defect in immunity resulting from impaired antibody production.
comments: If possible it is preferable to use a precise description of the observed manifestations leading to the inference of humoral immunodeficiency.

name: Recurrent streptococcus pneumoniae infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to streptococcus pneumoniae infections as manifested by a history of recurrent infections by streptococcus pneumoniae.

name: Abnormality of humoral immunity
definition: An abnormality of the humoral immune system, which comprises antibodies produced by B cells as well as the complement system.

name: Decreased circulating complement factor H concentration
definition: Concentration of the complement component factor H in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: Abnormal B cell physiology
definition: An abnormality of the physiological functioning of B cells.
comments: This term refers to any abnormality of the B cells, which play a role in the humoral immune response. The main functions of B cells are to produce antibodies, to perform the role of antigen presenting cells, and to develop into memory cells.

name: Cellular immunodeficiency
definition: An immunodeficiency characterized by defective cell-mediated immunity or humoral immunity.

name: Recurrent Haemophilus influenzae infection
definition: Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Haemophilus influenzae infection.

name: Recurrent Neisseria meningitidis infection
definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria meningitidis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Neisseria meningitidis infection.

synonyms.text: Increased susceptibility to neisseria meningitidis infections

name: Defective B cell activation
definition: A reduced ability of a B cell to become activated, i.e., the change in morphology and behavior of

name: Recurrent protozoan infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to protozoan infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of protozoan infection.

name: Combined immunodeficiency
definition: A group of phenotypically heterogeneous genetic disorders characterized by profound deficiencies of T- and B-cell function, which predispose the patients to both infectious and noninfectious complications.

name: Depletion of components of the alternative complement pathway
definition: An abnormal reduction in the components of the alternative complement pathway, such as the C3 protein or its cleavage products.

name: Recurrent opportunistic infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by opportunistic agents, i.e., by microorganisms that do not usually cause disease in a healthy host, but are able to infect a host with a compromised immune system.

name: Susceptibility to coronavirus 229e
definition: Increased susceptibility to coronavirus 229e, as manifested by recurrent episodes of coronavirus 229e.

name: Reduction of neutrophil motility
definition: An abnormal reduction of the cell motility of neutrophils.

name: Recurrent Candida infection
definition: Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Candida infection.

name: Decreased total T cell count
definition: Abnormal decrease in the absolute number of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, per microliter of blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

synonyms.text: Decreased absolute count of circulating T cells

name: Increased total B cell count
definition: The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is above the upper limit of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.

name: Recurrent bacterial skin infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections of the skin, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infectious dermatitis.
comments: Infectious dermatitis may manifest as impetigo, multiple purulent blisters, erythema, lymphadenopathy near the site of infection.

name: obsolete Decreased proportion of CD4-positive helper T cells
obsolete Markedly reduced T cell function
Chronic intestinal candidiasis
definition: Persistent overgrowth of Candida albicans in the gastrointestinal tract.

name: Elevated circulating alpha-globulin concentration
definition: The concentration of alpha-globulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Decreased total CD8+ T cell proportion
definition: Abnormal decrease of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

synonyms.text: Decreased proportion of CD8+ T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8-positive T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells

name: Decreased circulating complement factor B concentration
definition: Concentration of the complement component factor B in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: Decreased T cell activation
definition: Decreased or impaired activation of T cells in response to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

name: Recurrent gram-negative bacterial infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to infection by gram-negative bacteria, as manifested by a medical history of repeated or frequent infections by these agents.
comments: Gram-negative bacteria have a unique outer membrane, a thinner layer of peptidoglycan compared to gram-positive bacteria, and a periplasmic space between the cell wall and the membrane.

name: Decreased circulating complement C3 concentration
definition: Concentration of the complement component C3 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: Absence of CD8+ T cells
definition: Lack of detectible CD8-positive T cells

name: Dysfunctional alternative complement pathway
definition: An abnormality of the functioning of any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.

name: Absent specific antibody response
definition: Inability of the immune system to produce targeted, protective antibodies (immunoglobulins) against specific pathogens or vaccines in the setting of normal or near-normal serum levels of total IgG, IgA, and IgM and normal absolute counts of B cells and T cells.

name: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections
definition: An increased susceptibility to infections involving both the paranasal sinuses and the lungs, as manifested by a history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections.

name: Recurrent systemic pyogenic infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to systemic pyogenic infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of systemic pyogenic infections.

name: Recurrent Neisserial infections
definition: Recurrent infections by bacteria of the genus Neisseria, including N. meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis).

name: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
definition: At birth, newborns are endowed with maternal antibodies. IgG production normally begins at the age of two months. A delay in recovery from this physiological hypogammaglobulinemia between the 3rd and the 6th month of life, and of recovery period between 18 and 36 months defines transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy.

name: Recurrent infections in infancy and early childhood
definition: Recurrent infections at an early age with improvement in later childhood.

name: Maxillozygomatic hypoplasia
definition: Hypoplasia of the maxillozygomatic complex.

synonyms.text: Decreased projection of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex
Decreased size of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex

name: Sclerotic cranial sutures
definition: An increased density in the cranial sutures following obliteration.

name: Widely patent coronal suture
definition: The presence of a coronal suture (the cranial suture that separates the frontal and parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

name: Enlarged posterior fossa
definition: Abnormal increased size of the posterior cranial fossa.

name: Obtuse angle of mandible
definition: Abnormally flat (obtuse) angle of the mandible. The angle of the mandibular, located at the junction between the body and the ramus of the mandible, is normally close to being a right angle. This terms describes an abnormal increase of this angle such that the mandible appears flatter than normal.
comments: See PMID:17213440 Figure 1G for an example of an obtuse mandibular angle.

name: Calvarial osteosclerosis
definition: An increase in bone density affecting the calvaria (roof of the skull).

name: Absent/hypoplastic paranasal sinuses
definition: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the paranasal sinuses.

name: Absent ethmoidal sinuses
definition: Lack (aplasia) of the ethmoidal sinus.

synonyms.text: Failure of development of ethmoid sinuses

name: Premature closure of fontanelles
definition: Normally, the posterior and lateral fontanelles are obliterated by about six months after birth, the anterior fontanelle closes by about the middle of the second year. This term refers to the situation in which the fontanelles close at an inappropriately early time point.

synonyms.text: Early closure of the bregma sutures
Early closure of the cranial sutures
Premature closure of the bregma sutures
Premature closure of the cranial sutures

name: Calcification of falx cerebri
definition: The presence of calcium deposition in the falx cerebri.

name: Craniofacial osteosclerosis
definition: Abnormally increased density of craniofacial bone tissue.

name: Facial hyperostosis
definition: Excessive growth (overgrowth) of the facial bones, that is of the facial skeleton.

synonyms.text: Increase in size of the facial bones

name: Hypoplasia of the frontal bone
definition: Underdevelopment of the frontal bone.

synonyms.text: Decreased size of bone of forehead

name: Flat occiput
definition: Reduced convexity of the occiput (posterior part of skull).
comments: Reduced convexity of the occiput gives an appearance of flattening. There are no objective measures for convexity of the occiput, and evaluation depends heavily on the experience of the observer. This finding may or may not be accompanied by Brachycephaly (which should be coded separately), and may be observed more frequently when an infant is placed to sleep on his/her back. Occipital plagiocephaly can result from fusion or sclerosis of the lambdoid suture. If unilateral, this is accompanied by unilateral occipital flattening and bulging of the ispilateral frontal bone.

name: Fusion of middle ear ossicles
definition: Bony fusion of malleus, incus, and stapes.

name: Decreased calvarial ossification
definition: Abnormal reduction in ossification of the calvaria (roof of the skull consisting of the frontal bone, parietal bones, temporal bones, and occipital bone).
comments: A hypomineralised skull castes little or no acoustic shadow on prenatal ultrasound. This makes visualization of the intracranial anatomy clearer than normal. In conditions associated with profound hypomineralisation, the skull shape can be distorted by pressure from the ultrasound transducer later in pregnancy.

name: Widely patent sagittal suture
definition: The presence of a sagittal suture (the cranial suture that separates the left and right parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

name: Progressive sclerosis of skull base
definition: Progressively increasing bone density of the skull base without significant changes in bony contour.

name: Decreased circulating IgE concentration
definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin E (IgE) in blood.

name: Abnormality of the alternative complement pathway
definition: A deviation in any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.
comments: The alternative complement pathway is one of three complement pathways, which is an innate component of the immune system's natural defense against infections. The alternative complement pathway has three unique components, factor B, factor D, and properdin. {xref="PMID:16424154"}

name: Abnormal epiglottis morphology
definition: An abnormality of the epiglottis.

name: Secondary microcephaly
definition: Head circumference which falls below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender because of insufficient head growth after birth.

synonyms.text: Development of small head that was not present at birth

name: Small fontanelle
definition: A fontanelle that is small for age.

name: Prominent metopic ridge
definition: Vertical bony ridge positioned in the midline of the forehead.
comments: The ridge may extend from the hairline to the glabella or may be partial. The frontal suture of the skull is a dense connective tissue structure that divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and usually undergoes closure by the age of six years. A persistent frontal suture is known as a metopic suture or sutura frontalis persistens. This can lead to a ridged appearance of the forehead.

name: Postnatal macrocephaly
definition: The postnatal development of an abnormally large skull (macrocephaly).

name: Metopic suture patent to nasal root
definition: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone in infants and usually fuses by the age of six years. The suture runs from the bregma (the point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture) to the nasion or nasal root. This term applies if the suture is widely patent from bregma to nasal root.
comments: This feature is a characteristic of Schinzel-Giedion midface retraction syndrome.

name: Midline skin dimples over anterior/posterior fontanelles
Chronic myelogenous leukemia
definition: A myeloproliferative disorder characterized by increased proliferation of the granulocytic cell line without the loss of their capacity to differentiate.

name: Hemoglobin Barts
definition: Normal adult hemoglobin is composed of two chains each of alpha and beta globin. Hb Barts (Hemoglobin Barts) is a tetramer with four gamma globin chains, and is essentially pathognomonic for one or another form of alpha thalassemia. Hb Barts has an extremely high affinity for oxygen, resulting in almost no oxygen delivery to the tissues.
comments: Hb Bart is normally not present in adult blood. It makes up about 85-90 percent of hemoglobin in Hb Bart hydrops fetalis syndrome, and about 2-5 percent in HbH disease.

name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgM concentration
definition: Presence of a monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum.
comments: This is a characteristic feature of Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM), which is defined as a B-cell lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, characterized by monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum and infiltration of bone marrow with lymphoplasmacytic cells.

name: Transient erythroblastopenia
definition: A transient reduction in the number of erythroblasts in the circulation.

synonyms.text: Transient decrease in blood erythrocyte number

comments: An erythroblast, the immediate precursor of a normal erythrocyte which, still retains a cell nucleus.

name: Heinz body anemia
definition: Anemia characterized by abnormal intracellular inclusions, composed of denatured hemoglobin, found on the membrane of red blood cells.

name: obsolete Impaired neutrophil killing of staphylococci
Increased megakaryocyte count
definition: Increased megakaryocyte number, i.e., of platelet precursor cells, present in the bone marrow.

name: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia
definition: A type of T-cell lymphoma in which cancerous T-cells may present in the blood (leukemia), lymph nodes (lymphoma), skin or in multiple areas.
comments: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia is linked to infection by the human T-cell lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1).

name: Increased mean corpuscular volume
definition: Larger than normal size of erythrocytes.
comments: Macrocytosis refers to a mean cell volume (MCV) greater than 100 fL. If macrocytosis is an isolated abnormality, the amount of hemoglobin in the cell increases proportionately, so the mean cell hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) remains within normal limits.

name: Chronic disseminated intravascular coagulation
definition: A chronic form of disseminated intravascular coagulation in which a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus is present and destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
definition: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is characterized by the widespread activation of coagulation, which results in the intravascular formation of fibrin and ultimately thrombotic occlusion of small and midsize vessels.
comments: DIC is a complex syndrome in which there is pathological generation of thrombin and diffuse intravascular clot formation. DIC may occur as acute decompensated or chronic compensated form. In acute decompensated DIC, there is a sudden massive exposure of tissue factor over a brief time period; Intravascular coagulation can also compromise the blood supply to organs and, in conjunction with hemodynamic and metabolic derangements, may contribute to the failure of multiple organs. At the same time, the use and subsequent depletion of platelets and coagulation proteins resulting from the ongoing coagulation may induce severe bleeding. Chronic DIC, also known as compensated DIC, results from a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus. Under such conditions, destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

name: Pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anemia
definition: A type of sideroblastic anemia that is alleviated by pyridoxine (vitamin B-6) treatment.

name: Lymphoid leukemia
definition: A malignant lymphocytic neoplasm of B-cell or T-cell lineage involving primarily the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. This category includes precursor or acute lymphoblastic leukemias and chronic leukemias.

name: Reduced kininogen activity
definition: Amount or activity of kininogen is below the lower limit of normal. Kininogen functions as a cofactor in the contact phase of the intrinsic blood coagulation cascade.
comments: Kininogen is cleaved into the following 6 chains: 1) Kininogen-1 heavy chain; 2) T-kinin; 3) Bradykinin; 4) Lysyl-bradykinin; 5) Kininogen-1 light chain; and 6) Low molecular weight growth-promoting factor.

name: Bone marrow hypocellularity
definition: A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.

name: Biphenotypic acute leukemia
definition: A type of actue leukemia with features characteristic of both the myeloid and lymphoid lineages. These leukemias are for this reason are designated mixed-lineage, hybrid or biphenotypic acute leukemias.

name: Transient myeloproliferative syndrome
definition: A unique clonal neoplastic disorder that is linked to trisomy 21, is restricted to neonatal period, and spontaneously regresses. It often has characteristics of megakaryocytic lineage and is associated with GATA1 mutations in myeloblasts.

name: Exercise-induced hemolysis
definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that can be triggered by exertion.

name: Decreased mean platelet volume
definition: Average platelet volume below the lower limit of the normal reference interval.
comments: Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a measure of the average size of platelets, with a typical reference range of 7.5 to 11.5 femtoliters (fL).

name: T cell chronic lymphocytic lymphoma/leukemia
