synonyms.text: Narrowness of interpediculate distances in lower thoracic regions

name: Narrow anterio-posterior vertebral body diameter
definition: An abnormal reduction of the anterioposterior diameter of the vertebral body.

synonyms.text: Reduced anterior-posterior diameter of vertebral bodies

name: Poorly ossified cervical vertebrae
definition: Decreased ossification of the cervical vertebral bodies, i.e., of the Cervical vertebrae set.

name: Cervical spondylosis
definition: Arthrosis, i.e., of degenerative joint disease, affecting the cervical vertebral column.
comments: When osteoarthritis affects the spine, it is known as spondylosis.

name: Cervical vertebral bodies with decreased anteroposterior diameter
Thoracolumbar interpediculate narrowness
definition: A reduction of the distance between thoracolumbar vertebral pedicles.

name: Lumbar interpedicular narrowing
definition: Narrowing (becoming gradually narrower) of the distance between lumbar vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal (lower) end of the vertebral column.

name: Spondylolisthesis at L5-S1
definition: Complete bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis resulting in the anterior slippage of the fifth lumbar vertebral body (L5) onto the sacrum (level S1).

name: Premature anterior fontanel closure
definition: Early closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.

name: Inferior lens subluxation
definition: Partial displacement of the lens in the inferior direction.

name: High hypermetropia
definition: A severe form of hypermetropia with over +5.00 diopters.

name: obsolete Median cleft lip and palate
Moderate sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: The presence of a moderate form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

name: Central posterior corneal opacity
definition: Reduced transparency of the central posterior portion of the corneal stroma.

name: Bilateral conductive hearing impairment
definition: A bilateral type of conductive hearing impairment.

name: Abnormality of the vertebral spinous processes
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the sacrum
definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the sacral bone.

name: Abnormal coccyx morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of the coccyx.

name: Posterior helix pit
definition: Permanent indentation on the posteromedial aspect of the helix that may be sharply or indistinctly delineated.

synonyms.text: Indentation in back of outer ear
Pits in posterior aspect of ear helices

comments: They are usually linear to a narrow oval in shape and may be single or multiple.

name: Congenital sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A type of hearing impairment caused by an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve with congenital onset.

name: Long hairs growing from helix of pinna

synonyms.text: Long hairs growing from helix of ear

name: Absence of acoustic reflex
definition: Absence of the acoustic reflex, an involuntary contraction of the stapedius muscle that occurs in response to high-intensity sound stimuli.

synonyms.text: Absence of acoustic middle ear muscle reflexes

comments: Note that the acoustic reflex is also referred to as stapedius reflex, attenuation reflex, or auditory reflex.

name: Cleft at the superior portion of the pinna

synonyms.text: Cleft at the superior portion of the ear

comments: This term is used for Auriculocondylar syndrome (MIM:602483). Not clear if there is a clean delineation against cleft helix.

name: Low-frequency hearing loss
definition: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the low frequencies of sound (125 Hz to 1000 Hz).

name: Abnormally folded helix
definition: Any structural anomaly of the border of the helix, which usually forms a rolled rim but is highly variable in shape.

name: Microtia
definition: Underdevelopment of the external ear.
comments: The definitions of microtia follow a widely used, surgically based, classification of ear anomalies outlined by Weerda 1988. As microtia indicates at least both decreased length and width, and in more severe forms it includes abnormal shape of structures, all forms are acknowledged to be bundled terms, but are retained here because they are well established.

name: Cochlear malformation
definition: The presence of a malformed cochlea.
comments: A cochlear malformation may include a membranous abnormality, a bony abnormality, or a combination of the two.

name: Absent vestibular function
definition: Complete lack of functioning of the vestibular apparatus.

name: Vestibular areflexia
definition: Vestibular areflexia can be measured as the absence of the caloric nystagmus response in electronystagmography.

name: Microtia, second degree
definition: Median longitudinal length of the ear more than two standard deviations below the mean in the presence of some, but not all, parts of the normal ear.

name: Low-frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects primarily the lower frequencies.

name: Underfolded helix
definition: Underdevelopment of the helix that either affects the entire helix, or is localized.
comments: Helix folding is highly variable, and the range is illustrated in Figures 29 and 30. To use this term, the affected area must be too long to be considered a Cleft helix. Underdevelopment of part of the helix can lead to the impression that the scaphal area is enlarged.

name: Underfolded superior helices
definition: A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a lesser degree than normal.

name: Hypoplasia of the cochlea
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the cochlea.

name: Mild neurosensory hearing impairment
definition: The presence of a mild form of sensorineural hearing impairment.
comments: A neurosensory hearing loss with a deficit of 21-40 dB.

name: Slit-like opening of the exterior auditory meatus
definition: A type of stenosis of the external auditory meatus in which the opening of the external auditory meatus appears as a vertical slit.

name: Hypoplastic helices
definition: Underdevelopment of the helix, i.e., of the outer rim of the pinna.

name: Congenital conductive hearing impairment
definition: A type of conductive deafness with congenital onset.

name: Prominent antitragus
definition: Increased anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.

name: Postlingual sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment with onset after the acquisition of speech.

name: Mild conductive hearing impairment
definition: A mild form of conductive hearing impairment.
comments: Conductive hearing impairment with 21-40 dB deficit.

synonyms.text: Deformed external ear on one side

name: Supraauricular pit
definition: Benign congenital lesion of the supraauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

name: Progressive conductive hearing impairment
definition: A progressive type of conductive deafness.

name: Abnormal middle ear morphology
definition: An abnormality of the morphology or structure of the middle ear.

synonyms.text: Morphological abnormality of the middle ear

name: Infantile sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment with infantile onset.

name: Adult onset sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: The presence of sensorineural deafness with late onset.

name: Bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects both ears.

name: Severe sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A severe form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

name: Abnormal stapes morphology
definition: An abnormality of the stapes, a stirrup-shaped ossicle in the middle ear.

name: Pulsatile tinnitus
definition: Pulsatile tinnitus is generally classified a kind of objective tinnitus, meaning that it is not only audible to the patient but also to the examiner on auscultation of the auditory canal and/or of surrounding structures with use of an auscultation tube or stethoscope. Usually, pulsatile tinnitus is heard as a lower pitched thumping or booming, a rougher blowing sound which is coincidental with respiration, or as a clicking, higher pitched rhythmic sensation.
comments: Pulsatile tinnitus may be associated with vascular abnormalities such as arterioevenous shunts or glomus tumors or the jugular vein, arterial bruits related to a high-riding carotid artery (close to the auditory areas) or carotid stenosis, or venous abnormalities such as a dehiscent jugular bulb or to hypertension. Finally, in some patients, mechanical abnormalities such patulous eustachian tubes, palatomyoclonus (small spasms of muscles in the soft palate area), or idiopathic stapedial muscle spasm may represent the underlying cause of pulsatile tinnitus.

name: Ureteral dysgenesis
definition: A developmental anomaly of the ureter.
comments: If possible, a more specific term describing the precise type of ureteral dysgenesis should be chosen.

name: Agonadism
definition: Absence of sex glands (gonads are the organs that produce gametes; testis in males and ovary in females).
comments: Gonadal agenesis refers to the lack of development of gonads during fetal development; it may not be possible clinically to determine if gonal tissue was present at any point of development. For this reason, we regard agonadism and gonadal agenesis as synonymous.

name: Urinary bladder wall hypertrophy
definition: Increase in thickness of the wall of the urinary bladder. This finding may be seen in conditions such as bladder outlet obstruction and may be accompanied by increased trabeculation of the bladder wall musculature.

synonyms.text: Hypertrophy of the urinary bladder wall

name: Nephroblastomatosis
definition: Presence of persistent islands of renal blastema in the postnatal kidney. Nephroblastomatosis represents a complex abnormality of nephrogenesis and has been defined as the persistence of metanephricblastema into infancy and childhood.

name: Uric acid urolithiasis independent of gout
Autonomic erectile dysfunction
definition: Impotence (inability to develop or maintain an erection) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

name: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
definition: A type of extracapillary glomerulonephritis characterized by the formation of crescent-like cellular proliferation.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fallopian tube
definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the fallopian tube.

name: Multiple small medullary renal cysts
definition: The presence of many cysts in the medulla of the kidney.
comments: This feature is the cardinal sign of medullary cystic disease, also known as medullary sponge disease.

name: Renotubular dysgenesis
definition: A developmental defect characterized by absence or poor development of proximal renal tubules.
comments: Renotubular dysgenesis is generally accompanied by early onset and persistent oligohydramnios that leads to the Potter sequence.

name: Urethral stenosis
definition: Abnormal narrowing of the urethra.

name: Renal sarcoma
definition: A sarcoma of the kidney.

name: Clitoral hypertrophy
definition: Hypertrophy of the clitoris.
comments: Increased size of the clitoris.

name: Gonadal dysgenesis, male
definition: Unusual gonadal development in a person with a 46,XY male karyotype, leading to an unassigned sex differentiation.

name: Abnormal spermatogenesis
definition: Incomplete maturation or aberrant formation of the male gametes.

name: Calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis
definition: The presence of calcium- and oxalate-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

name: Congenital megaureter
definition: A developmental disturbance with extreme ureteral dilatation.
comments: The cause of congenital megaloureter is thought to be aperistalsis of the distal ureter, leading to dilatation. The defect in peristalsis may be due to faulty development of muscle layers of ureter, that is, there is a functional, not a mechanical cause of obstruction.

name: Congenital nephrotic syndrome
definition: Nephrotic syndrome with onset within the first three months of life.

name: Renal hypoplasia/aplasia
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the kidney.

name: Renal tubular epithelial necrosis
definition: Coagulative necrosis of tubular epithelial cells, defined as cells with increased cytoplasmic eosinophilia and nucleus that has a condensed chromatin pattern with fuzzy nuclear contour or has barely visible nuclear basophilic staining. The extent of cortical tubular necrosis is scoredsemiquantitatively as none, mild (less than 25% tubules with necrosis), moderate (25-50 percent), and severe (over 50%).
comments: Renal tubular epithelial necrosis is a histomorphological definition that corresponds to the clinical term of acture tubular necrosis. Acute death of renal tubular cells that usually results from prolonged renal ischemia, nephrotoxins, or sepsis. The clinical course of acute tubular necrosis may be divided into initiation, maintenance, and recovery phases.

name: Enlarged labia minora
definition: Increase in size of the folds of skin between the outer labia.

name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the uterus
definition: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the uterus.

name: Bilateral cryptorchidism
definition: Absence of both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

name: Solitary bladder diverticulum
definition: Presence of a single diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.

name: Renal hamartoma
definition: A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that are native to the kidneys.

name: Hypoplasia of the fallopian tube
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the fallopian tube.

name: Gonadal calcification
definition: Deposition of calcium salts in gonadal tissue.

name: Absent scrotum
definition: Congenital absence of the scrotum.
comments: Both the sac and rugae are absent. This finding may be accompanied by an (Apparently) absent testis and Cryptorchidism, which should be coded separately.

name: Partial development of the penile shaft
definition: A congenital condition of the external male genitalia in which the shaft of the penis fails to fully develop.
comments: This feature is based on a description in PMID:15273283 for Sudden infant death with dysgenesis of the testes syndrome (OMIM:608800).

name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
definition: The presence of non-malignant hyperplasia of the prostate.

name: Urethrovaginal fistula
definition: The presence of a fistula between the vagina and the urethra.

name: Unilateral renal atrophy
definition: A unilateral form of atrophy of the kidney.

name: Unilateral renal dysplasia
definition: A unilateral form of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

name: Urethral diverticulum
definition: The presence of a diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urethra.

name: Gonadal dysgenesis with female appearance, male
definition: Unusual gonadal development in a person with a 46,XY male karyotype, leading to a more female sex differentiation.
comments: Very bad term - try to get rid of it later.

name: Hypoplasia of the ovary
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the ovary.

name: Hypoplasia of the vagina
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the vagina.

name: Female external genitalia in individual with 46,XY karyotype
definition: The presence of female external genitalia in a person with a male karyotype.

name: Renal hypophosphatemia
definition: Renal hypophosphatemia is defined as reduced serum phosphate (e.g., below 0.70 mmol/l) and an inappropriately high renal phosphate excretion.
comments: Three primary mechanisms of hypophosphatemia exist: increased renal excretion, decreased intestinal absorption, and movement of phosphate from the extracellular to intracellular compartments. The initial step in diagnosis involves determining whether hypophosphatemia is renal or nonrenal.

name: Dysplastic testis
definition: A descriptive term denoting a developmental anomaly of the male gonad characterized by architectural disorganization of the testicular parenchyma, which may include irregular or poorly formed seminiferous tubules, a thinned tunica albuginea, and increased or fibrotic interstitial tissue. Macroscopically, the testis may range from near-normal in size and appearance to a small, firm, or streak-like structure.

name: Decreased testicular size
definition: Reduced volume of the testicle (the male gonad).

name: Partially duplicated kidney
definition: The presence of a partially duplicated kidney.

name: Longitudinal vaginal septum
definition: The presence of a longitudinal vaginal septum, thereby creating a vaginal duplication.

name: Coronal hypospadias
definition: A mild form of hypospadias in which the urethra opens just under the corona glandis, that is, where the head of the penis meets the shaft.

name: Abnormal aryepiglottic fold morphology
definition: An abnormality of the aryepiglottic fold.
comments: The aryepiglottic fold is a fold of mucous membrane extending on each side between the lateral border of the epiglottis and the summit of the arytenoid cartilage.

name: Cartilaginous ossification of larynx
definition: Ossification affecting the set of cartilages of larynx.
comments: This term describes abnormal ossification affecting one or more of the cartilages of the larnyx (cricoid cartilage, thyroid cartilage, epiglottic cartilage, arytenoid cartilage, corniculate cartilage, cuneiform cartilage, triticeal cartilage, and sesamoid cartilage).

name: Laryngeal hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the larynx.

name: Laryngeal atresia
definition: Congenital absence of the lumen of the larynx. Laryngeal atresia is a rare condition. If the laryngeal opening fails to develop, fluid secreted by the lungs cannot be expelled. In a fetus with laryngeal atresia, the lungs are either normal or hyperplastic, not hypoplastic. Mortality is reported as 100%. At obstetric US examination, views of the fetal neck demonstrate a dilated trachea filled with trapped fluid. Views of the fetal chest show enlarged, hyperechoic lungs, with dilated fluid-filled bronchi. Fetal ascites is usually present.
comments: Laryngeal atresia results from failure of recanalization of the laryngotracheal tube during the third month of gestation. Laryngeal atresia manifests as acute airway obstruction in the newborn immediately following clamping of the umbilical cord and is fatal without immediate airway management with a tracheotomy. Congenital laryngeal atresia is a rare anomaly that is mostly incompatible with life. Most authors claim that this malformation is related to an arrest of the sixth brachial arch at different gestational stages during normal embryologic development. Complete laryngeal atresia results in a desperate emergency during the first few moments of life, and surgical intervention must occur within 2 to 5 minutes of birth to enable respiration. The most dramatic physical finding is that the child is aphonic, with absence of any cry or gasp at birth.

name: Laryngeal cleft
definition: Presence of a gap in the posterior laryngotracheal wall with a continuity between the larynx and the esophagus.
comments: Embryologically, the trachea and esophagus share a common lumen until they are separated by the development of the tracheoesophageal septum. Failure of this fusion and incomplete development of the tracheoesophageal septum may lead to congenital abnormalities such as isolatedlaryngeal cleft, tracheoesophageal fistula, and esophageal atresia, depending on the severity of the abnormality. Patients with laryngeal cleft may present with feeding difficulty, chronic cough, stridor, pneumonia or respiratory distress, depending on the size of the cleft.

name: Laryngeal cartilage malformation
definition: A malformation of the laryngeal cartilage.

synonyms.text: Vocal impairment, severe, due to laryngeal cartilage abnormalities

name: Aplasia of the epiglottis
definition: Absence of the epiglottis.

name: Laryngeal calcification
definition: Calcification (abnormal deposits of calcium) in the laryngeal tissues.

name: Bowing of the vocal cords
definition: Bowing (abnormal curvature) of the vocal folds.

name: Unilateral vocal cord paralysis
definition: A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on one side.

synonyms.text: Unilateral paralysis of the vocal cord

name: Violent behavior
definition: Conduct and/or behavior, both verbal and non-verbal, including but not limited to verbal and/or physical aggression, attacks, threats, harassment, intimidation, and other disruptive behaviors in any form or through any medium, that cause or have the potential to cause a reasonable person to fear physical harm from any individual(s) or group(s) towards any person(s) or property. This is commonly defined as a violent act characterized by the use of physical force, anger, or sudden intense activity.

name: No social interaction
definition: Lack of intentional participation in interactions with another person.

name: Auditory hallucination
definition: Perception of sounds without auditory stimulus.

name: Self-mutilation of tongue and lips due to involuntary movements
definition: Uncontrolled movements result in tissue damage to the tongue and lips.

synonyms.text: Self-mutilation of tongue and lips due to involuntary movements

name: Abnormal sexual behavior
definition: A deviation of sexual behaviors from the personal norms of the individual in the context of socially and culturally recognized patterns of human sexual behaviors.

name: Obsessive-compulsive trait
definition: The presence of one or more obsessive-compulsive personality traits. Obsessions refer to persistent intrusive thoughts, and compulsions to intrusive behaviors, which the affected person experiences as involuntary, senseless, or repugnant.
comments: Obsessions have been defined as intrusive and unwanted thoughts that are subjectively experienced as unacceptable.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ear
definition: The presence of aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the ear.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the external ear
definition: The presence of aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of all or part of the external ear.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle ear
definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of all or part of the middle ear.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the inner ear
definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the inner ear.

name: Abnormal prostate morphology
definition: An abnormality of the prostate.

name: Abnormal renal artery morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of the renal artery.

name: Abnormal vocal cord morphology
definition: An abnormality of the vocal cord.
comments: The vocal cords, also known as the vocal folds, represent a subdivision of the larynx, and consist of twin infoldings of mucous membrane stretched horizontally across the larynx.

name: Wide proximal femoral metaphysis
definition: Increased width of the proximal part of the shaft (metaphysis) of the femur.

name: Wide capital femoral epiphyses
definition: Abnormally wide morphology of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

synonyms.text: Wide end part of innermost thighbone

name: Delayed ossification of pubic rami
definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the rami (branches) of the pubic bone.

name: Iliac crest serration
definition: Irregularities of the iliac crest that produce the appearance of a lace border around it.

name: Delayed pubic bone ossification
definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the pubic bone.

name: Cone-shaped capital femoral epiphysis
definition: A cone-shaped deformity of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

synonyms.text: Cone-shaped end part of innermost thighbone

name: Dysplastic iliac wing
definition: A general term that describes a congenital defect in the iliac wing resulting from abnormal development.

name: Femoral retroversion
definition: An abnormal backward rotation of the hip relative to the knee such that the hips are externally rotated with the foot pointed outward instead of straight ahead (out-toeing).
comments: Femoral torsion, also known as femoral rotation or femoral version, refers to the twist between the proximal and distal parts of the femur on the transverse plane. Femoral anteversion averages between 30-40 degrees at birth, and between 8-14 degrees in adults. This term applies if the amount of femoral torsion is below this range.

name: Early ossification of capital femoral epiphyses
definition: Developmental acceleration of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

name: Widened greater sciatic notch
definition: The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a increase in the lateral dimension of the notch.

name: Limited hip movement
definition: A decreased ability to move the femur at the hip joint associated with a decreased range of motion of the hip.

name: Hypoplasia of the lesser trochanter
definition: Underdevelopment of the lesser trochanter.

name: Hypoplasia of the femoral head
definition: Underdevelopment of the femoral head.

name: Broad femoral head
definition: Increased width of the femoral head.

name: Acetabular dysplasia
definition: A smaller than normal acetabulum that has insufficient femoral head coverage leading to abnormal hip joint contact pressures, instability and pain.

synonyms.text: Decreased femoral head coverage by acetabulum

comments: Acetabular dysplasia can lead to hip pain and early-onset hip osteoarthritis.

name: High iliac wing
definition: Increased height of the wing (or ala) of the ilium (which is the large expanded portion which bounds the greater pelvis laterally).

name: Flattened femoral head
definition: An abnormally flattened femoral head.

name: Aplastic pubic bone
definition: A developmental defect characterized by lack of development of the pubis bone.

name: Large iliac wing
definition: Increased size of the ilium ala.

name: Narrow femoral neck
definition: An abnormally reduced diameter of the femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

name: Absent ossification of capital femoral epiphysis
definition: Lack of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

synonyms.text: Absent ossification of femoral capital epiphyses

comments: The ossification center of the capital femoral epiphysis appears at the end of the first year after birth.

name: Hypoplastic ischiopubic ramus
definition: Underdevelopment of the ischiopubic ramus, which is comprised of the inferior pubic ramus and the inferior ramus of the ischium.

name: Inferior pubic ramus hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the lower branch of the pubis bone (inferior pubic ramus).
comments: The pubis is the anterior part of the hip bone and forms the anterior and inferior borders of the obturator foramen (the obturator foramen is the opening between the ischium and pubic bones). It is divisible into a body, a superior and an inferior ramus.

name: Hypoplastic iliac body
definition: Underdevelopment of the body of ilium.

name: obsolete Dislocation of the femoral head
Delayed proximal femoral epiphyseal ossification
definition: Developmental delay of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

synonyms.text: Delayed ossification of the proximal femoral epiphysis

comments: The proximal femoral epiphyseal ossification center normally appears at about age 6 months.

name: Delayed femoral head ossification
definition: Delayed ossification of the femoral head.

synonyms.text: Delayed maturation of the head of the thigh bone

name: Hypoplastic pubic ramus
definition: Underdevelopment of a ramus (branch) of the pubic bone.

name: Multicentric femoral head ossification
definition: There is normally one ossification center in the head of the femur. This term applies if there are multiple such centers.
comments: Additionally, the ossification center of the capital femoral epiphysis appears at the end of the first year after birth. This is not what this term refers to.

synonyms.text: Speckled calcifications in end part of innermost long bone of upper arm

name: Hypoplastic pelvis
definition: Underdevelopment of the bony pelvis.

name: Mesomelic short stature
definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by disproportionate shortening of the medial parts of the extremities (forearm or lower leg).

name: Severe intrauterine growth retardation
definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is 4 or more standard deviations below average, corrected for sex and gestational age.

name: Moderately short stature
definition: A moderate degree of short stature, more than -3 SD but not more than -4 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.

name: Severe postnatal growth retardation
definition: Severely slow or limited growth after birth, being four standard deviations or more below age- and sex-related norms.

name: Moderate postnatal growth retardation
definition: A moderate degree of slow or limited growth after birth, being between three and four standard deviations below age- and sex-related norms.

name: Neonatal short-trunk short stature
definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with congenital onset recognizable at birth.

name: Failure to thrive secondary to recurrent infections
definition: Insufficient weight gain or inappropriate weight loss for a child, that is attributed to an endogenous recurrent infections.

synonyms.text: Faltering weight secondary to recurrent infections
Weight faltering secondary to recurrent infections

name: Feeding difficulties in infancy
definition: Impaired feeding performance of an infant as manifested by difficulties such as weak and ineffective sucking, brief bursts of sucking, and falling asleep during sucking. There may be difficulties with chewing or maintaining attention.

name: Disproportionate short-limb short stature
definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short limbs but an average-sized trunk.
comments: A type of dwarfism (marked short stature with adult height below 147 cm) in which the limbs are disproportionately affected. Note that brachymelia is a general term referring to shortening of the limbs. Micromelia refers to the shortening of entire limbs (in contrast to rhizomelia, mesomelia, and acromelia, which refer to shortening of the proximal, middle, or distal portions of the limbs).

name: Mild intrauterine growth retardation
definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 2 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 3 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

name: Adipose tissue loss
definition: A reduction in the amount of adipose tissue (fat) compared with the amount previously present in an individual.

name: Postnatal growth retardation
definition: Slow or limited growth after birth.

name: Rhizomelia
definition: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of limbs (i.e. the femur and humerus).

synonyms.text: Disproportionately short upper portion of limb

name: Childhood-onset truncal obesity
definition: Truncal obesity with onset during childhood, defined as between 2 and 10 years of age.

name: Neonatal short-limb short stature
definition: A type of short-limbed dwarfism that is manifest beginning in the neonatal period.

synonyms.text: Short limb dwarfism recognisable at birth
Short limb dwarfism recognizable at birth

name: Childhood-onset short-trunk short stature
definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with onset in childhood.

synonyms.text: Disproportionate short-trunk short stature, identifiable in childhood

name: Generalized neonatal hypotonia
definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) manifesting in the neonatal period and affecting the entire musculature.

synonyms.text: Generalised low muscle tone in neonate
Generalized low muscle tone in neonate

name: Axial hypotonia
definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) affecting the musculature of the trunk.

name: Generalized lymphadenopathy
definition: A generalized form of lymphadenopathy.

synonyms.text: Swollen lymph nodes affecting all regions of the body

name: Acute rhabdomyolysis
definition: An acute form of rhabdomyolysis.

name: Distal lower limb amyotrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy of distal leg muscles.
comments: Distal lower limb muscle atrophy is commonly due to peripheral neuropathy.

name: Loss of ability to walk in early childhood
Pelvic girdle amyotrophy
definition: Atrophy of the muscles of the pelvic girdle (also known as hip girdle), i.e., the gluteal muscles, the lateral rotators, the adductors, the psoas major and the iliacus muscle.

name: Floppy infant
definition: Floppiness/hypotonia is defined as reduced resistance to passive movement of joints. Physical examination of floppy/hypotonic infants shows head lag, lack of shoulder and elbow muscle contraction on traction response, inability to tighten the shoulder girdle muscles (or slipping through) when held under the axillae, scarf sign (when the arm is pulled to the opposite side, the arm wraps around the neck with the elbow crossing midline), hyperdorsiflexion of the feet, easy apposition of the thumb against the forearm, feet touching the cheek with ease and without discomfort, frog leg position, and inverted U sign on ventral suspension (head, arms, and legs hanging down without elbow or knee flexion and the trunk rounded in a dome shape).
comments: This term should not be used for new annotations. Instead, state the type of onset of hypotonia more exactly.

name: Proximal upper limb amyotrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy affecting proximally located muscles of the arms.

synonyms.text: Proximal muscle atrophy in upper limbs

name: Shoulder muscle hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the shoulder.

name: Pectoralis major hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the pectoralis major.
comments: The pectoralis major is a thick, fan-shaped muscle of the anterior chest.

name: Intrinsic hand muscle atrophy
definition: Atrophy of the intrinsic muscle groups of the hand, comprising the thenar and hypothenar muscles; the interossei muscles; and the lumbrical muscles.

name: Progressive distal muscular atrophy
definition: Progressive muscular atrophy affecting muscles in the distal portions of the extremities.

name: Proximal lower limb amyotrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy affecting proximally located muscles of the legs, i.e., of the thigh.

name: Distal upper limb muscle weakness
definition: Reduced strength of the distal musculature of the arms.

name: Calf muscle hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the muscuklature of the calf.

name: Tibialis muscle weakness
definition: Muscle weakness affecting the tibialis anterior muscle.
comments: This is a bundled term which should be made obsolete.

name: Nonprogressive muscular atrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy that does not display a progression in severity with time.

name: Exercise-induced muscle stiffness
definition: A type of muscle stiffness that occurs following physical exertion.

name: Muscle hypertrophy of the lower extremities
definition: Muscle hypertrophy primarily affecting the legs.

name: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain
definition: Decreased activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.

synonyms.text: Decreased activities of mitochondrial-encoded respiratory chain complexes
Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory complexes

name: Calf muscle hypertrophy
definition: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the calf muscles.

synonyms.text: Muscular hypertrophy of the calf muscles

comments: Distal lower limb hypertrophy

name: Neck muscle hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the neck.

name: Increased intramuscular fat
definition: An abnormal increase in the amount of intramuscular fat tissue.

name: Agenesis of the diaphragm
definition: Congenital lack, i.e., aplasia of the diaphragm.
comments: An extremely large diaphragmatic defect, or apparent absence of the hemidiaphragm, is called agenesis of the diaphragm; this defect probably represents the severe end of the Bochdalek hernia spectrum rather than a distinct entity.

name: Pelvic girdle muscle atrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles that attach to the pelvic girdle (the gluteal muscles, the lateral rotators, adductor magnus, adductor brevis, adductor longus, pectineus, and gracilis muscles).

name: Exercise-induced leg cramps
definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles of the leg brought on by physical exertion.

name: Increased intraabdominal fat
definition: An abnormal increase in the amount of intraabdominal fat tissue.

name: Proximal lower limb muscle weakness
definition: A lack of strength of the proximal muscles of the legs.

synonyms.text: Proximal muscle weakness in lower limbs

name: Proximal upper limb muscle weakness
definition: A lack of strength of the proximal muscles of the arms.

synonyms.text: Proximal muscle weakness in upper limbs

name: Pectoralis hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the pectoral muscle.

name: Loss of truncal subcutaneous adipose tissue
definition: Loss (reduction of previously present) of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the region of the trunk.

synonyms.text: Loss of fat tissue in trunk
Loss of subcutaneous truncal adipose tissue

name: Increased subcutaneous truncal adipose tissue
definition: The presence of an abnormally increased amount of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the trunk of the body.

synonyms.text: Increased fat below the skin in trunk

name: Hypoplasia of the musculature
definition: Underdevelopment of the musculature.

name: Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles
Biceps hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of the biceps muscle.

name: Hypoplasia of serratus anterior muscle
definition: Underdevelopment of the serratus anterior muscle, which is involved in abduction, upward Rotation, and elevation of the scapula.

name: Upper limb muscle hypoplasia
definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the arm.

name: Loss of gluteal subcutaneous adipose tissue
definition: Loss (reduction of previously present) of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the gluteal region.

synonyms.text: Loss of fat tissue below the skin in gluts

name: Progressive loss of facial adipose tissue

synonyms.text: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face, progressive
Progressive loss of facial subcutaneous adipose tissue
Progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face

name: Exercise-induced muscle fatigue
definition: An abnormally increased tendency towards muscle fatigue induced by physical exercise.

name: Abdominal wall muscle weakness
definition: Decreased strength of the abdominal musculature.
comments: This may be associated with protuberance of the abdomen.

name: Increased connective tissue
definition: The presence of an abnormally increased amount of connective tissue.

name: Hypoplasia of latissimus dorsi muscle
definition: Underdevelopment of the latissimus dorsi muscle, which is involved in adduction, extension, internal rotation, and transverse extension of the shoulder and assists in movement of the scapula.

name: Foot dorsiflexor weakness
definition: Weakness of the muscles responsible for dorsiflexion of the foot, that is, of the movement of the toes towards the shin. The foot dorsiflexors include the tibialis anterior, the extensor hallucis longus, the extensor digitorum longus, and the peroneus tertius muscles.
comments: Dorsiflexion of the foot extends the foot superiorly, as if taking the foot off the gas pedal.

name: Generalized weakness of limb muscles
definition: Generalized weakness of the muscles of the arms and legs.

name: Amyotrophy of ankle musculature
definition: Atrophy of the muscles of the ankle.

name: Exercise-induced rhabdomyolysis
definition: Rhabdomyolysis induced by exercise.

name: Difficulty running
definition: Reduced ability to run.

name: Peroneal muscle atrophy
definition: Atrophy of the peroneous muscles, peroneus longus (also known as Fibularis longus), Peroneus brevis (also known as fibularis brevis, and Peroneus tertius (also known as fibularis tertius).
comments: The peroneus muscles (longus, brevis, and tertius) originate on the fibula and insert on the metatarsals.

name: Quadriceps muscle atrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy involving the quadriceps muscle.

name: Increased muscle glycogen content
definition: An increased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.

name: Distal lower limb muscle weakness
definition: Reduced strength of the distal musculature of the legs.

synonyms.text: Distal muscle weakness in lower limbs

comments: This finding can be due to peripheral neuropathy.

name: Generalized limb muscle atrophy
definition: Generalized (unlocalized) atrophy affecting muscles of the limbs in both proximal and distal locations.

synonyms.text: Generalised muscle atrophy, proximal and distal
Generalized muscle atrophy, proximal and distal

name: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from upper limbs

synonyms.text: Loss of fat tissue below the skin from upper limbs

name: Increased muscle lipid content
definition: An abnormal accumulation of lipids in skeletal muscle.
comments: Increased neutral lipid content may be observed on muscle biopsies specimen with the specific staining of Sudan black or oil red O techniques by optic microscopy.

name: Scapular muscle atrophy
definition: Atrophy of the muscles that are responsible for moving the scapula, which are the levator scapulae, the infraspinatus muscle, the teres major, the teres minor, and the supraspinatus muscle.
comments: Need to add new UBERON term for scapula muscle

name: Progressive distal muscle weakness
definition: Progressively reduced strength of the distal musculature.

name: Generalized lipodystrophy
definition: Generalized degenerative changes of the fat tissue.

name: Progressive spinal muscular atrophy
definition: Progressive spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

name: Inflammatory myopathy
definition: Chronic muscle inflammation accompanied by muscle weakness.

name: Decreased Achilles reflex
definition: Decreased intensity of the Achilles reflex (also known as the ankle jerk reflex), which can be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.

name: Progressive proximal muscle weakness
definition: Lack of strength of the proximal muscles that becomes progressively more severe.
comments: Removed logical definition that used anonymous class. Outstanding term request in UBERON for proximal muscle organ.

name: Weakness of long finger extensor muscles
Midline notch of upper alveolar ridge

synonyms.text: Midline cleft of maxillary alveolar process
Midline cleft of upper alveolar ridge
Midline notch of maxillary alveolar process
Midline notch of maxillary alveolar ridge
Midline notch of upper gum ridge

name: Alveolar ridge overgrowth
definition: Increased width of the alveolar ridges.

synonyms.text: Hyperplasia of alveolar process of jaw

comments: This finding may or may not be accompanied by increased height of the alveolar ridge. This is not to be confused with Prominent palatal ridges or gingival overgrowth. This distinction of gingival from alveolar ridge overgrowth may be difficult, especially in milder degrees of the finding.

name: Speech articulation difficulties
definition: Impairment in the physical production of speech sounds.
comments: Speech articulation difficulties can result from abnormalities of the vocal tract (the larynx and the pharyngeal, oral, and nasal cavities).

synonyms.text: Progressive hypertrophy of alveolar process of jaw

name: Recurrent oral thrush
definition: Chronic accumulation and overgrowth of the fungus Candida albicans on the mucous membranes of the mouth, generally manifested as associated with creamy white lesions on the tongue or inner cheeks, occasionally spreading to the gums, tonsils, palate or oropharynx.

name: Median cleft palate
definition: Cleft palate of the midline of the palate.

synonyms.text: Thick anterior alveolar process of jaw

name: Submucous cleft lip
definition: A cleft of the lip with overlying mucous membrane.
comments: Submucous cleft lip may lead to increased nasal resonance.

name: Anterior open-bite malocclusion
definition: Anterior open bite is a malocclusion characterized by a gap between the anterior teeth (incisors), that is, by a deficiency in the normal vertical overlap between antagonist incisal edges when the posterior teeth are in occlusion.

synonyms.text: Absence of overlap of anterior upper and lower teeth
Anterior open bite between upper and lower teeth
Gap between upper and lower front teeth when biting

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the pubic bone
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the pubic bone.

name: Abnormal ossification of the pubic bone
definition: Abnormal ossification (bone tissue formation) affecting the pubic bone, also known as the pubis.

synonyms.text: Abnormal maturation of the pubic bone

name: Abnormal pelvis bone ossification
definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the bony pelvis.

synonyms.text: Abnormal maturation of the pelvis bone
Abnormal ossification involving the bones of the pelvis

name: Abnormal ossification involving the femoral head and neck

synonyms.text: Abnormal maturation of thigh bone head and neck

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the femoral head and neck

synonyms.text: Absent/small head and neck of thighbone
Absent/underdeveloped head and neck of thighbone

name: Denervation of the diaphragm
definition: Interruption of the innervation of the diaphragm.

name: Diaphragmatic eventration
definition: A congenital failure of muscular development of part or all of one or both hemidiaphragms, resulting in superior displacement of abdominal viscera and altered lung development.

name: Aplasia of the left hemidiaphragm
definition: Congenital absence of the left half of the diaphragm.

name: Diaphragmatic weakness
definition: A decrease in the strength of the diaphragm.
comments: Diaphragmatic paralysis is an extreme form of diaphragmatic weakness. Weakness of the diaphragm can result from abnormalities at any site along its neuromuscular axis, although it most frequently arises from diseases in the phrenic nerves or from myopathies affecting the diaphragm itself. Presence of diaphragmatic weakness may be suspected from the complaint of dyspnea (particularly on exertion) or orthopnea; or the presence of rapid, shallow breathing or, more importantly, paradoxical inward motion of the abdomen during inspiration on physical examination.

name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving the skeleton
definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of one or more components of the skeleton.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the skull
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the maxilla
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the maxilla.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the mandible
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the mandible.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the frontal sinuses
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of frontal sinus.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the sinuses
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of a cranial sinus or sinuses.

name: Abnormal axial skeleton morphology
definition: An abnormality of the axial skeleton, which comprises the skull, the vertebral column, the ribs and the sternum.

name: Aplasia/hypoplasia affecting bones of the axial skeleton
definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of bones of the axial skeleton.

name: Mixed hypo- and hyperpigmentation of the skin
Abnormal adipose tissue morphology
definition: An abnormality of adipose tissue, which is loose connective tissue composed of adipocytes.

name: Lipodystrophy
definition: Degenerative changes of the fat tissue.

synonyms.text: Inability to make and keep healthy fat tissue

name: Increased adipose tissue
definition: An increase in adipose tissue mass by hyperplastic growth (increase in the number of adipocytes) or by hypertrophic growth (increase in the size of adipocytes occurring primarily by lipid accumulation within the cell).

name: Abnormal appendicular muscle morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of the appendicular musculature, comprising muscles of the upper limb and pectoral girdle as well as muscles of the lower limb and pelvic girdle.

synonyms.text: Muscle issues in the arms and/or legs

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the musculature of the extremities
Upper limb amyotrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the upper limbs.

name: Hand muscle atrophy
definition: Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the hand.

synonyms.text: Amyotrophy involving the musculature of the hand

comments: This term can be used to described bilateral amyotrophy of the musculature of the hand.

name: Abnormality of the musculature of the thorax
definition: A disease or lesion affecting the muscles of the thorax.

name: Abnormal tarsal bone mineral density
definition: This term applies to all changes in bone mineral density of the tarsal bones, which (depending on severity) can be seen on x-rays as a change in density and or structure of the bone.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of bone mineral density involving tarsal bones

name: Osteolysis involving bones of the feet
Duplication involving bones of the feet

synonyms.text: Duplication involving bones of the feet

name: Synostosis involving bones of the lower limbs
definition: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones lower limbs.

synonyms.text: Fusion involving the bones of the lower limbs

name: Osteolysis involving bones of the lower limbs
Synostosis involving bones of the feet

synonyms.text: Fusion involving the bones of the feet

name: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in muscle tissue

synonyms.text: Depletion of mitochondrial dna in skeletal muscle tissue

name: Duplication of bones involving the upper extremities

synonyms.text: Duplication of bones involving the upper extremities

name: Supernumerary bones of the axial skeleton
Abnormal cerebral artery morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of a cerebral artery. The cerebral arteries comprise three main pairs of arteries and their branches, which supply the cerebrum of the brain. These are the anterior cerebral artery, the middle cerebral artery, and the posterior cerebral artery.

name: Enlarged epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.

synonyms.text: Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger
Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger

name: Small epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.

synonyms.text: Small end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Small end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger
Small end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger

name: Triangular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.

synonyms.text: Delta-shaped epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
Triangular end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Triangular end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger
Triangular end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger

name: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the little (5th) finger.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of the innermost bone little finger
Abnormality of the innermost bone pinkie finger
Abnormality of the innermost bone pinky finger

name: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the 5th finger.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of end part of little finger bone
Abnormality of end part of pinkie finger bone
Abnormality of end part of pinky finger bone

name: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the fifth finger. This epiphysis is located on the proximal end of the phalanx.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger

name: Triangular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.

synonyms.text: Delta-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
Triangular end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Triangular end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Triangular end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger

name: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of the phalanx.

synonyms.text: Angel-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Cone-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger

name: Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Sclerosis of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.

synonyms.text: Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger

name: Enlarged epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.

synonyms.text: Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger

name: Small epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.

synonyms.text: Small end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Small end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Small end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger

name: Absent epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
definition: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger.

synonyms.text: Absent end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Absent end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Absent end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger

Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched metacarpal (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the metacarpal), a partially fused appearance of the two bones (in most cases the fused bone resembles a Y-shape), or two separate metacarpal bones appearing side to side.

comments: Thumb placement index greater than 0.55; or, the base of the thumb appears closer to the wrist than is typical. name: Bracket epiphyses of the thumb

name: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the thumb

Finger symphalangism
definition: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones of the fingers. The synonymous term "symphalangism of the hand" may be translated as fusions of bones of varying digree, that involve at least one phalangeal bone of the hand. If bony fusions are referred to as "Symphalangism" the fusion occurs in a proximo-distal axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers in a radio-ulnar axis are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly.

synonyms.text: Synostosis involving bones of the fingers

name: Metacarpal synostosis
definition: Fusion involving two or more metacarpal bones (A synostosis of the first metacarpal and the proximal phalanx of the thumb can also be observed, note that the first metacarpal bone corresponds to a proximal phalanx).

name: Carpal synostosis
definition: Synostosis (bony fusion) involving one or more bones of the carpus (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, pisiform).

name: Synostosis involving the 1st metacarpal
definition: Fusion of the 1st metacarpal with another bone. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2 to 5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

synonyms.text: Fusion involving 1st long bone of hand

name: Chronic CSF lymphocytosis
definition: Chronic cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lymphocytosis is defined as the finding, in at least two serial CSF examinations, of more than 5 cells per cubic millimeter.

synonyms.text: Fusion involving the 2nd long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 3rd long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 4th long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 5th long bone of hand

name: Increased CSF interferon alpha
definition: Increased concentration of interferon alpha in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: Chilblains
definition: Chilblains, also called perniosis, are an inflammatory skin condition related to an abnormal vascular response to the cold. We are unaware of a reliable estimate of incidence. It typically presents as tender, pruritic red or bluish lesions located symmetrically on the dorsal aspect of the fingers, toes, ears and nose. Less commonly, reports describe involvement of the thighs and buttocks. The lesions present hours after exposure to cold and usually resolve spontaneously in one to three weeks.

name: Retinal capillary hemangioma
definition: A benign vascular tumor of the retina without any neoplastic characteristics.

name: Spinal hemangioblastoma
definition: A hemangioblastoma of the spinal cord.

name: Abnormal epididymis morphology
definition: An abnormality of the epididymis.
comments: The epididymis is the structure that connects efferent ductules to vas deferens.

name: Papillary cystadenoma of the epididymis
definition: A cystadenoma, an epithelial tumor, that originates within the head of the epididymis.
comments: Papillary cystadenomas of the epididymis are partially or completely cystic or solid lesions, between 1-3 cm in diameter and arise from the efferent duct epithelium of the head of epididymis.

name: Subependymal nodules
definition: Small nodular masses which originate in the subependymal region of the lateral ventricles and protrude into the ventricular cavity. They may represent subependymal hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis.

name: Cortical tubers
definition: Cortical tubers in the brain are hamartomatous lesions typically located at the gray-white matter interface, commonly in the frontal and parietal lobes. Cortical tubers are composed of abnormal glial and neural cells, and the size, number, and location vary among patients.

name: Subependymal giant-cell astrocytoma
definition: A demarcated, largely intraventricular tumor in the region of the foramen of Monro composed of spindle to large plump or ganglion-like cells with eosinophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and somewhat pleomorphic nuclei with occasional prominent nucleoli. These tumors are almost always associated with tuberous sclerosis.

name: Hypomelanotic macule
definition: Hypomelanotic macules ("ash leaf spots") are white or lighter patches of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by a lack of melanin. White ash leaf-shaped macules are considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.
comments: While hypopigmentation is a general term that refers to any form of decreased or absent skin pigmentation, hypomelanosis more specifically refers to a reduction of epidermal melanin.

name: Adenoma sebaceum
definition: The presence of a sebaceous adenoma with origin in the sebum secreting cells of the skin.
comments: Facial angiofibromas, also known as adenoma sebaceum, are reddish papillary lesions (fibrous skin tumors) that are found around the nose, cheeks, and chin and considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.

name: Shagreen patch
definition: A plaque representing a connective-tissue nevus. Connective tissue naevi are uncommon skin lesions that occur when the deeper layers of the skin do not develop correctly or the components of these layers occur in the wrong proportion. Shagreen patches are oval-shaped and nevoid, skin-colored or occasionally pigmented, smooth or crinkled. The word shagreen refers to a type of roughened untanned leather.

name: Dental enamel pits
definition: The presence of small depressions in the dental enamel.

name: Abnormal subungual morphology
definition: A lesion located beneath a fingernail or toenail.

name: Subungual fibromas
definition: The presence of fibromata beneath finger or toenails.

name: Bladder neoplasm
definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary bladder.

name: Renal neoplasm
definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the kidney.

name: Achromatic retinal patches
definition: Areas of the retina lacking pigmentation. Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation less than 1 disk diameter in size and tending to be located in the midperiphery of the retina.

synonyms.text: Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation

name: Neoplasm of striated muscle
definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in striated muscle, either skeletal muscle or cardiac muscle.

name: Cardiac rhabdomyoma
definition: A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.

name: Rhabdomyoma
definition: A benign tumor of striated muscle.

name: Cerebral hamartoma
definition: The presence of a hamartoma of the cerebrum.
comments: Hamartomatous lesions (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) affecting and sometimes originating from the cerebrum.

name: Plexiform neurofibroma
definition: A neurofibroma in which Schwann cells proliferate inside the nerve sheath, producing an irregularly thickened, distorted, tortuous structure.

name: Glioma
definition: The presence of a glioma, which is a neoplasm of the central nervous system originating from a glial cell (astrocytes or oligodendrocytes).
comments: Gliomas can be classified as 1) ependymomas, 2) astrocytomas (including glioblastoma multiforme), 3 oligodendrogliomas, and 4) mixed gliomas, such as oligoastrocytomas.

name: Optic nerve glioma
definition: A glioma originating in the optic nerve or optic chiasm.

name: Spinal neurofibroma
definition: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the spine.
comments: Spinal neurofibromas can affect the spinal cord or the spinal nerve roots. Spinal neurofibromas can occur at cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral levels.

name: Tibial pseudarthrosis
definition: Pseudarthrosis, or "false joint" of the tibia is the result of a developmental failure in the tibia progressing to spontaneous fracture and subsequent fibrous nonunion. The fracture is rarely present at birth but commonly develops during the first 18 months of life.

name: Lisch nodules
definition: The presence of pigmented, oval and dome-shaped raised hamartomatous nevi of the iris..

name: Abnormal antihelix morphology
definition: An abnormality of the antihelix.
comments: An abnormal form of the antihelix, which is the curved prominence of cartilage, parallel with and in front of the helix, and which divides into the crura antihelicis, between which is a triangular depression, the fossa triangularis.

name: Hypoplasia of the antihelix
definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the antihelix.

name: Aplasia of the parotid gland
definition: Absence of the parotid gland.

name: Nephrosclerosis
definition: Nephrosclerosis refers to thickening or scarring ("sclerosis") resulting from damage to the renal arterioles, also referred to as arteriosclerosis of the kidney arteries.

name: Stiff shoulders
definition: Shoulder joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in shoulders when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

name: Distichiasis
definition: Double rows of eyelashes.
comments: Distichiasis can be defined as the abnormal growth of lashes from the orifices of the Meibomian glands on the posterior lamella of the tarsal plate, resulting in a double row of eyelashes.

name: Abnormal spinal dura mater morphology
definition: An abnormality of the spinal dura mater, which is the outermost of the three layers of the meninges surrounding the spinal cord.

synonyms.text: Abnormality of the spinal dura mater

name: Spinal arachnoid cyst
definition: Presence of arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal extradurally in the epidural space.

synonyms.text: Epidural arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal

name: Thick nasal septum
definition: Abnormally increased thickness of the nasal septum.

name: Lumbosacral hirsutism
definition: Abnormally increased hair growth in the lumbosacral region.

name: Large earlobe
definition: Increased volume of the earlobe, that is, abnormally prominent ear lobules.
comments: All gradations in size of the earlobe may be seen from absent to clearly enlarged compared to average. This finding is highly variable. Lobe size increases throughout adulthood.

name: Aplasia of the pectoralis major muscle
definition: Absence of the pectoralis major muscle.

name: Cleft in skull base
definition: A bony defect in the skull base.

name: Fibrous syngnathia
definition: Complete or nearly complete soft tissue fusion of the alveolar ridges.
comments: This finding is associated with severely reduced mobility, or lack of mobility, between the upper and lower jaws. This finding is the severe end of a spectrum that includes oral synechiae.

name: Ankyloblepharon
definition: Partial fusion of the upper and lower eyelid margins by single or multiple bands of tissue.
comments: A minimally expressed form, especially when located fully laterally, may be more difficult to ascertain and would be a subjective feature. A band may break and leave no evidence of its presence. Note that the term is distinct from cryptophthalmos.

name: Popliteal pterygium
definition: A pterygium (or pterygia) occurring in the popliteal region (the back of the knee).

name: Intercrural pterygium
definition: A pterygium (or pterygia) in the intercrural (groin) region.

name: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails
definition: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails is a rare and distinctive anomaly seen in popliteal pterygia syndrome.

name: Neck pterygia
definition: Pterygia affecting the neck.

name: Antecubital pterygium
definition: Pterygium affecting the elbow. This is a cutaneous web that can lead to severe flexion contracture of the elbow joint. Antecubital pterygium can be unilateral, bilateral, symmetric, or asysmmetric.

name: Anterior clefting of vertebral bodies
definition: Anterior schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.

name: Facial wrinkling
definition: Excessive wrinkling of the skin of the face.

name: Limb pain
definition: Chronic pain in the limbs with no clear focal etiology.

name: Low hanging columella
definition: Columella extending inferior to the level of the nasal base, when viewed from the side.

synonyms.text: Columella extends below the ala nasi
Extension of the columella below the ala nasi

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the hand
definition: Small or missing phalangeal bones of the fingers of the hand.

name: Broad phalanges of the hand
definition: Increased width of the phalanges of the hand.

synonyms.text: Widening of phalanges of the hand

name: Bullet-shaped phalanges of the hand
definition: The presence of short and wide phalanges which taper distally ("bullet shaped").

synonyms.text: Conical bullet-shaped distal ends of phalanges

name: Osteolytic defects of the phalanges of the hand
definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the phalanges of the hand.

synonyms.text: Breakdown of small bones of fingers

name: Patchy sclerosis of finger phalanx
definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.

Uneven increase in bone density in finger bone

name: obsolete Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand
Triangular shaped phalanges of the hand
Amniotic constriction ring
definition: Annular constrictions around the digits, limbs, or trunk, occurring congenitally (sometimes causing intrauterine autoamputation) and also associated with a wide variety of disorders. Constrictive amniotic bands are the result of primary amniotic rupture, which can lead to entanglement of fetal tissue (especially limbs) in fibrous amniotic strands.
comments: Pseudoainhum is a rare condition of unknown etiology that produces digital constricting rings, most commonly on the small fingers.

name: Adactyly
definition: The absence of all phalanges of all the digits of a limb and the associated soft tissues.
comments: This descriptor does not require absence of the metacarpal or metatarsal bones. A qualifying phrase is added to specify which limb has the attribute of adactyly.

name: Absent thumb
definition: Absent thumb, i.e., the absence of both phalanges of a thumb and the associated soft tissues.

name: Short thumb
definition: Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the thumb.

name: 3-4 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes three and four.

name: Iliac horns
definition: Horn-like malformations of the iliac crests with symmetrical bilateral central posterior iliac processes. A characteristic finding in the Nail-Patella syndrome. Iliac horns are visible on X-ray and may be palpable, but are asymptomatic.

name: Lester's sign
definition: A zone of darker pigmentation around the central part of the iris with a roughly cloverleaf or flower shape.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the biceps
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the biceps muscle.

name: Biceps aplasia
definition: Absence of the biceps muscle.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the triceps
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the triceps muscle.

name: Triceps aplasia
definition: Absence of the triceps muscle.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the musculature of the thigh
definition: Absence or underdevelopment involving the musculature of the thigh.

name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the quadriceps
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the quadriceps muscle.

name: Quadriceps aplasia
definition: Absence of the quadriceps muscle.

name: Perianal abscess
definition: The presence of an abscess located around the anus.

name: Hemisacrum
definition: A hemisacral defect involving the sacral vertebrae S2 to S5. In hemisacrum, the first sacral vertebra is intact and there is agenesis involving only S2-S5.

name: Bifid sacrum
definition: Presence of a bifid sacral bone.

name: Teratoma
definition: The presence of a teratoma.
comments: Teratomas are germ-cell tumors commonly composed of multiple cell types derived from one or more of the three germ layers. They derive from embryonic pluripotent cells and may have various degrees of maturation, according to which they are classified as mature, immature, and malignant. Teratomas are found with decreasing frequency in the ovaries and testis, mediastinum, retroperitoneal space, sacrococcygeal zone, pineal and other intracranial locations.

name: Presacral teratoma
definition: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma located anterior to the sacrum and entirely inside the body (Altman type IV).
comments: Sacrococcygeal teratomas are thought to originate from multipotential cells in Henson's node, which migrates caudally to rest in the coccyx.

name: Branchial anomaly
definition: Congenital developmental defect arising from the primitive branchial apparatus.
comments: During embryonic development the major head and neck structures are formed from the five pharyngeal arches (bands of tissue). Incomplete, failed or persistent embryonic development of these arches results in several anomalies or defects in the neck.

name: Branchial fistula
definition: A congenital fistula in the neck resulting from incomplete closure of a branchial cleft.

name: Branchial cyst
definition: A branchial cyst is a remnant of embryonic development resulting from a failure of obliteration of a branchial cleft and consists of a subcutaneous cystic mass. Cysts are located anterior or posterior to the ear or in the submandibular region.
comments: Branchial cyst have to be distinguished from the preauricular cysts and sinuses, which are ectodermal remnants from an aberrant development of the auditory tubercles, tend to be bilateral, and are localized anterior to the tragus of the ear.

name: Cholesteatoma
definition: Cholesteatoma is a benign but potentially destructive growth consisting of keratinizing epithelium located in the middle ear and/or mastoid process. In cholesteatoma, a skin cyst grows into the middle ear and mastoid. The cyst is not cancerous but can erode tissue and cause destruction of the ear.

name: Euthyroid goiter
definition: A goiter that is not associated with functional thyroid abnormalities.

name: Supernumerary spleens
definition: The presence of two or more accessory spleens.

name: Maternal diabetes
definition: Maternal diabetes can either be a gestational, mostly type 2 diabetes, or a type 1 diabetes. Essential is the resulting maternal hyperglycemia as a non-specific teratogen, imposing the same risk of congenital malformations to pregnant women with both type 1 and type2 diabetes.

name: Aplasia of the phalanges of the hand
definition: Absence of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.

synonyms.text: Absent finger bone of the hand

name: Short phalanx of finger
definition: Short (hypoplastic) phalanx of finger, affecting one or more phalanges.

name: Tooth agenesis
definition: The absence of one or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop

synonyms.text: Failure of development of some teeth

comments: Teeth agenesis needs to be confirmed by X-rays. Teeth agenesis encompasses hypodontia, oligodontia, and anodontia. The total number and the type of teeth missing should be added to the description. The clinical absence of a tooth due to a disturbed eruption should not be termed teeth agenesis but a missing tooth.

name: Low-output congestive heart failure
definition: A form of heart failure characterized by reduced cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure owing to ischemic heart disease, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and other causes.

name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
definition: A form of diabetes insipidus caused by failure of the kidneys to respond to vasopressin (AVP).

name: Anomaly of the upper limb diaphyses
definition: A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the arm.

name: Amelia involving the upper limbs

name: Upper limb phocomelia
definition: Missing or malformed long bones of the upper limbs with the distal parts (the hands) connected to the variably shortened or even absent upper extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the whole limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).

name: Upper limb peromelia
definition: Peromelia affecting only the upper limbs. That is, the distal parts of the arm are missing leading to stump formation.

name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the extremities
definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the extremities.

name: Lower limb undergrowth
definition: Leg shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the lower extremity.

synonyms.text: Hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs

name: Aplasia involving bones of the lower limbs

synonyms.text: Absent bones of the lower limbs

name: Amelia involving the lower limbs
definition: Complete or near-complete absence of a leg.

name: Lower limb phocomelia
definition: Phocomelia affecting only the lower limbs.

name: Lower limb peromelia
definition: Peromelia affecting only the lower limbs. That is, the distal parts of the leg are missing leading to stump formation.

name: Forearm undergrowth
definition: Forearm shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the forearm.

name: Aplasia involving bones of the upper limbs

synonyms.text: Absent bones of the upper limbs

name: Upper limb undergrowth

synonyms.text: Hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs

name: Aplasia involving bones of the extremities
Limb undergrowth
definition: Limb shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.

synonyms.text: Hypoplasia involving bones of the extremities

name: Amelia
definition: Congenital absence (aplasia) of one or more limbs.

name: Peromelia
definition: The distal parts of the limbs are missing leading to a stump formation.

name: Phocomelia
definition: Missing or malformed long bones of the extremities with the distal parts (such as hands and/or feet) connected to the variably shortened or even absent extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the entire limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).

name: Peripheral neuropathy
definition: Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.
comments: Terms from this subhierarchy should be used to describe functional abnormalities seen in peripheral neuropathy. Morphological abnormalities should be coded separately.

name: Mononeuropathy
definition: A focal lesion of a single peripheral nerve. Damage to a sensory nerve is accompanied by sensory impairment of all modalities in the affected anatomic distribution.

definition: Short and wide proximal phalanges that taper distally . Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
