Symptoms induced by this disease are not specific: progressive dyspnea, non-productive cough, low-grade fever, arterial partial pressure of oxygen below 65 mmHg, and chest radiographs demonstrating bilateral, interstitial shadowing.
comments: Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) is caused by Pneumocystis jirovecii, a ubiquitous fungus. The taxonomy of the organism has been changed; Pneumocystis carinii now refers only to the Pneumocystis that infects rats, and P. jirovecii refers to the distinct species that infects humans. However, the abbreviation PCP is still the preferred acronym to designate the clinical syndrome of Pneumocystis pneumonia, although PJP is commonly used.

name: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
definition: Infection of the lungs with aspergillus. In the respiratory mucosa, the spores may germinate into hyphae, which in turn can invade the mucosa leading to invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.
comments: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis usually occurs in severely immunocompromised patients. Classic at-risk patients are those with prolonged neutropenia, either due to chemotherapy or immunosuppressive therapy, post hematopoietic stem cell transplant (SCT), or solid organ transplant.

name: Unusual protozoan infection
definition: An unusual protozoan infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a protozoal agent.

name: Severe Toxoplasma infection
definition: Toxoplasmosis is a widespread parasitic infection that is frequently asymptomatic in immunocompetent patients. However, this obligate intracellular protozoan parasite can evade the immune system and persist for the life of its host in cyst form, predominantly in the brain, retina, and muscles. Reactivation of latent cysts may occur when the immune system fails to maintain cytokine pressure, which mainly relies on gamma interferon (IFN-gamma). Toxoplasmosis is a life-threatening infection in immunocompromised patients (ICPs).

name: Severe giardiasis
definition: An unusually severe infection due to Giardia lamblia, also called Giardia duodenalis or Giardia intestinalis, which is a protozoan parasite of the small intestine that causes extensive morbidity worldwide.
comments: Several reports of giardiasis in immunocompromised patients exist.

name: Unusual helminthic infection
definition: An unusual helminthic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a worm (helminth).

name: Unusual parasitic infection
definition: An unusual parasitic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a parasite.

name: Glomerular basement membrane duplication
definition: Glomerular basement membrane duplication (GBM-DP) can be seen with Periodic acid-Schiff and silver stains. This appearance results from the presence of subendothelial deposits and the so-called mesangial interposition whereby mesangial cells, infiltrating mononuclear cells, or even portions of endothelial cells interpose themselves between the endothelium and basement membrane, with new, inner GBM-like material being laid down. This produces a double contour or tram-track appearance on light or electron microscopy. This finding often reflects splitting of the lamina densa and is associated with disease processes such as membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, transplant glomerulopathy, and diabetic nephropathy.

synonyms.text: Double contour of glomerular basement membrane

comments: Glomerular basement membrane duplication (GBM-DP) is often found in diabetic neprhopathy and is a pathological feature that suggests endothelial injury. See Figure 1 of PMID:30467801. Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) is a pattern of pathological injury characterized by thickening of or double contour formation on the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) (membrano-) with mesangial and/or endocapillary proliferation (proliferative). When injury persists, new basement membranes can form underneath the damaged endothelium, leading to the characteristic tram track appearance by silver staining.

name: Bone fracture
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the continuity of a bone.

name: Abnormal regulatory T cell proportion
definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

synonyms.text: Abnormal CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cell proportion
Abnormal CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cell count
Abnormal proportion of regulatory T cells

comments: Identification of Treg cells remains problematic, because accumulating evidence suggests that all the presently-used Treg markers (CD25, CTLA-4, GITR, LAG-3, CD127 and Foxp3) represent general T-cell activation markers, rather than being truly Treg-specific.

name: Increased regulatory T cell proportion
definition: Abnormal increase of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

synonyms.text: Elevated CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cell count
Elevated proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Increased proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Increased proportion of CD4+CD25+ Treg cells
Increased proportion of regulatory T cells

name: Decreased regulatory T cell proportion
definition: Abnormal decrease of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

synonyms.text: Decreased proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Decreased proportion of CD4+CD25+ Treg cells
Decreased proportion of regulatory T cells
Reduced proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells

name: Persistent human papillomavirus infection
definition: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are small oncogenic viruses. HPV has been shown to cause a variety of lesions and malignancies, which predominantly affect the anogenital region. Low-risk, non-oncogenic HPV types are associated with anogenital warts and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis while high-risk, oncogenic types are associated with cervical, penile, anal, vaginal, vulvar, and oropharyngeal cancers. Infection with anogenital HPV is usually asymptomatic and resolves spontaneously without consequences in the immunocompetent host. When disease does occur, the most common manifestation is genital warts, which may be small papules, or flat, smooth or pedunculated lesions. This resolution of HPV lesions is not generally seen in the immunosuppressed, resulting in severe, persistent and extensive manifestations of HPV disease.

name: Abnormal CD8+ T cell subset proportion
definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of any CD8+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD8+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

name: Subcutaneous abscess
definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris located in the subcutaneous tissue (subcutaneous fat layer), below the dermis.

name: Hypoplastic dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
definition: Underdeveloped hemidesmosomes at the dermoepidermal junction. Hemidesmosomes are the specialized junctional complexes, that contribute to the attachment of epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane in stratified and other complex epithelia, such as the skin.
comments: With this feature, the intracellular attachment plates may be thinner than usualler or separated into small, triangular segments. The thickness of the hemidesmosomes may be less than usual.

name: Radial artery aplasia
definition: Congenital absence of the radial artery.

name: Abnormal retinal nerve fiber layer morphology
definition: A structural abnormality of the retinal nerve fiber layer

synonyms.text: Abnormal retinal nerve fibre layer morphology

comments: The retinal nerve fiber layer consists of unmyelinated ganglion cell axons coursing on the vitreal surface of the retina to the optic disc. These axons become myelinated after entering the optic nerve.

name: Retinal nerve fiber edema
definition: Swelling (edema) of the retinal nerve fibers.

name: Conception by assisted reproductive technology
definition: A history of conception by an assisted reproductive technology such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and cryopreservation.
comments: Assisted reproductive technology is used primarily for infertility treatments to achieve pregnancy.

name: Bite cells
definition: Red blood cells that appear to have parts of them bitten away.
comments: This feature can be observed with acute hemolytic anemia (AHA) related to glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency. In this disorder, AHA can be triggered by ingestion of fave beans, infections, and certain medications. The blood film can show poikilocytosis with bite cells.

name: Tympanosclerosis
definition: A stiffening of the tympanic membrane due to calcification, typically presents as white plaque-like lesions, involving discrete regions of the tympanic membrane and/or middle ear.
comments: Plaques related to tympanosclerosis do not form spherical lesions and are typically within the drum substance itself which is normally easily discerned when using the binocular view of a microscope rather than the monocular, two-dimensional view of a hand-held otoscope. Such plaques can alter compliance of the tympanic membrane and can lead to sclerotic fixation of the ossicles, both of which can result in a mild conductive hearing loss. Histologically, lesions vary slightly according to their stage of development showing differing amounts of increased fibroblasts, abnormal fibers, areas of hyalinization, and areas of calcification into an osseous-like matrix. Most patients require no treatment.

name: Echopraxia
comments: Involuntary imitation or repetition of another person's actions. {xref="PMID:22807284"}

name: Spontaneous conjunctival filtering bleb
definition: Avascular cystic elevations of the superior conjunctiva not related to ocular surgery or trauma.

name: Prostate mass
definition: A lump detected in the prostate. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.
comments: The word mass is often used interchangeably with tumor, which derives from the Latin word tumor that originally meant any form of swelling. A small mass may be asymptomatic. Larger masses may cause pain if they press on a nerve or organ, or may lead to other manifestations depending on their location. In general, the finding of a mass will lead to a workup to determine the nature of the mass.

name: Periarticular soft-tissue mass
definition: A lump detected in the region that surrounds a joint. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.
comments: The word mass is often used interchangeably with tumor, which derives from the Latin word tumor that originally meant any form of swelling. A small mass may be asymptomatic. Larger masses may cause pain if they press on a nerve or organ, or may lead to other manifestations depending on their location. In general, the finding of a mass will lead to a workup to determine the nature of the mass.

name: Aplasia of the olfactory tract
definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the olfactory tract, which causes anosmia, a complete loss of the sense of smell.

name: Abnormal urine protein level
definition: Any deviation of the concentration of one or more proteins in the urine.

name: Increased urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin
definition: An increased concentration of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin in the urine (there is no generally accepted threshold, but some studies choose a threshold of above 150 nanogram per milliliter).
comments: An increased urinary NGAL concentration may indicate tubular injury.

name: Abnormal tubular basement membrane morphology
definition: Abnormal structure of the basement membrane of the renal tubulus.

name: Thickening of the tubular basement membrane
definition: Increase in thickness of the basement membrane of the tubulus of the kidney.

name: Podocyte hypertrophy
definition: Increased visceral epithelial cell size, with or without cytoplasmic protein droplets.
comments: Podocytes, also called visceral glomerular epithelial cells, are terminally differentiated cells that line the outer surface of the glomerular basement membrane. Podocytes prevent protein leakage into the urinary space, and also provide important tensile strength to the glomerular capillaries, by opposing the hydrostatic pressure from within. In contrast to glomerular endothelial and mesangial cells, podocytes do not typically proliferate. Studies have shown that following podocyte loss, the inability of podocytes to proliferate contributes to the development of glomerulosclerosis. Consequently, in order to cover the denuded glomerular basement membrane, podocytes increase in size due to hypertrophy. Although this is initially compensatory, podocyte hypertrophy is likely maladaptive, and contributes to glomerulosclerosis.

name: Increased urine neutrophil count
definition: Abnormally increased count of neutrophils in urine.

name: Myofibromatosis
definition: A mesenchymal neoplasm characterized by solitary or multiple nodules involving the skin, striated muscles, bones and, sometimes, viscera. It usually appears as a subcutaneous nodule, but can also appear as an ulcer, pedunculated lesion, or similar to a hemangioma. Histology shows well-circumscribed tapered cell lobes, resembling smooth muscle cells. At its center, perivascular round cells (hemangiopericitoides) are usually observed, giving a biphasic appearance.

name: Anticardiolipin IgG antibody positivity
definition: The presence of circulating IgG autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

name: Anticardiolipin IgM antibody positivity
definition: The presence of circulating IgM autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

name: History of recent animal bite
definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an animal.
comments: The spectrum of injury is broad and infectious complications, generally due to unusual pathogens, are common.

name: History of recent insect bite
definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an insect.

name: History of recent tick bite
definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to a tick.

name: Blood pressure substantially higher in legs than arms
definition: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the legs being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the arms. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.

synonyms.text: Blood pressure substantially higher in lower than upper extremities
Blood pressure substantially lower in arms than legs
Blood pressure substantially lower in upper than lower extremities

comments: This feature may be seen, for instance, in Takayasu arteritis.

name: Blood pressure substantially higher in arms than legs
definition: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the arms being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the legs. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.

synonyms.text: Blood pressure substantially higher in upper than lower extremities

comments: This feature can be observed in aortic coarctation.

name: Tracheal duplication cyst
definition: A cyst in the trachea, whose wall is made up by tissue similar to the bronchial tree, including cartilage and smooth muscle, and is lined by secretory respiratory epithelium composed of cuboid or columnar ciliated epithelium.
comments: Tracheal duplication cyst is a rare congenital malformation presenting in childhood with stridor or dysphagia from a mass effect on the trachea or esophagus. The features of the tracheal duplication cyst are similar to those of bronchogenic duplication cyst and laryngeal duplication cyst, but with histopathological features of the trachea. The trachea is known to originate from the respiratory diverticulum, a ventral outpouching of foregut lumen. The postulated embryological basis of a tracheal duplication cyst may be similar to that of the anomalous bronchi and is a result of abnormal budding of the bronchial tree during the fourth to sixth weeks of embryogenesis.

name: Calcium phosphate crystalluria
definition: The presence of calcium phosphate crystals in the urine.
comments: Calcium phosphate crystals are pleiomorphic, often appearing as birefringent stars or needles, occurring in isolation or in clumps. Plates are granular and non-birefringent.

name: Calcium oxalate crystalluria
definition: The presence of calcium oxalate crystals in the urine.
comments: There are two types of calcium oxalate crystals, the dihydrate (or Wedellite) and the monohydrate (orWhewellite), which are frequently found together in the same sample. The former have mostly a typical bipyramidal shape, while the latter are more pleiomorphic, although the ovoid shape is the most frequent. Bipyramidal crystals are birefringent only when large or in aggregates, but even then birefringence is usually not intense. The monohydrates, however, are always strongly birefringent. Calcium oxalate may be found in normal subjects, often as a consequence of ingestion of foods like chocolate, beet-root, peanuts, rhubarb, spinach, etc., in stoneformers, in patients with hyperoxaluria, or after ethylene glycol poisoning.

name: Calcium carbonate crystalluria
definition: The presence of calcium carbonate crystals in the urine.
comments: Calcium carbonate crystals usually appear as clumped granules.

name: 2-Methylbutyryl glycinuria
definition: Increased concentration of 2-methylbutyryl glycine in the urine.
comments: This phenotype can be related to a defect in the degradation pathway of L- isoleucine leading to increased urinary excretion of 2-methylbutyryl glycine.

name: Increased circulating mead acid level
definition: An abnormally elevated concentration od mead acid in the blood circulation.
comments: Elevated serum Mead acid as a proportion of total fatty acids is an indirect marker of a deficiency of essential fatty acids.

name: Elevated circulating succinate
definition: An increase concentration of succinate in the blood circulation.

name: Elevated urinary uromodulin level
definition: The concentration of uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) is exclusively produced in the kidney and is the most abundant protein in normal urine. Levels of uromodulin in the urine and in the blood, where it is present in lower amounts, are valuable biomarkers for tubular mass and renal function.

name: Anti-dsDNA antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against double-stranded DNA.
comments: Anti-DNA antibodies can be observed in persons with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), being a formal classification criterion.

name: Distal joint hypermobility
definition: Lack of stability of a distal joint (e.g., finger).

name: Positive blood 1,3 beta glucan test
definition: Beta-1,3-glucan is a major constituent of all of the characterized fungal cell walls, making up between 30-80 percent of the mass of the wall. It is a biomarker of fungal infections such as invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

name: Nevus comedonicus
definition: A type of epidermal nevus characterized by closely arranged, dilated follicular openings with keratinous plugs resembling classical comedones.
comments: Nevus comedonicus has a predilection for the face and neck area. Nevus comedonicus presents with grouped, dilated, plugged follicular ostia in a honeycomb pattern. The plugged ostia contain lamellated keratinaceous material. Their appearance resembles black dots but the material cannot be easily removed mechanically in contrast to acne comedones. Nevus comedonicus lesions might present with various patterns of distribution: unilateral, bilateral, linear, interrupted, segmental, or blaschkoid.

name: Abnormal oocyte morphology
definition: An abnormal structure of the female germ cell (egg cell).

name: Abnormal zona pellucida morphology
definition: Abnormal structure of the oocyte extracellular matrix region known as the zona pellucida.
comments: During mammalian fertilization, sperm need to reach the cumulus-oocyte complex, get through the hyaluronic matrix of the cumulus and penetrate the zona pellucida (ZP) in order to fuse with the egg.

name: Thin zona pellucida
definition: Reduced thickness of the zona pellucida.

name: Increased circulating adrenic acid concentration
definition: An increased concentration of adrenic acid (also known as cis-7,10,13,16-Docosatetraenoic acid) in the blood circulation.

name: Reduced response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
definition: Failure of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test to induce an appropriate increased in luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels.

synonyms.text: Reduce response to GnRH stimulation test

name: GM1-ganglioside accumulation
definition: Cellular accumulation of GM1 gangliosides.
comments: At the neuropathological level, severe infantile GM1-gangliosidosis patients exhibit distended neurons that contain typical lamellar inclusions referred to as membranous cytoplasmic bodies which are also found in other lipidoses. Although neurons are the primary target for storage, astrocytes may also appear abnormally vacuolated. Neuronal pathology in late onset forms is delayed and tends to be more severe in deeper structures of the brain than in the cortex. Inclusions in the liver are of fibrillar nature and are different from the lamellar bodies in neurons. Abnormal accumulation of GM1-ganglioside and, to a much lesser extent, its asialo-derivative GA1, in the brain is the most prominent biochemical feature.

name: Branch retinal artery occlusion
definition: Blockage of a branch of the retinal artery. This can cause loss of a section of visual field.

name: Abnormal neoplastic cell morphology
definition: A morphological abnormality of of tumor or neoplastic cells, characterized by atypical size, shape, cytoplasmic or nuclear features, or other deviations from normal cellular architecture.

name: Cilioretinal arteriolar hypoperfusion
definition: Ischemia in the territory of the cilioretinal artery causing opacification of the inner retina and visual loss. This is most commonly seen in central retinal vein occlusion in the young.

name: Ophthalmic artery occlusion
definition: Acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery (branch of the internal carotid artery) that may lead to severe ischemia of the affected globe and associated ocular tissues. It can present with a similar picture to central retinal artery occlusion associated with choroidal ischemia.

name: Branch retinal vein occlusion
definition: Blockage of a branch of the retinal vein. It may present with sudden-onset of painless vision loss or visual field defect correlating to the area of perfusion of the obstructed vessels.

name: Central retinal vein occlusion
definition: Central retinal vein occlusion is an occlusion of the main retinal vein posterior to the lamina cribrosa of the optic nerve and is typically caused by thrombosis.
comments: Central retinal vein occlusion may be associated with glaucoma or ocular hypertension. If the central retinal vein has two tributaries at the optic disc, hemiretinal vein occlusion may occur. It can cause cilioretinal arteriolar hypoperfusion.

name: Hemiretinal vein occlusion
definition: A variant of central retinal vein occlusions that involves the superior or inferior half of the retina.

name: Tumor signet ring cell
definition: A signet ring has a flattened surface at the top of the ring with an engraved or raised symbol, historically used to stamp a seal into correspondence. Comparatively, these cells acquire a signet cell morphology due to accumulation of abundant mucin in cytoplasm, leading to nuclei dislocation to the periphery.
comments: A cancer is labelled a signet ring cell adenocarcinomas if greater than half of tumor cells show prominent intracytoplasmic mucin and an eccentrically placed crescent-shaped nucleus.

name: Abnormal drug response
definition: An anomalous response to a medication related to individual variation in metabolic or immune response to drugs varying from potentially from potentially life-threatening adverse drug reactions to alteration of therapeutic efficacy.

name: Increased blood drug concentration
definition: High plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

name: Decreased blood drug concentration
definition: Low plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

name: Adverse drug response
definition: An unpleasant or harmful reaction resulting from treatment with a drug.

name: Reduced drug efficacy
definition: Decreased response to a drug intervention in comparison to the expected response.

name: Refractory drug response
definition: Absent or significantly reduced efficacy of drug intervention characterized by lack of measurable benefit or deterioration of disease course.

name: Reduced circulating cholinesterase activity
definition: Activity or concentration of cholinesterase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
comments: Serum cholinesterase (butyrylcholinesterase (BChE)) is an enzyme that hydrolyzes acetylcholine. BChE is synthetized in the liver and has conventionally been used as a liver function test.

name: Cholesterol crystalluria
definition: The presence of cholesterol crystals in the urine.
comments: Cholesterol crystals are transparent plates with well-defined edges and corners, which polarize light inconstantly. They are not found in normal subjects, and characteristically occur in patients with lipiduria secondary to nephrotic syndrome.

name: Abnormal CD8+ TEMRA T cell proportion
definition: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory RA TEMRA T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.

synonyms.text: Abnormal CD8-positive TEMRA T cell proportion
Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells, terminally differentiated

name: Abnormal dendritic cell count
definition: A deviation from the normal count of dendritic cells in the peripheral blood circulation. Dendritic cells are of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).
comments: Dendritic cells (DC), the professional antigen-pre-senting cells that prime specific immune responses,comprise a very small percentage of circulating whiteblood cells.

name: Abnormal circulating haptoglobin concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation.
comments: Haptoglobin is primarily produced in the liver and is functionally important for binding free hemoglobin fromlysed red cells in vivo, preventing its toxic effects.

name: Elevated circulating haptoglobin concentration
definition: The concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Haptoglobin is an acute-phase reactant whose levels can become elevated in the presence of infection and inflammation.

name: Decreased circulating haptoglobin concentration
definition: The concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Abnormal circulating A-type atrial natriuretic peptide concentration
definition: A measurable change in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

synonyms.text: Abnormal A-type atrial natriuretic peptide level

name: Increased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide concentration
definition: A measurable elevation in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

synonyms.text: Increased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide level

name: Decreased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide concentration
definition: A measurable reduction in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

synonyms.text: Decreased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide level

name: Superior cerebellar dysplasia
definition: Abnormal morphological development of the superior part of the cerebellum.

name: Multilobulated spleen
definition: The fetal spleen is lobulated, and these lobules normally disappear before the birth. Lobulation of the spleen may persist into adult life and be typically seen along the medial part of the spleen. A persisting lobule results in a variation in shape of the spleen.
comments: Sometimes a splenic lobule may extend medially anterior to the upper pole of the left kidney and less often posterior to the upper pole of the left kidney. Although these lobules are not of any clinical importance, close relation of the splenic lobule to the upper pole of the left kidney may cause misinterpretations as a mass originating from the kidney by the radiologists.

name: Thick pachygyria
definition: Pachygyria with a very thick cerebral cortex measuring 10-20 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

synonyms.text: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm

name: Anterior predominant pachygyria with 5-10 mm cortical thickness
definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness between 5 and 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically over 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

name: Posterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

synonyms.text: Pachygyria with cortical thickness over 10 mm posterior predominant

name: Perisylvian predominant thick cortex pachygyria
definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and a perisylvian predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Perisylvian predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

synonyms.text: Pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm perisylvian predominant

name: Anterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and an anterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Anterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe over the frontal and temporal lobes.

synonyms.text: Pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm anterior predominant

name: Pachygyria with 5-10 mm cortical thickness
definition: Pachygyria with a mildly thickened cerebral cortex measuring 5-10 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

name: Prolonged reptilase time
definition: An abnormally increased duration of the reptilase time. Reptilase time is a functional plasma clotting assay, which is based on the enzymatic activity of batroxobin. By specifically cleaving fibrinogen A from fibrinogen, batroxobin leads to the formation of a stable fibrin clot. The time, starting from the addition of batroxobin to the plasma sample, until clot formation is the reptilase time and is given in seconds.
comments: Reptilase time may be increased with a deficiency of fibronogen. Unlike the thrombin time, this assay is not affected by the presence of heparin, hirudin, or direct thrombin inhibitors in a blood sample.

name: IgA heavy chain paraproteinemia
definition: An abnormal IgA heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: IgG heavy chain paraproteinemia
definition: An abnormal IgG heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: IgM heavy chain paraproteinemia
definition: An abnormal IgM heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: Increased circulating arachidonic acid concentration
definition: An increased circulation of arachidonic acid in the blood circulation.

name: Abnormal circulating 18-hydroxycorticosterone level
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: Decreased circulating 18-hydroxycortisone level
definition: A subnormal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: Increased circulating 18-hydroxycortisone level
definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: Abnormal sarcomere morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the sarcomere, which is unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z disks.

name: Abnormal Z disk morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the Z disk, which is the platelike region of a muscle sarcomere to which the plus ends of actin filaments are attached.
comments: Z-discs (Z-disk, Z-line, Z-band) delineate the lateral borders of sarcomeres and are the smallest functional units in striated muscle. The core of a Z-disc consists of actin filaments coming from adjacent sarcomeres which are crosslinked by alpha-actinin molecules. Z-discs, which are difficult to detect in conventional light microscopy, appear in the longitudinal view of electron microscopy as electron dense bands with varying sizes, ranging from 30 to 50 nm in fast muscle and 100 t0 140 nm in slow muscle and cardiac myocytes.

name: Z-band streaming
definition: Streaming or smearing of the Z band, which is then no longer confined to a narrow zone which bisects the I band. The Z disk may extend across the I band or the entire sarcomere in a zigzag manner. Focal thickening, smudging, and blurring of the Z band takes place concurrently. Myofibrillar disorganization is a frequent but not invariable accompanying change.

name: Tubulointerstitial bacterial infiltration
definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of bacteria identified on routine and/or special (Brown-Hopps) stains.
comments: Tubulointerstitial bacteria can be ascending or vascuolcentric/blood-born. This finding can be associated with neutrophil rich infiltrates.

name: Tubulointerstitial fungal infiltration
definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of yeast or hyphal-microrganisms identified on routine and/or special (PAS, silver) stains.
comments: Tubulointerstitial fungi be ascending or vascuolcentric/blood-born. This finding can be associated with necrotizing tubulointerstitial lesions.

name: Simple ear
definition: The pinna has fewer folds and grooves than usual.

name: Reflex seizure
definition: Seizures precipitated by exogenous stimuli.
comments: Included in 2001 ILAE Proposed Classification of Seizures. Seizures precipitated by fever, head injury, or alcohol withdrawal or anti-epileptic medication withdrawal are not provoked seizures.

name: Eating-induced seizure
definition: A seizure precipitated by aspects of anticipating food, eating itself, or the post-prandial period.

name: Hot water-induced seizure
definition: A seizure precipitated by pouring cupfuls of very hot water (40 to 50 degrees Celsius) in rapid succession over the head. Bathing in this manner is the most common trigger.

name: Praxis-induced seizure
definition: A seizure precipitated by complex, cognition-guided tasks often involving visuomotor coordination and decision-making.

name: Proprioceptive-induced seizure
definition: A seizure precipitated by movement or a change in posture.

name: Reading-induced seizure
definition: A seizure precipitated by reading.
comments: These are typically manifest by myoclonic movements of the jaw or throat, increasing in frequency and potentially culminating in a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure if reading continues.

name: Somatosensory-induced seizure
definition: A somatosensory reflex seizure is a seizure precipitated by somatic stimulation of a specific part of the body in the absence of startle or surprise.

name: Startle-induced seizure
definition: Startle-induced seizures are triggered by multiple and non-specific stimuli (auditory, somatosensory, and rarely visual) and are characterized by their sudden unexpected nature. Sudden noise rather than pure sound is the most effective acoustic stimulus.
comments: Seizures are stereotyped and typically unilateral or bilateral tonic in nature.

name: Thinking-induced seizure
definition: Seizures induced by thinking and decision-making.
comments: These have been reported occurring in response to higher nonverbal mental activity such as playing chess or card games, performing mathematical calculation, drawing complex figures, manipulating spatial information, and typing.

name: Visually-induced seizure
definition: Seizures evoked by visual stimuli. This includes clinical seizures induced by strobe lighting, television and other screens, flickering environmental lighting and self-induction by causing a strobe effect.

name: Focal aware motor seizure
definition: A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.

name: Focal aware atonic seizure
definition: A type of focal atonic seizure during which awareness is fully retained throughout.

name: Motor seizure
definition: A motor seizure is a type of seizure that is characterized at onset by involvement of the skeletal musculature. The motor event could consist of an increase (positive) or decrease (negative) in muscle contraction to produce a movement.
comments: This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized.

name: Focal atonic seizure
definition: A focal seizure characterized at onset by sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic activity, typically lasting more than 500 ms but less than 2 seconds. It may involve the head, trunk, jaw or limb musculature.

name: Clonic seizure
definition: A clonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.
comments: This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized. Thus it can be used for coding clonic seizures when the onset is not known.

name: Hypohomocysteinemia
definition: A decreased concentration of homocysteine in the blood.

name: Dermal sinus tract
definition: A dermal sinus tract is an abnormality present at birth over the dorsal midline where an abnormal epithelialized connection from the skin tracks inwards towards the spine, most commonly seen in the lumbosacral region.
comments: The dermal sinus tracks in from the skin and may end in the soft tissues, epidural space, or intradurally, where it is commonly associated with (generally benign) intradural inclusion tumors (including dermoid, epidermoid, or teratoma), thickened fatty filum, tethered cord, or diastematomyelia (split cord syndrome). Dermal sinus tracts are different from innocuous coccygeal dimples, which are located lower within the gluteal cleft and are not associated with cutaneous stigmata; completely 'classic' dimples do not require further workup or follow-up. See Figure 1 of PMID:31484633.

name: Mammary duct ectasia
definition: A non-proliferative inflammatory disorder of the large duct (milk duct) of the breast; as such, it affects nipple and areola complex. The condition is characterized by focal dilatation of the lactiferous duct system is due to endoluminal changes, as well as the loss of duct wall elastin, leading to abnormally dilated and tortuous lactiferous ducts with associated periductal inflammation and fibrosis. Mammary duct ectasia may present with nipple discharge or palpable mass.

name: Breast abscess
definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the breast.

name: Nipple tenderness
definition: Pain or discomfort produced by touching the nipple.

name: Floating gallbladder
definition: An abnormal configuration in which the gallbladder is pedunculated, hanging free of the liver, and attached only by the cystic mesentery,

name: Biospecimen phenotypic feature
definition: A phenotypic abnormality obvserved in a biospecimen such as a biopsy or an extirpated tumor or tissue.

name: Abnormal lymph-node biospecimen
definition: Any abnormal phenotypic feature observed in a biospecimen derived from a lymph node, generally obtained by lymph node biopsy (removal of lymph node tissue for microscopic examination).
comments: The lymph nodes are organized lymphoid organs that contain lymphocytes within a fine reticular stroma. The structures within a lymph node include the capsule, subcapsular sinus, cortex (B cell zone with follicles and germinal centers), paracortex (T cell zone), medullary sinuses, medullary cords and hilus.

name: Abnormal lymph-node tissue architecture
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of the tissue of a lymph node.
comments: Each tissue is composed of many different cell types that assemble into organized patterns. Tissue architecture is defined by the cellular and extracellular compartments that cooperate with each other through division of labor.

name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular finding
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality within cells located in a lymph node.

name: Abnormal Q wave
definition: An anomaly of the Q wave of the electrocardiogram.
comments: Physiologically, the Q wave is mainly observed in the lateral leads aVL, I, V5, and V6 and is not observed in leads V1 to V3. The Q wave points downward and has a width less than 0.03s (i.e., 1 small square) and a depth of less than 3 mm (3 small squares), and it does not exceed 1/4 of the R wave in the given lead. The development of pathological Q waves has long been correlated with worsened outcome in patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction

name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular antigen expression
definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) by cells located in a lymph node.

name: Altered lymph-node tissue architecture
definition: An alteration that affects multiple components of the architecture of a lymph node.

name: Effaced lymph-node architecture
definition: Effacement of architecture typically refers to a cellular infiltrate destroying the normal follicular architecture of a lymph node. This effacement may result in sheets of cells that do not form clear architecture (seen in many lymphomas) or may lead to replacement of the normal architecture by atypical architecture, for example effacement of normal lymph node architecture (including normal follicles and patent lymph node sinuses) by many abnormal follicles in follicular lymphoma.

name: Vaguely nodular lymph-node architecture
definition: In contrast to normal lymph node architecture or that of follicular lymphoma, where follicles are typically distinct and readily identifiable on H&E stained biopsy sections, the cells within an atypical lymph node may show what appear to groups of cells forming vague nodules but not forming clear follicles.
comments: This finding, if not an artifact of poor tissue processing, favors lymphoma but may be seen in reactive states.

name: Lymph-node capsular invasion by lymphocytes
definition: Migration of substantial numbers of lymphocytes into the capsule of a lymph node.
comments: Lymph node capsules are formed by fibrous tissue encapsulating the lymph node, and typically have few or no lymphocytes within the capsule itself.

name: Lymph-node extracapsular extension by lymph-node lymphocytes
definition: Migration of lymphocytes into the soft tissues surrounding the lymph node.
comments: Lymph node capsules are formed by fibrous tissue encapsulating the lymph node, and typically the lymphocytes within a lymph node do not extravasate outside of the capsule into soft tissues surrounding the lymph node.

name: Increased lymph-node epithelioid histiocyte count
definition: Number of epithelioid histiocytes (histiocytes are tissue-resident macrophages) located within a lymph node above the upper limit of normal.

name: Scattered lymph node individual epithelioid histiocytes
definition: Many individual (not clustered) epithelioid histiocytes throughout at least part of a lymph node.
comments: Histiocytes are tissue-resident macrophages with a moderate amount of cytoplasm that can occasionally show more abundant cytoplasm and appear similar to epithelial cells. These epithelioid histiocytes may be scattered and/or clustered together within lymph nodes under certain conditions, but are generally not prominent in benign non-reactive lymph nodes.

name: Clustered lymph node epithelioid histiocytes
definition: Formation of clusters (group of cells positioned near each other) of epithelioid histiocytes within a lymph node.
comments: Histiocytes are tissue-resident macrophages with a moderate amount of cytoplasm that can occasionally show more abundant cytoplasm and appear similar to epithelial cells. These epithelioid histiocytes may be scattered and/or clustered together within lymph nodes under certain conditions, but are generally not prominent in benign non-reactive lymph nodes.

name: Abnormal lymph-node follicle architecture
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of follicles of a lymph node.
comments: A lymph node follicle is a loosely arranged structure with an outer mantle of small T lymphocytes and a germinal center composed of B lymphocytes, follicular dendritic cells, and macrophages.

name: Floral-pattern lymph node follicles
definition: Atypical lymph node follicles that have mantle zone cells invaginating/infiltrating into the follicle centers, which is said to confer a flower-like appearance.

name: Colonization of follicles by lymphoma cells
definition: In contrast to follicular lymphoma, which typically is a lymphoma that forms follicles or potentially completely replaces normal follicles, some lymphomas (most commonly marginal zone lymphoma) can infiltrate normal follicles so both normal lymphocytes and the infiltrating lymphoma cells are present. This is called colonization of follicles by the lymphoma cells.

name: Crowded lymph-node follicles
definition: Reduction in the average distance between adjacent lymph node follicles.
comments: Follicles in lymph nodes are usually spaced apart, however in certain conditions such as florid reactive follicular hyperplasia and follicular lymphoma, the follicles can become very crowded, even back-to-back with few interfollicular cells in between.

name: Lymph-node follicular lysis
definition: An abnormal morphology of hyperplastic lymph node follicles characterized by distortion of the follicular architecture by tongues and clusters of dark blue mantle cells impinging on and invading the reactive germinal center (Mostly T cells and mantle-zone B cells).

name: Non-polarized lymph node germinal centers
definition: A loss of the typical polarization of the architecture of a lymph node germinal center.
comments: Germinal centers typically have one side containing mostly larger centroblasts and the other side containing mostly small centrocytes. The side with more centroblasts appears darker on an H&E stained section and is termed the dark zone and the other side appears lighter and is termed the light zone. This polarization of germinal center topology is often visualized on H&E stained sections of reactive lymph nodes but may not be as obvious if the germinal centers are small or if the specific section happens to contain mostly dark zone or mostly light zone. This polarization is typically lost in follicular lymphomas.

name: Irregularly shaped lymph node germinal centers
definition: A deviation from the typically fairly round or oval form of a lymph node germinal center.
comments: Germinal centers may become more elongated and/or take on irregular shapes such as somewhat snake-like/serpentine or other shapes.

name: Abnormal lymph-node marginal or mantle zone morphology
definition: An abnormality of the structure of the mantle or marginal zone of a lymph node.
comments: The normal marginal zone is the area circumferentially adjacent to the mantle zone and distal to the germinal center of a reactive (secondary) follicle.

name: Abnormal lymph node marginal zone morphology
comments: Marginal zones are not typically present in lymph nodes, and when they are, they are difficult to distinguish from mantle zones on H&E. Marginal zones are a rim/band of lymphocytes surrounding mantle zones in secondary follicles (those containing germinal centers), and are typically only visualized in specific locations such as Peyer patches of the small bowel, or spleen, and not normally seen in lymph nodes. Expansion of marginal zones should prompt evaluation for a possible marginal zone lymphoma.

name: Abnormal lymph node mantle zone morphology
Abnormal bursal fluid morphology
definition: An anomaly of the synovial-like fluid found within a bursa, which is a small, closed sac lined by synovial membrane that reduces friction between tissues such as tendons, muscles, ligaments, and bones.

name: Lymph node with expanded mantle zones
definition: Enlargement of the typical outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.

synonyms.text: Germinal centers with expanded mantle zones
Germinal centres with expanded mantle zones

comments: Secondary follicles (follicles with germinal centers) typically show mantle zones which are a rim or band of mostly B cells surrounding germinal centers that on H&E appears as densely packed small lymphocytes immediately surrounding germinal centers. The mantle zone is usually relatively thin (i.e. only a few rows of lymphocytes extending out from the germinal center), however may be significantly expanded, particularly in mantle cell lymphoma.

name: Lymph node with poorly defined germinal center borders
definition: Reduced demarcation of the border between germinal centers and mantle zones. This border is typically seen as a crisp line on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained lymph node sections.
comments: Although not necessarily a neoplastic feature, the border between germinal centers and mantle zones may become poorly demarcated in certain lymphomas.

name: Abnormal lymph-node germinal center morphology
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of germinal centers of a lymph node.
comments: The germinal center is a specialized microstructure that forms in secondary lymphoid tissues, producing long-lived antibody secreting plasma cells and memory B cells, which can provide protection against reinfection.

name: Elevated bursal fluid leukocyte count
definition: The count of leukocytes per unit volume in a bursa aspirate specimen is above the uppper limit of normal.
comments: This finding is characteristic of septic arthritis. To ascertain this finding, typically, a specimen of bursal fluid is removed from the inflammed joint with a needle and syringe (aspiration) and examined microscopically.

name: Mantle zone pattern
definition: This refers to an architectural pattern of infiltration where atypical lymphocytes surround germinal centers, often expanding the mantle zones but without effacing architecture.
comments: This pattern may be observed in mantle cell lymphoma.

name: Germinal centers with absent marginal zones
Decreased biparietal diameter
definition: Fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone, below the lower limit of normal, usually taken to be two standard deviations below the norm or above the 3rd percentile for the gestational age.

name: Increased biparietal diameter
definition: Fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone, above the upper limit of normal, usually taken to be two standard deviations above the norm or above the 97th percentile for the gestational age.

name: Poorly defined primary lymph-node follicles
definition: Lack of the typical easily recognized delineation of primary follicles within lymph nodes.
comments: Follicles generally are relatively distinct at low magnification on H&E stained slides, however may not be obvious on the H&E stained slide, requiring immunohistochemistry to confirm the presence of follicle formation.

name: Progressive transformation of germinal centers
definition: This is a condition sometimes seen in a subset of germinal centers of reactive lymph nodes where germinal centers become enlarged and infiltrated by benign mantle zone cells and some T cells.
comments: While PTGC is a relatively common finding, there is an association with nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, and morphologically may mimic follicular lymphoma (as well as immunohistochemically with regard to BCL2 staining if not carefully evaluated at high magnification), particularly the floral variant.

name: Absent germinal center tingible body macrophages
definition: Lack of observable tingible body macrophages (TBMs) in germinal centers (GCs) of secondary lymphoid follicles. TBMs represent unique, large phagocytic cells that reside and are a subset of mononuclear phagocytes.
comments: Germinal centers typically contain macrophages that are engulfing cells undergoing apoptosis from the antigen selection process. The macrophages have relatively abundant cytoplasm containing apoptotic debris and are termed tingible-body macrophages (tingible is a somewhat non-specific term simply meaning capable of being stained). Tingible-body macrophages may be rare or absent in abnormal germinal centers such as in follicular lymphoma. Tingible body macrophages owe their name to their ability to actively phagocytose apoptotic lymphoid cells, and the tingible bodies (TBs) observed in their cytoplasm are apoptotic bodies.

name: Lack of germinal center mitotic figures
definition: Absence of extreme paucity of mitotic figures in a lymph node germinal center.
comments: Germinal centers typically have many cells undergoing cell division and therefore mitotic figures are frequently seen within germinal centers. If multiple germinal centers are present, it is unusual not to see at least some mitotic figures. Absent/decreased mitotic figures is an abnormal finding typically seen in low grade follicular lymphomas.

name: Non-polarized mantle zones
definition: Lack of the typical polarization of the outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.
comments: Secondary follicles (follicles with germinal centers) typically show mantle zones which are a rim or band of mostly B cells surrounding germinal centers that on H&E appears as densely packed small lymphocytes immediately surrounding germinal centers. The mantle zones typically are thicker (are several rows of lymphocytes extending out from the germinal center) on one side and thinner (only one or very few rows of lymphocytes extending out from the germinal center) on the other side. This polarization is not always obvious but is often seen, and is often lost in some atypical conditions such as lymphomas involving or surrounding germinal centers.

name: Hyalinized lymph-node vessels
definition: Hyalinized means to become clear/translucent such as collagen becoming more pale staining (collagen is typically quite eosinophilic, meaning attracted to the pink/red dye eosin); however, with regard to vessels in the lymph node, hyalinization is often used to describe vessel walls that appear markedly thickened or surrounded by eosinophilic material such as collagen, not necessarily translucent appearing.

name: Lymph-node follicular sclerosis
definition: Collagen deposition, typically with decreased cellularity, within lymph-node follicles.

name: Compressed lymph-node sinuses
definition: Loss of the typical patency (openness) of lymph node sinuses.
comments: Lymph node sinuses are structures that carry fluid and some cells traveling to and from the lymph node parenchyma, and often contain some histiocytes. These are normally patent but may be compressed by proliferating or infiltrating cells such as lymphoma to the point where they are no longer visible on routine H&E stained sections.

name: Lymph-node proliferation centers
definition: Proliferation centers are a finding specific to chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma where regions (typically relatively small, comparable to the size of a lymph node follicle) appear more pale on H&E stained sections (though they may become enlarged to merge together). These areas contain increased numbers of enlarged lymphoma cells with nucleoli (prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts) and show a higher proliferation rate (readily visualized with a Ki-67 immunohistochemical stain) than surrounding lymphoma cells. They can be mistaken as vague follicle formation and are therefore sometimes referred to as pseudofollicles.

name: Cytologic atypia in mantle cells
definition: Lymphocytes in the mantle zones of lymph node secondary follicles show cellular atypia such as enlarged size, increased cytoplasm, atypical distribution of chromatin, or irregular nuclear contours.
comments: This finding may raise suspicion of a neoplasm of mantle zone cells such as mantle cell lymphoma. Other lymphomas with cytologic atypia such as marginal zone lymphoma may also replace normal mantle zone cells.

name: Increased lymph-node eosinophils
definition: Eosinophils count within a lymph node above normal limits.
comments: Lymph nodes typically contain very few if any eosinophils but the number of eosinophils may be high in certain reactive or neoplastic states.

name: Increased lymph-node plasma cells
definition: Number of plasma cells per lymph node above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Lymph nodes typically contain some plasma cells and the number of plasma cells may be increased, sometimes forming sheets of plasma cells, in certain reactive or neoplastic conditions.

name: High lymph node non-germinal center mitotic activity
definition: Increased numbers of mitotic figures outside of germinal centers.
comments: Within lymph nodes, germinal centers typically show a high rate of cell division and correspondingly high number of cells undergoing mitosis. Cells outside of germinal centers typically show low levels of cell division visualized as low numbers of mitotic figures. Increased numbers of mitotic figures outside of germinal centers may be seen in certain reactive or neoplastic states.

name: Lymph-node lymphocyte monocytoid morphology
definition: Lymphocytes that show morphologic features resembling monocytes, such as increased cytoplasm and slightly enlarged nuclei that are more irregular than most lymph node lymphocytes.
comments: This finding may be seen in reactive conditions such as monocytoid B-cell hyperplasia of certain infections or in neoplastic states such as certain marginal zone lymphomas.

name: Reduced lymph node lymphocyte morphological variability
definition: Decreased morphological variability of lymph node lymphocytes as compared to the typically somewhat heterogeneous morphology of populations of benign lymph node lymphocytes.
comments: Lymph nodes often contain primarily small lymphocytes but typically have some admixed larger lymphocytes and show a little morphological variability. Neoplastic states may show increased morphological variability or decreased morphological variability, the latter showing unusually monotonous morphology among the population of lymphocytes.

name: Increased large lymphocytes in lymph node
definition: An increased number of large lymphocytes within a lymph node compared to a normal non-reactive lymph node.
comments: Lymph nodes will often show primarily small lymphocytes with relatively few scattered large lymphocytes (often termed immunoblasts). Increased large cells may indicate a reactive condition such as mononucleosis or a neoplastic condition. It may also help differentiate two different neoplasms such as marginal zone lymphoma (which often has increased scattered large cells) and mantle cell lymphoma (which usually has decreased scattered large cells).

name: Hodgkin morphology cells
definition: Hodgkin cells are typically large and often show very large nucleoli and sometimes binucleation or multinucleation. Reed-Sternberg cells are a type of Hodgkin cell that is binucleated with very large nucleoli that stains slightly red on H&E stained sections (often said to mimic owl eyes). Other Hodgkin cell morphologies include cells that are dying with dark basophilic (blue) nuclei that appear somewhat smudged (mummified cells) and cells with a large space around or adjacent to the nuclei and retracted cytoplasm after tissue fixation (lacunar cells). Hodgkin cells are characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma, however several non-Hodgkin lymphomas and noN-neoplastic conditions are known to sometimes show a few similar morphology cells.

name: Irregular lymph-node lymphocyte nuclei
definition: Lymph node lymphocyte nuclei that are more irregular than the typical round to slightly oval shapes of the majority of lymph node lymphocytes.
comments: More irregularly shaped nuclei can be seen in normal germinal centers (i.e. centrocytes) and in many types of lymphomas.

name: Lymph-node Dutcher bodies
definition: Dutcher bodies are collections of immunoglobulin protein that overlie or invaginate into the nucleus of plasma cells. These nuclear pseudoinclusions can occasionally be seen in reactive states and may be increased in specific neoplastic conditions.

name: Finely dispersed lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes with less dense, evenly distributed chromatin than the normal densely packed, often clumped chromatin of mature lymphocytes.
comments: This finding is seen in very immature lymphocyte precursors (i.e. lymphoblasts in lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma) or blastoid cells such as in blastoid mantle cell lymphoma.

name: Abnormal lymph-node lymphocyte chromatin
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the chromatin (complex of DNA and protein which comprises chromosomes) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

name: Clumping of lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes show multiple small densely packed areas of chromatin that appear as relatively evenly spaced clumps of basophilic (blue) staining within the nuclei on Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained sections.
comments: This is a somewhat non-specific finding but one that is often more prominent in lymphocytes of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma.

name: Abnormal lymph-node lymphocyte cytoplasm morphology
definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the cytoplasm (material located within the cell membrane but excluding the nucleus) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

name: Decreased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
definition: The amount of cytoplasm in lymphocytes is even less than the relatively little cytoplasm found in the majority of lymphocytes within lymph nodes.
comments: This finding is typically seen in centrocytes, either within normal germinal centers or neoplastic centrocytes in follicles of follicular lymphoma.

name: Increased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
definition: Increased amount of cytoplasm compared to the majority of lymphocytes in a benign lymph node.
comments: This finding may be observed in reactive or neoplastic lymphocytes located in a lymph node.

name: Abnormal level of lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
definition: Detection of an abnormal level of CD19 on the cell(s) of interest in a lymph node with the use of anti-CD19 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
comments: Most B-lineage lymphomas and leukemias show CD19 expression. Neoplastic plasma cells (plasma cells are derived from B cells), however, often lose CD19 expression.

name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular B-cell marker expression
definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) that is normally expressed by B lymphocytes.
comments: This term is intended to be applied to findings of lymph-node biopsies in diseases such as lymphoma.

name: Abnormal level of lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
definition: Detection of abnormal levels of CD20 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD20 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
comments: CD20 is normally expressed fairly highly on B-lineage cells, except plasma cells (down-regulate CD20 expression to the point where only a small subset of cells show expression).

name: CD79a expression
definition: Detection of the presence of CD79a on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD79a antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
comments: Most B-lineage lymphomas and leukemias as well as plasma cell neoplasms (plasma cells are derived from B cells) show CD79a expression.

name: Increased lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
definition: Increased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.
comments: CD20 is normally expressed fairly highly on B-lineage cells, but occasionally may show increased levels of expression relative to normal resting B cells. Increased expression is best visualized using flow cytometry when a population of normal B cells is present for comparison.

name: Decreased lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
definition: Decreased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.
comments: CD20 is normally expressed fairly highly on B-lineage cells, but occasionally may show decreased levels of expression relative to normal resting B cells. Decreased expression is best visualized using flow cytometry when a population of normal B cells is present for comparison.

name: Decreased lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
definition: Decreased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.
comments: CD19 is normally expressed fairly highly on B-lineage cells, but occasionally may show decreased levels of expression relative to normal resting B cells. Decreased expression is best visualized using flow cytometry when a population of normal B cells is present for comparison.

name: Increased lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
definition: Increased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.
comments: CD19 is normally expressed fairly highly on B-lineage cells, but occasionally may show increased levels of expression relative to normal resting B cells. Increased expression is best visualized using flow cytometry when a population of normal B cells is present for comparison.

name: PAX5 expression
definition: Detection of the presence of PAX5 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-PAX5 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry).
comments: PAX5 is a transcription factor that helps control B-cell lineage differentiation and is expressed in the nucleus of immature and mature B cells (including most neoplastic forms), but not in plasma cells.

name: Germinal center B-lymphocyte BCL2 expression
definition: Positive staining for BCL2 apoptosis regulator protein in lymph-node germinal center B cells.
comments: The BCL2 family of proteins regulate apoptosis, and BCL2 itself displays anti-apoptotic functions. In normal germinal centers, where antigenic selection leads to apoptosis of B cells that recognize self proteins, BCL2 is not expressed. Most low grade follicular lymphomas show aberrant expression of the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2, presumably helping to prevent the germinal center derived neoplastic B cells from undergoing apoptosis. Expression of BCL2 by germinal center B cells is abnormal and typically seen in low grade follicular lymphomas and in at least a subset of B cells in many high grade follicular lymphomas as well. Careful inspection is required when interpreting the stain, however, as normal T cells and occasionally infiltrating mantle zone B cells may also be seen in germinal centers, and these should not be interpreted as BCL2 expression in germinal center B cells.

name: Abnormal occipitofrontal diameter
definition: Abnormal occipitofrontal diameter (OFD) refers to a fetal head width measurement, taken between the root of the nose to the most prominent part of the occiput on an ultrasound image that lies outside the expected range for a given gestational age. The expected range typically falls between the 3rd percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations below the mean) and the 97th percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations above the mean).

name: Decreased occipitofrontal diameter
definition: Occipitofrontal diameter, measured with fetal sonography, below the lower limit of normal.

name: Increased occipitofrontal diameter
definition: Occipitofrontal diameter, measured with fetal sonography, above the upper limit of normal.

name: Abnormal elbow morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

name: Abnormal elbow physiology
definition: A functional anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

name: Restrictive eating
definition: A behavioral pattern characterized by a deliberate and sustained limitation of food intake, often involving avoidance of certain foods, restriction of portion size, or prolonged fasting, resulting in reduced energy or nutrient consumption relative to physiological needs.
comments: Restrictive eating refers to the intentional restriction of eating, not merely a loss of appetite. This behavior is a characteristic feature of anorexia nervosa and some other eating disorders.

name: Abnormal fetal abdominal circumference
definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the fetal abdominal circumference, which is typically measured sonographically in a transverse view using the outer borders of the skin line at the plane where the fetal stomach, umbilical vein and portal sinus is visible. Abnormal fetal abdominal circumference is defined as less than the 10th or greater than the 90th percentile for gestational age.

name: Increased fetal abdominal circumference
definition: The distance around the abdomen of a fetus, generally as measured by prenatal sonography, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Abnormal fetal head circumference
definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the fetal head circumference, which is typically measured sonographically in the axial plane at the level of the thalami and cavum septic pellucidi, using the outer border of the bony calvarium. Abnormal fetal head circumference is defined as less than the thrid percentile or 2 standard deviations below the mean or greater than the 97the percentile or 2 standard deviations above the mean.

name: Decreased fetal head circumference
definition: Fetal head circumference less than the third percentile or 2 standard deviations below the mean.

name: Increased fetal head circumference
definition: Fetal head circumference above the 97th percentile or 2 standard deviations above the mean.

name: Increased anteroposterior lens thickness
definition: Increase in the anteroposterior (axial) dimension of the crystalline lens relative to the overall length of the globe.

name: Ankle instability
definition: Failure of ligamentous and muscular structures of the ankle to maintain normal joint alignment during movement, resulting in excessive motion that causes manifestations such as subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the ankle with movement, ankle 'giving way' or sensation of ankle dislocating.

name: Retinal phlebitis
definition: Inflammation of retinal venules as manifested by perivascular sheathing or cuffing, vascular leakage and/or occlusion.
comments: Retinal phelbitis is typically seen in sarcoidosis.

name: Ophthalmic artery hypoperfusion
definition: Chronic hypoperfusion due to large vessel disease e.g. carotid artery stenosis, Takayasu disease. Typically presents dilated veins, low retinal arterial pressure, peripheral microaneurysms, ocular hypotension and may lead to iris neovascularisation. Patients may have postural hypotension.

name: Focal hyperpigmented area associated with subretinal scar tissue
definition: Localized hyperpigmented areas, in the context of subretinal scar tissue, as seen after subretinal neovascularisation.
comments: This includes Fuchs spot seen in myopic retinopathy.

name: Discrete fundus hypopigmentation
definition: Well-demarcated areas of the fundus, with relative reduction in pigment, with respect to the rest of the fundus.
comments: Discrete fundus hypopigmentation is seen in vitiligo, lacunae of CHRPE and achromatic retinal patches.

name: Macular pseudohole
definition: A macular pseudohole is a partial-thickness gap in a normal-thickness fovea, located in the center of the macula.
comments: The diagnosis of macular pseudohole requires an examination by optical coherence tomography (OCT).

name: Lamellar macular hole
definition: A lamellar macular hole is a structural abnormality of the macula, characterized by a partial-thickness gap in a thinner fovea, located in the center of the macula.
comments: Lamellar macular hole (LMH) is a vitreoretinal disorder characterized by an irregular foveal contour, a break in the inner fovea, dehiscence of the inner foveal retina from the outer retina, and the absence of a full-thickness foveal defect with intact foveal photoreceptors. The diagnosis of LMH requires an examination by optical coherence tomography (OCT).

name: Middle cerebral artery berry aneurysm
definition: A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA). MCA berry aneurysms may occur at the MCA bifurcation, on the anterior communicant artery, the anterior cerebral artery, the internal carotid artery, or on the posterior communicant artery.

name: Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of an artery that originates from the abdominal aorta.
comments: The abdominal aorta extends from the T12 vertebra and terminates at the L4 vertebra. It gives off anterior, lateral, and posterior branches that supply the abdominal viscera and vertebrae at this level, eventually dividing into the common iliac arteries. Upaired branches (and their typical location) comprise the celiac artery (T12), the superior mesenteric artery (L1), the inferior mesenteric artery (L3), and the median sacral artery. Paired branches comprise the middle adrenal arteries, the renal arteries (L1-2), the gonadal arteries (between L2 and L3), the inferior phrenic arteries, and the lumbar arteries. The abdominal aorta bifurcates into right and left common iliac arteries at L4.

name: Posterior humeral circumflex artery occlusion
definition: Blockage of the posterior circumflex humeral artery (PCHA), which arises from the third part of the axillary artery and supplies the shoulder joint and a number of its associated muscles. The lesion can be ascertained angiographically, whereby dye is injected both with patient's humerus at the side of the body and again with shoulder held in abduction and external rotation. Test is positive if there is evidence of PCHA occlusion with arm in abduction and external rotation but artery is patent when arm is held at the side.
comments: The axillary artery can be compressed by the humeral head owing to abduction and external rotation of the shoulder joint caused by overhead motion, as typified by pitching.

name: Scapulothoracic incongruity
definition: A lack of smooth, physiological alignment or movement between the scapula (shoulder blade) and the posterior thoracic wall (the rib cage). The scapulothoracic joint is unique, as it lacks true synovial articulation and is dynamically controlled through surrounding muscular contractions. The scapula glides on the posterior thorax covered with muscle layers rather than a cartilaginous surface. This feature can be ascertained by radiography or CT scan of the scapula showing incongruity of the scapulothoracic space.
comments: Snapping scapula syndrome, washboard syndrome, or scapulothoracic crepitobursitis are clinical manifestations of scapulothoracic incongruity usually associated with painful crepitus and shoulder joint dysfunction when attempting overhead motion.

name: Latissimus dorsi rupture
definition: A tear of the latissimus dorsi (LD). Injury to the LD can occur at various locations, from the tendon to the muscle belly. The LD is a broad, flat muscle occupying most of the lower posterior thorax. The muscle's primary function is to move the upper extremity, but it is also considered an accessory muscle of respiration.

name: Distal clavicular osteolysis
definition: Degeneration and resorption of the distal part of the clavicle near the acromioclavicular (AC) joint. Distal clavicular osteolysis (DCO) is an atypical injury occurring most often in athletes and weight lifters, specifically those who perform repetitive overhead movements.
