synonyms.text: Reduced desire to interact with peers

name: Reduced sharing of interests
definition: An absence or abnormally low frequency of engaging with others to share personal interests or topics. Interest sharing includes offers of information about oneself as a form of social interaction.
comments: Interest sharing should be assessed in the context of cultural and developmental norms.

name: Reduced object sharing
definition: An absence or reduction in object sharing. Object sharing is an early emerging social skill in which a child will share objects such as toys, balls, or books with parents or peers during object play.
comments: This term should not be applied to children younger than one year of life.

name: Abnormal communicative facial expressions
definition: Abnormal expressions (movements or position of muscles of the face that convey the emotional state of an individual to observers during social interactions) comprising abnormalities of quantity, range, context-appropriateness, and quality.
comments: This term describes the way facial expressions are used for communicating to other people (social communication). This term does not comprise abnormal facial expressions related to motoric neurological deficits such as hypomimic facies observed in individuals with Parkinson syndrome.

name: Facial expressions that do not match the context
definition: Production of facial expressions that are misaligned with the social context.

name: Abnormal quality of facial expression
definition: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are exaggerated or muted.
comments: This feature does not include facial motor tics.

name: Abnormal gesture use
definition: Abnormality in the use of gestures defined as hand, shoulder, and head movements that convey a shared meaning within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.
comments: Gestures refer to movements of the arms, hand, shoulders, or head and do not include facial expressions.

name: Poor conversational reciprocity
definition: Reduced use of reciprocal (back and forth) conversation, as compared to what would be expected for language level.
comments: Poor conversational reciprocity may be characterized by deficits in the ability to make comments about discussion topics of others, failure to ask questions, and not building a conversation on comments of others. Affected persons may not know what to say next in a conversation, may not notice if others are bored with a given topic, may conduct a one-sided conversation (talking but not listening), or may veer off topic more than is socially acceptable.

name: Ectopic tooth eruption
definition: A condition in which the permanent teeth, because of deficiency of growth in the jaw or segment of jaw, assume a path of eruption that intercepts a primary tooth, causes its premature loss and produces a consequent malposition of the permanent tooth.

name: Corpus cavernosum hypoplasia
definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by undergrowth of the corpus cavernosum.

name: Elevated circulating thymine concentration
definition: Concentration of the nucleobase thymine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

name: Positive lactose hydrogen breath test
definition: Elevated hydrogen gas level in exhaled breath following oral administration of lactose. In individuals with lactose intolerance, undigested lactose in the colon will be metabolized by colonic bacteria, releasing hydrogen gas.
comments: The enzyme lactase phlorizin hydrolase, located at the intestinal brush border, is necessary for the hydrolysis of lactose, the main sugar in milk. Due to the genetically programmed decrease in intestinal lactase activity that occurs post-weaning (lactase non-persistence), a large proportion of the human population loses, in adult age, the possibility to digest and absorb lactose.

name: Triggered by exposure to medication
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by administration of a medication.

name: Triggered by allopurinol
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allopurinol.

name: Ameliorated by oral zinc supplementation
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by oral zinc supplementation.

name: Curved dental root
definition: A root of a tooth that is more rounded than normal.

name: Abnormal four chamber view of the fetal heart
definition: The four-chamber (4Ch) view of the fetal heart is the most widely used screening examination for the detection of structural cardiac abnormalities during routine fetal ultrasonography. In the healthy normal fetus, the apical 4Ch view demonstrates four well-developed chambers, a concordant atrioventricular (AV) connection, unobstructed AV valves (mitral and tricuspid valves), the foramen ovale flap opening into left atrium (LA), and an intact interventricular septum. Additionally, the pulmonary venous opening can be visualized at the LA wall. Any structural deviations from normal anatomy may lead to congenital heart disease that can be determined by the 4Ch view of the fetal heart's ultrasound imaging.

name: Spleen hamartoma
definition: A hamartomatous lesion (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) localized in the spleen.

name: Positive lupus band test
definition: Deposits of immunoglobulins and complement components along the dermoepidermal junction.

name: Bone marrow erythroid vacuolization
definition: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow.
comments: See Figure 1 of PMID:29716882.

name: Triggered by electromagnetic field
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to an electromagnetic field.

name: Exposure history
definition: Information about current and past exposure to metals, dust, fibers, fumes, chemicals, biologic hazards, radiation, noise, and/or vibration at work or home.

name: Asbestos exposure
definition: History of exposure to asbestos, a fibrous mineral with physical and chemical properties that make it resistant to heat and degradation.
comments: Mesothelioma is an occupational disease occurring as a result of asbestos exposure in the workplace.

name: Medication history
definition: Information about current or past medications taken by an individual.

name: Aminoglycoside exposure
definition: History of having taken aminoglycoside antibiotics.
comments: Aminoglycosides include gentamycin, tobramycin, amikacin, kanamycin, and streptomycin, and may be associated with ototoxicity.

name: Statin exposure
definition: History of having taken statins, also known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.
comments: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, or statins, are widely used for hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular disease.

name: Potassium-sparing diuretic exposure
definition: History of having taken a potassium-sparing diuretic exposure such as amiloride, eplerenone, spironolactone, and triamterene.

name: Carbamazepine exposure
definition: History of having taken carbamazepine.

name: Valproate exposure
definition: History of having taken valproate (valproic acid).

name: Hydralazine exposure
definition: History of having taken hydralazine.

name: Calcium channel blocker exposure
definition: History of having taken a calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, verapamil, or diltiazem.

name: Triggered by nickel
comments: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to nickel.

name: Triggered by poison ivy, poson oak, or sumac
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac. These three plants each contain urushiol. Contact with these plants is the most common causes of clinically diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis.

synonyms.text: Contact with poison ivy, poison oak, or sumac

name: History of exclusive breast feeding
definition: A past medical history of having been fed exclusively by breast feeding.

name: Nutrition history
definition: A part of the past medical history consisting of information about the typical food intake of an individual.

name: High dietary oxalate intake
definition: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing high levels of oxalate, such as green-leaf vegetables, tea, nuts, chocolate and rhubarb.

synonyms.text: Foods high in oxalate, high intake

comments: An increased load of dietary oxalate presented to the kidneys has been linked to different kidney-related conditions and injuries.

name: Recent honey ingestion
definition: A history of ingestion of honey in recent weeks.

name: Raw egg-white ingestion
definition: A history of eating raw egg whites.

name: Exacerbated by sodium channel blocking agent exposure
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of sodium channel blocking agents such as phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine, topiramate, and zonisamide.

synonyms.text: Sodium channel blocking drugs aggravate findings

name: Addictive nitrous oxide use
definition: Addiction to inhaled nitrous oxide gas (N2O) is a growing concern.

name: Recent blood transfusion
definition: A past medical history of a recent blood transfusion.

name: Ameliorated by colchicine
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of colchizine.

name: Ameliorated by vitamin D
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of vitamin D.

name: Exacerbated by phenytoin exposure
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of phenytoin.

name: Triggered by angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to anngiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, and lisinopril.

name: Prostaglandin E1 exposure
definition: History of having been treateed with prostaglandin E1.

name: 5-fluorouracil exposure
definition: History of having been treated with 5-fluorouracil.

name: 6-mercaptopurine exposure
definition: History of having been treateed with 6-mercaptopurine.

name: Isoniazid exposure
definition: History of having been treateed with isoniazid.

name: Absent cavum septum pellucidum
definition: The cavum septum pellucidum (CSP) is an important fetal midline forebrain landmark that is normally visible by prenatal sonography. This term refers to the lack of visibility of the CSP on prenatal sonography. The CSP normally can be visualized between 18 and 37 weeks of gestation. Lack of visualization of the CSP in this time period generally requires follow up and may indicate the presence of underlying malformations such as malformations of the corpus callosum. The lack of CSP before 18 weeks or after 37 weeks of gestation (or postnatally) is considered a normal finding.

name: Fetal abdominal cyst
definition: Fetal abdominal cysts are usually detected during the second trimester anomaly scan or discovered incidentally at later gestations. However, a definitive diagnosis is often not made until postnatal life. The most common etiologies of fetal abdominal cysts are: ovarian, gastrointestinal cystic duplication, liver and choledochal, meconium pseudocysts, mesenteric and adrenal. Following identification of a cyst, careful morphological assessment allows the prediction of their natural history and importantly, the likelihood of surgical intervention being required postnatally.
comments: Fetal ultrasound cannot always distinguish the origin of a cystic lesion in the abdominal region.

name: Fetal bowel dilatation
definition: Fetal bowel dilatation is characterized by fluid-filled intestinal loops which measure at least fifteen millimeters long or seven millimeters in diameter. Ultrasonographic image of dilated fetal bowel is a sign of intestinal mechanical or functional obstruction and its prevalence will depend on the underlying condition: bowel atresia or stenosis, malrotation with volvulus, meconium ileus, total colonic aganglionosis, and meconium plug syndrome. The etiology of fetal bowel dilatation is a difficult prenatal diagnosis since ultrasound has limited accuracy for bowel evaluation.

name: Left ventricular dilatation
definition: Enlargement of the chamber of the left heart ventricle.

name: Fetal trigonocephaly
definition: A fetal ultrasound finding defined by flattening of the occiput with pointing of the frontal bones and brachycephaly with an increased cephalic index. It is characterized by keel shaped deformity of forehead with midline ridge, bilateral fronto temporal constriction with compensatory biparietal expansion, supra orbital and lateral orbital retrusion and hypotelorism. This finding is said to resemble a strawberry.
comments: Fetal trigonocephaly can be seen in trisomy 18 (or other chromosomal abnormalities) and monogenic syndromes, particularly also in craniosynostosis syndromes and some skeletal dysplasias.

name: Abnormal fetal heart outflow tract
definition: A prenatal anomaly of the outflow tract. Fetal ultrasound may not always be able to easily and accurately describe the outflow anomaly, but can detect abnormal anatomy. Often, follow up with a fetal echo is recommended, but fetal ultrasound is limited.
comments: The left ventricular outflow tract is the anatomic structure through which the left ventricular stroke volume passes towards the aorta. The right ventricular outflow tract is the structure through which the right ventricular stroke volume passes to the pulmonary artery.

name: Recent past medical history
definition: History of events that precede the current presenting condition and are thought to be of potential relevance, having occurred in the hours, days, or weeks before the current condition.

name: History of recent viral illness
definition: Medical history of a viral illness in recent weeks.

name: History of recent dental procedure
definition: Medical history of a dental procedure in recent weeks.

name: Abnormal hepatic artery morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the hepatic artery or its branches.

name: Hepatic artery hyperplasia
definition: Abnormal increase in size of the hepatic arteries.

name: Lymph node necrosis
definition: Areas of necrotic tissue within a lymph node.

name: Multinucleated neuron
definition: Neurons that contain more than one nucleus.

name: History of recent contralateral injury
definition: A history of an injury that occurred several hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint and is located on the other side of the body relative to the current presenting complaint.

name: Alternating laterality
definition: Occurring on the left and right in succession. This term can refer to alternating sides of the body (e.g., Alternating hemiplegia) or alternative sides of the visual field (e.g., some migraine auras).

name: Cervical squamous cell papilloma
definition: A benign tumor arising from the epithelial surface of the cervix and usually caused by Human Papillomavirus infection.

name: Liver leiomyoma
definition: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm that arises in the liver.

name: Typified by high penetrance
definition: Description of conditions in which only an incomplete but relatively high proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for incomplete, but high penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 80 percent but less than 100 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: Typified by moderate penetrance
definition: Description of conditions in which only a moderate proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for moderate penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 20 percent but less than 80 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: Typified by low penetrance
definition: Description of conditions in which only a low proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for low penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least some but less than 20 percent of carriers would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: Decreased Succinyl-CoA 3-ketoacid CoA transferase activity
definition: Decreased activity of the enzyme succinyl-CoA 3-ketoacid CoA transferase.
comments: Succinyl-CoA: 3-ketoacid CoA transferase (SCOT; EC 2.8.3.5, gene symbol OXCT1) is a mitochondrial homodimer essential for ketone body utilization.

name: Reduced phytanic acid oxidase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Activity of the enzyme phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase (PhyH; EC 1.14.11.18) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts. PhyH plays a role in the catabolism of phytanic acid, a branched-chain fatty acid that is a normal constituent of the human diet.

name: Reduced bifunctional protein activity
definition: Diminished activity of hydroxysteroid 17-beta dehydrogenase 4 (HSD17B4), also known as D-bifunctional protein (DBP), a peroxisomal enzyme that catalyzes multiple steps of beta-oxidation of very long chain fatty acids.

name: Decreased circulating plasmalogen concentration
definition: Reduced plasmalogen concentration in the blood circulation.
comments: Plasmalogens are a class of membrane glycerophospholipids that contain a vinyl-ether linked alkyl chain at the sn-1 position of the glycerol backbone and, typically, a polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain at the sn-2 position.

name: Post-vaccination varicella zoster virus infection
definition: Infection with live, attenuated varicella-zoster virus following vaccination. This is an extremely rare event that may indicate immunocompromise.

synonyms.text: Varicella zoster virus infection after vaccination

name: Recent steroid exposure
definition: History of having been treated with corticosteroid medications in recent weeks.

name: Shark teeth
definition: Eruption of permanent teeth behind deciduous (baby) teeth before they have fallen out, resulting in a double row of teeth. This phenomen is typically observed between the ages of 5 to 7 years.

name: Pontine T2 hypointensity
definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the pons.

name: Anti-platelet antigen antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against antigens present on the surface of thrombocytes such as the glycoproteins GPIIb/IIIa, GPIb/IX, and GPIa/IIa.

name: Anti-voltage-gated potassium channel antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a voltage-gated potassium channel.

synonyms.text: Voltage gated potassium channel antibodies in blood

comments: Voltage-gated potassium channels represent a family of transmembrane channels responsible for returning the depolarized cell to a resting state after each nerve impulse.

name: Vegan diet
definition: A history of following a vegan diet characterized by avoidance of food sourced from animals including meat, fish, and dairy products.

name: History of previous pregnancy with hydrops fetalis
definition: One or more previous pregnancies in which the fetus developed hydrops fetalis.

synonyms.text: History of hydrops fetalis in newborn offspring

name: Ameliorated by potassium supplements
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting a potassium supplement.

name: Ameliorated by niacin
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting niacin (vitamin B3).

name: Aggravated by exposure to medication
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with a medication.

name: Bleeding ameliorated by vitamin K
definition: Applies to bleeding that is significantly reduced by treatment with vitamin K.

synonyms.text: Vitamin K treatment reduces bleeding significantly

name: Anti-retroviral therapy exposure
definition: History of having been treated with an antiretroviral agent.

name: Potassium-wasting diuretic exposure
definition: History of having been treated with a potassium-wasting diuretic such as thiazide (chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, metolazone) and loop (bumetanide, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, torsemide) diuretics.

name: Tricyclic antidepressant exposure
definition: History of having been treated with a tricyclic antidepressant medication.

name: Excessive dental attrition
definition: A higher than expected amount of attrition of teeth, as menifested by loss of tooth characteristics including rounding or sharpening of incisal edges, loss of cusps, and fracturing of teeth, to an extent that is deemed more than would be expected at a given age.

synonyms.text: Excessive wear and tear on teeth

name: Positionally dependent pain
definition: Pain improves or worsens with changes in body position.

name: Abnormal erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) outside of the normal range.

name: Reduced erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) below the lower limit of normal.

name: Elevated erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) above the upper limit of normal.

name: Spermatogonial maturation arrest
definition: A type of spermatogenesis maturation arrest in which the block of developmental occurs in the spermatogonial stage. Testicular histology shows seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells and spermatogonial cells but no further differentiated cells like spermatocytes or round spermatids.

name: Elevated circulating neuron-specific enolase concentration
definition: Concentration of neuron-specific enolase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.
comments: Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is an important tumor marker in the serum of patients with lung cancer. Elevated serum NSE levels are also associated with neuroblastoma, neuroendocrine neoplasms, renal cell carcinoma, multiple myeloma, brain trauma, Guillain-Barre syndrome, and other diseases.

name: Reduced leukocyte alpha-mannosidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of an alpha-mannosidase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

name: Increased circulating alpha-mannosidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

name: Reduced leukocyte cathepsin D activity
definition: Concentration or activity of cathepsin D as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal. The reduction in cathepsin D activity can also be measured in fibroblasts.

name: Reduced leukocyte N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

name: Pseudohyperkalemia
definition: Pseudohyperkalemia describes a falsely elevated potassium level upon measurement of the serum electrolyte concentration due to disruption of cells during the collection or processing of the sample.
comments: Pseudohyperkalemia is an elevation of potassium in the serum that results during collection, storage, or handling of a blood sample, and is not representative of the potassium level in vivo. Pseudohyperkalemia can result from increased tourniquet tension, increased pressure from a patient's fist being clenched, or mechanical lysis of hematocytes during pneumatic tube delivery of samples to the laboratory or the centrifugation process. This term is meant to refer to habitually artefactually high plasma potassium levels owing to a temperature-dependentred cell leak as seen in Cryohydrocytosis.

name: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in cultured fibroblasts. Fibroblasts are easy to grow in culture and are the main cell type involved in producing extracellular matrix. They are used as a convenient model system for measuring enzyme activity for enzymes that are not expressed in blood cells. Usually, the test is done in fibroblasts for convenience rather than for the investigation of a pathophysiology specific to fibroblasts.

name: Reduced heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

name: Reduced N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

synonyms.text: Reduced N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts

comments: N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.4) catalyzes the cleavage of the 6-sulfate groups of the N-acetyl-D-galactosamine 6-sulfate units of the macromolecule chondroitin sulfate and of the D-galactose 6-sulfate units of the macromolecule keratan sulfate.

name: Reduced acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.14) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase hydrolyzes heparan sulfate and keratan sulfate.

synonyms.text: Reduced acetylglucosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts

name: Reduced erythrocyte porphobilinogen deaminase activity
definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of porphobilinogen deaminase (EC 4.3.1.8) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

name: Reduced holocarboxylase synthetase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of holocarboxylase synthetase (EC 6.3.4.10) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

name: Abnormal circulating alpha mannosidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase outside of the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

name: Reduced tissue alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.49) is below the limits of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including cultured fibroblasts.

name: Reduced erythrocyte arginase activity
definition: Activity or concentration of arginase (EC 3.5.3.1) in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal. Arginase catalyzes the last step of the urea cycle.

name: Reduced mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.9) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.
comments: Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase is a short-chain-length-specific thiolase that is encoded by the ACAT1 gene.

name: Reduced tissue beta-mannosidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of beta-mannosidase (EC 3.2.1.25) below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidas enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts.

synonyms.text: Reduced beta-mannosidase activity in cultured fibroblasts

comments: Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catalyzes the final exoglycosidase step in the degradation pathway for N-linked oligosaccharide moieties of glycoproteins.

name: Reduced 3-methylcrotonyl CoA carboxylase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Activity of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (EC 6.4.1.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

name: Reduced branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Activity of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex (EC 1.2.4.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
comments: Branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex is an inner-mitochondrial enzyme complex that catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacids derived from isoleucine, leucine, and valine.

name: Reduced erythrocyte galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity
definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT; EC 2.7.7.12) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.
comments: Galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase is the second enzyme in the galactose metabolic pathway.

name: Abnormal erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity
definition: Activity of adenosine deaminase in red blood cells outside the limits of normal.

name: Reduced isovaleryl CoA dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Activity of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.99.10) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

name: Reduced glycerol kinase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Activity of glycerol kinase (EC 2.7.1.30) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

name: Increased circulating vitamin A concentration
definition: Concentration of vitamin A above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

name: Elevated circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
definition: Concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: Diminished breath sounds
definition: A reduction in the intensity of the breath sound as ascertained by auscultation of the lung.

name: Anti-AK5 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-adenylate kinase 5 (AK5).

name: Anti-AMPAR antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR).

name: Anti-Amphiphysin antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Amphiphysin.

name: Anti-ARHGAP26 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Rho GTPase-activating protein 26 (ARHGAP26).

name: Anti-CARP VIII antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Carbonic anhydrase-related protein VIII (CARPVIII).

name: Anti-CASPR2
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2).

name: Anti-CV2/CRMP5 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against CV2/CRMP5. Anti-CV2/CRMP5 autoantibody is the most commonly detected anti-neuronal autoantibody. Patients with typical paraneoplastic chorea show fully developed chorea in the course of weeks to months with acute inflammation in the striatum.

name: Anti-DPPX antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6 (DPPX).

name: Anti-FGFR3 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against FGFR3.

name: Anti-GABA(A)R antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid A receptor, i.e., GABA(A)R.

synonyms.text: Anti-gamma amino butyric acid type A receptors antibody

name: Anti-GABA(B)R antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid B receptor, i.e., GABA(B)R.

name: Anti-GAD65 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65).

name: Anti-Gephyrin antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Gephyrin.

name: Anti-GFAP antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP).

name: Anti-GlyR antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Glycine receptor (GlyR).

name: Anti-Homer-3 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Homer-3.

name: Anti-Hu antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Hu.

name: Anti-Iglon5 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against immunoglobulin-like cell adhesion molecule 5 (IgLON5).

name: Anti-ITPR1 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (ITPR1).

name: Anti-Kelch like protein 11 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against kelch-like protein 11 (KLHL11).

name: Anti-LGI1 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 (LGI1).

name: Anti-Ma antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma.

name: Anti-Ma2 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma2.

name: Anti-Ma1 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma1.

name: Anti-mGluR1 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1).

name: Anti-mGluR5 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5).

name: Anti-neurexin-3alpha antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neurexin-3alpha.

name: Anti-P/Q-type VGCC antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs).

name: Anti-MAP1B antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against microtubule-associated protein 1B (MAP1B).

name: Anti-PKCgamma antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against protein kinase Cgamma.

name: Anti-Ri antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ri, an antineuronal antibody.

name: Anti-Septin-5 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Septin-5.

name: Anti-SEZ6L2 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against seizure-related 6 homolog like 2 (SEZ6L2).

name: Anti-SOX1 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against SOX1. Anti-SOX1 antibodies, also known as antiglial nuclear antibody (AGNA), are specifically found in paraneoplastic neurological disorders. Since SOX1 is expressed in neuronal precursor cells in the developing central nervous system, it has been used as an early marker of neural stem cells.

synonyms.text: Anti-Sry-like high mobility group box (SOX) 1 antibody

name: Anti-Tr/DNER antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Tr/DNER. Anti-Tr antibodies are directed against cerebellar Purkinje cells (termed anti-Tr or PCA-Tr). Anti-Tr autoantibodies are frequently associated with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Anti-Tr antibodies are defined by a specific staining pattern in cerebellar tissue that is characterized by punctate immunoreactivity in both the dendritic tree and soma of Purkinje cells but not in their axons. This characteristic pattern is indicative of the presence of anti-Tr antibodies. The Delta/Notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor (DNER) was identified as the target antigen of anti-Tr.

synonyms.text: Anti-delta/notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor antibody

name: Anti-TRIM46 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the axon initial segment protein tripartite motif 46 (TRIM46).

name: Anti-TRIM9/TRIM67 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against TRIM9/TRIM67.

name: Anti-Yo antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Yo.

name: Anti-titin antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against titin.

name: Anti-Zic4 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Zic family member 4 (ZIC4).

name: Distal radioulnar joint space widening
definition: Increased space between the distal radius and distal ulna at sigmoid notch (radioulnar distance more than 6 mm at the sigmoid notch).

name: Anti-Sj/ITPR1 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Sj/inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor.

name: Anti-D2 R antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dopamine-2 receptor.

name: Anti-GluK2 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamate kainate receptor subunit 2 (GluK2).

name: Anti-Lrp4 antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against low-density lipoprotein receptor (Lrp4).

name: Anti-ryanodine receptor antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against ryanodine receptor.

name: Anti-Kv1.4 antibody
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.4.

name: Distal radioulnar joint translation
definition: Abnormal linear movement or displacement of the ulnar head relative to the radius at the wrist, indicating instability of the distal radioulnar joint, which is the distal articulation between the radius and ulna, acting as a major weight-bearing joint at the wrist and distributing forces across the forearm bones.
comments: CT scan shows subluxation of the distal ulna either volar, dorsal, or lateral such that it is no longer congruent in the sigmoid notch.

name: Selective mutism
definition: Voluntary failure to use spoken language (at whatever level attained) in selective social contexts over a period of time.

name: Limited repertoire of facial expression
definition: An abnormally limited range of facial expressions demonstrated by a lack of nuance of facial expression to match specific social situations or an inability to demonstrate a normal range of emotions with one's face.

name: Excessive interest in others
definition: A strong desire to interact and engage with others that is perceived to be inappropriate or excessive in the context of cultural norms.

name: obsolete Reduced response to another's attempt to get direct attention
Abnormal pitch
definition: Persistently abnormally high or low-pitched vocalization or speech than is considered the norm for the context of social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.
comments: Pitch refers to the frequency of sound waves (measured in Hertz).

name: Disjointed sentences
definition: Persistent abnormalities in the sentence structure in speech, phrases may not be logically connected to each other, gives the impression of rambling. This may be a characteristic feature of the individual or may be a change from the norm of the affected individual.
comments: Loose association is highly correlated with flight of ideas and for which it is the speech-based expression. Typically it is very difficult to follow the logic in the expressed speech. The affected individual's speech is characterized by expressions in speech that have weak (e.g. tangential/circumstantial) connections between ideas.

name: Neologism
definition: Consistent use of an invented word that is unique to an individual.

name: Overly formal/pedantic language
definition: Use of language that is overly formal, precise, detailed, or pedantic for the social context.
comments: This term may apply to a persistent and ongoing feature of the affected individual or to a change from baseline.

name: Midline hand movements
definition: Hand stereotypies within the medial plane of the body.

name: Abnormal Intonation
definition: Abnormal rise and fall of the voice in speech and vocalization for the context and cultural situation.

name: Abnormal speech rate
definition: Speech that is abnormally fast or slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.
comments: The term Abnormal speech rate can also be used for a comparison at the individual level, speech that is faster or slower compared to the baseline of the individual.

name: Abnormal speech rhythm
definition: Speech with persistent abnormal rhythm or pattern for the context and cultural situation. This may occur constantly throughout conversations with the person or may occur in periodic bursts lasting several minutes to hours.

name: Ambiguous facial expression
definition: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are perceived as odd or mechanical. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical facial expressions. These expressions may be difficult to interpret for someone who is not familiar with the individual making the expression.

name: Exaggerated facial expression
definition: A tendency to make facial expressions that are exaggerated and a failure to make subtle facial expressions in a social context when a subtle expression is more appropriate.

name: Muted facial expression
definition: A tendency to produce facial expressions with decreased intensity or expressivity which appear muted or flat.

name: Abnormal peer relationships
definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships or lacking close friends.

name: Stereotypic movements of face and head
definition: Abnormal movements of face and head.

name: Stereotypic upper-extremity movements
definition: Abnormal movements of the upper extremities.

name: Stereotypic whole-body movements
definition: Abnormal movements of the whole body.

name: Abnormal interest in others
definition: A deviation from typical perceived social engagement with other individuals given the social context. This may manifest as either an excessive interest (e.g., persistent preoccupation with another person, excessive attempts to engage) or an abnormal lack of interest (e.g., minimal or absent social curiosity) in others.

name: Reduced social insight
definition: A lack of awareness of social rules in multiple social settings, which are simple or intuitive to others in the same social setting.

name: Reduced awareness of convention
definition: Reduced awareness of expected conventions, which are normal and expected for particular social settings or interactions.

name: Abnormal HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is outside of the reference limit for age.

synonyms.text: Abnormal HLA-DR expression on T cells
Abnormal proportion of DR+ T cells

comments: HLA-DR expression on T cells is an activation marker; elevated proportions reflect in vivo T cell activation status even when measured ex vivo without prior stimulation. This feature can be measured by flow cytometry.

name: Abnormal relationship
definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships, lacking close friends, or having a relational network that is abnormal given one's cultural context.

name: Impaired social imitation
definition: Reduced use of imitation of tasks or movements of others in play or learning.
comments: The ability to imitate others is common in children during early cognitive development (4-5 years old) and can be abnormal in children with developmental delay.

name: Infrequent social initiations
definition: Social initiation refers to the ability to begin interactions with other people. This term refers to a reduction in the frequency with which an individual attempts to begin interactions. The term should only be used for individuals who are assessed to have sufficient intellectual and language skills to interact with others.

synonyms.text: Infrequent attempts to direct the attention of another person
Reduced attempt to get or direct the attention of another person

comments: Social interactions can be begun by eye contact, nodding with the head, saying hello, or otherwise capturing the attention of another person with the intention of starting an interaction. The failure of a person to initiate social interactions with others can be observed when the examiner assesses that the person has had the opportunity to initiate interactions but did not do so for an extended period. Additionally, the interaction must be spontaneous and not prompted by another individual. This can be observed in individuals with long-standing social deficits, such as those with autism, as well as in episodic disorders like severe depressive episodes.

name: Reduced responsiveness to social cues
definition: A tendency to display responces to social cues that are interpreted (e.g., by family members, peers, or caregivers) as diminished compared to what would be expected based on the developmental stage and cultural context of an individual.

synonyms.text: Lack of response to verbal cues

comments: This term describes a behavioral abnormality and does not apply if the lack of response is assessed to be due to hearing impairment or intellectual disability.

name: Social disinhibition
definition: A tendency to violate social norms because of a failure to resist temptations or urges in social settings.
comments: A tendency to social disinhibition can be acquired after traumatic brain injury and may be described as insensitivity to others. Manifestions of social disinhibition may include (1) insertion of poorly considered utterances including insensitive remarks,overly intimate information, sexual references, and swear words, (2) failure to adhereto the rules of discourse leading to poor turn-taking, excessive side tracks, off topics,and talking too much, and (3) speaking from an egocentric perspective, that is,lacking concern, selfishness, childishness, arguing, not getting along with others.

name: Diminished integration of verbal and non-verbal communicative behavior
definition: A communicative abnormality where one's nonverbal and verbal communication are poorly integrated. This may occur when verbal and nonverbal communication are intact alone but are abnormal when used together, or an abnormality in the use of typically integrated communication such as the use of beat gestures during speech.

name: obsolete Reduced immediate imitation of others
Increased HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is above the upper reference limit for age.

synonyms.text: Elevated proportion of DR+ T cells
Elevated proportion of HLA-DR expressing T cells

comments: Reflects increased in vivo T cell activation.

name: Decreased HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is below the upper reference limit for age.

synonyms.text: Reduced proportion of DR+ T cells
Reduced proportion of HLA-DR expressing T cells

comments: May reflect T cell hypoactivation or exhaustion.

name: Reduced cooperative imaginative play
definition: Failure of a child to engage with peers games that involve creating imaginary scenarios or narratives, for instance, in which children pretend to be characters or act out adventurous scenarios.

name: obsolete Reduced responsiveness to verbal cues
Lack of expressed empathy
definition: The observation that an affected person tends not to provide situationally appropriate responses to other people in times when these people are in emotional need. For instance, failure to provide comfort to a person who is sad or crying.
comments: Empathy can be defined as the ability to explain, predict and interpret behavior by attributing mental states such as desire, beliefs, intentions and emotions to oneself and to other people. Empathy cannot be directly observed.

name: Bradylalia
definition: Speech that is abnormally slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.
comments: Bradylalia can also be used for speech that is slower compared to the baseline of the individual.

name: Excessively loud speech
definition: Speech which is persistently abnormally and noticeably loud or high volume for the social and cultural context and is not due to a structural or muscular abnormality. Those around the person often consider them to be shouting.

name: Excessively quiet speech
definition: Speech which is persistently abnormally quiet, or of low in volume for the social and cultural context. This includes persistent and inappropriate whispering. It is not due to a medical or surgical condition that results in hoarseness, nor structural or muscular abnormality that results in low speech volume.

name: Abnormal speech volume
definition: Speech that is abnormally loud or quiet for the social and cultural context in which it is spoken. It is clinically noted by others, including family, friends, or clinical providers.

name: Reduced attention regulation
definition: An abnormality in one's ability to control their attention towards a specific subject or task can include difficulties in changing or maintaining attention.

name: Reduced impulse control
definition: Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse.

name: Sensory behavioral abnormality
definition: Abnormal sensory behavior, including avoiding or seeking sensory input or difficulty modulating sensory stimuli.

name: Idiosyncratic gesture
definition: When one uses gestures that are unique to them and have no apparent meaning to others.

name: Atypical sorting
definition: Atypical focus on arranging, balancing, or positioning objects; may be atypical in focus or intensity.

name: Excessive checking
definition: Checking behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

name: Excessive hand washing
definition: Hand washing behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

name: Resistance to trivial environmental changes
definition: Distress in response to minor changes in one's environmental expectations.
comments: Typical examples of resistance to trivial environmental changes include distress when receiving the wrong color cup or when furniture is moved.

name: obsolete Reduced nonverbal responsiveness to verbal cues
obsolete Reduced verbal responsiveness to verbal cues
Reduced co-speech gestures
definition: Reduced use of speech-integrated gestures such as the use of beat gestures.

name: Limited head nodding or shaking
definition: Absence or reduction in the use of head nodding to indicate agreement or head shaking to indicate disagreement.

name: Limited pointing
definition: Absence or reduction in the use of pointing to request or direct another's attention.

name: Sensory hypersensitivity
definition: A decreased tolerance to sensory stimuli that triggers emotional and/or physical distress.

name: Sensory hyposensitivity unexplained by sensory deficit
definition: Increased tolerance to sensory stimuli due to diminished sensory ability.

name: Auditory hypersensitivity
definition: Hyperresponsive to sound that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Tactile hypersensitivity
definition: A decreased tolerance to physical touch.

name: Auditory sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit of specific sounds or noises that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Gustatory sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit of a particular taste that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Olfactory sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit of specific scents, smells, or fragrances that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Tactile sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit of a specific texture that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Vestibular sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit of vestibular stimulation that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Visual sensory seeking
definition: Pursuit visual stimulation by looking at specific sights, images, and/or colors that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

name: Socially inappropriate questioning
definition: A tendency to ask questions that are overly personal or otherwise inappropriate in the social situation in which they are asked.

name: Spinning
definition: An excessive frequency of spinning one's body.

name: Delayed Echolalia
definition: Repetition of borrowed words or phrases outside of the context in which they were originally heard. E.g., scripting from TV shows or movies.

name: Immediate Echolalia
definition: Immediate repetition of another person's speech.

name: Excessive cleaning
definition: Excessive cleaning of surfaces, living space, or environment that is excessive for the situational context.

name: Facial expressions not directed to others
Reduced social smiling
definition: Reduced production of smiles during engagement with an interactive parent, caregiver, or peer.
comments: In typical development, smiling is one of the most commonly observed social behaviors during the first 6 months of life. Most babies begin to smile by the age of about 2 months.

name: Abnormal play
definition: An abnormality in a child's ability play.
comments: Does not apply to the presence of abnormal play. The presence of abnormal play should be specified under atypical repetitive behaviors.

name: Reduced imaginative play skills
definition: Reduced or lack of pretending in play (does not assign abstract properties to objects, use invisible objects, or use objects in nonliteral ways other than their intended purpose in play).

name: Nonfunctional or atypical use of objects in play
definition: Use of objects in atypical, unimaginitive ways other than for which they are intended (banging, throwing, shaking, sorting, lining up, spinning).

name: Infrequent social engagement with peers
definition: Lower than typical number of attempts to engage peers in conversation, play, or other interactions.
comments: Social engagement refers to the interaction of an individual with others in a contextually appropriate manner.

name: Avoidance of emotional intimacy
definition: An atypically high tendency to avoid interpersonal exchanges characterizing by sharing of personal feelings, expressions of understanding, affirmation, and demonstrations of caring.

name: Failure to offer information to initiate social interaction
definition: An atypically low tendency to offer information as a means to initiate or sustain social interactions or direct another's attention.
comments: This term refers specifically to offering information in order to initiate social interactions and should not be applied to a person who is reluctant to offer information when prompted.

name: Difficulty understanding nonliteral meaning of conversation
Difficulty recognizing another's emotions
definition: A difficulty in recognizing or interpreting the emotional states of other individuals.
comments: This may include problems identifying emotions from facial expressions, tone of voice, or contextual cues, and may extend to reduced empathic understanding when others describe their feelings. Frequently observed in individuals with autism spectrum disorder and other conditions affecting social cognition.

name: Abnormal social emotional interactions
definition: An atypically low production of emotion social communications including those produced by communicative behaviors such as facial expressions, body language, and verbal communication.

name: Objectification of others
definition: A tendency to interact with others as if they are objects with functional purpose rather than engaging in social/emotional interactions.

name: Abnormal response to social norms
definition: An atypical understanding or application of social rules and conventions that guide interpersonal behavior. This may include reduced awareness of social norms or rigid, context-insensitive adherence to them.

name: Indifference to social norms
definition: Failure to follow social norms (shared standards of acceptable behavior) even though one has awareness of these norms and the ability to follow them.
comments: Indifference to social norms is characterized by an indifference to the consequences of breaking social norms.

name: Aggression towards others
definition: Aggression that is directed towards other individuals, as opposed to oneself.

name: Aggression towards caregivers
definition: Aggression that is directed towards caregivers.

name: Aggression toward non-caregivers
definition: Aggression that is directed towards non-caregivers.

name: obsolete Deficit applying language skills across context
Abnormal rituals
definition: Insistence on rituals which are self-imposed on a person's environment including directing the behavior of those around them.

name: obsolete Reduced use of language for social purposes
Jumping
definition: An excessive frequency of jumping in place.

name: Delay in the acquisition of cooperative play skills
definition: Failure to acquire the ability to play cooperatively, a type of play in whichchildren work together towards a common goal and in which a child displays interest both in the play and in the the other child or children involved in playing. This ability is observed in neurotypical children from the age of 3 to 6 years.

name: Reduced social reciprocity
definition: Reduced responses to other people's emotions and/or a lack of modulation of behaviour according to social context.

name: obsolete Infrequent social engagement with peers
Olfactory hallucination
definition: Perception of smell without olfactory stimulus.

name: Gustatory hallucination
definition: Perception of taste without gustatory stimulus.

name: Abnormal interpretation of external stimuli
definition: Abnormal perception of reality is characterized by an abnormal or inaccurate experience of external stimuli.

name: Proprioceptive hallucination
definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of distorted or abnormal sensations related to one's body position or movement.

name: Disturbed perception with a stimulus
definition: A perceptual experience in which an individual's perception of sensory stimuli is altered or disrupted in some way, resulting in abnormal or distorted sensory perceptions despite the presence of actual external stimuli.

name: Illusions
definition: Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli.

name: Inattentiveness illusion
definition: Instances in which individuals fail to perceive or notice salient or significant stimuli in their visual field due to a lack of attention.

name: Illusions due to affect
definition: Perceptual distortions or misinterpretations of sensory information arise as a result of the individual's emotional or affective state.

name: Pareidolia
definition: Apophenia is a psychological phenomenon in which individuals perceive familiar patterns or meaningful images in random or ambiguous stimuli, such as clouds, shadows, or inanimate objects.

name: Autoscopy
definition: A phenomenon in which an individual perceives themselves from an external perspective, as if they are observing their own body or self from a location outside of their physical body.

name: Subjective eidetic images
definition: A mental phenomenon is when an individual can vividly visualize or recall visual information from memory with exceptional detail and accuracy. These images are experienced subjectively by the individual, meaning they are not physically present or visible to others.

name: Amplification of social interactions
definition: A increase in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.

name: Diminishment of emotional responsiveness
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm.
comments: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

name: Somatic hallucination
definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of sensory experiences related to the body or its internal organs, systems, or processes. It is a hallucinatory experience that primarily affects bodily sensations rather than external sensory perceptions.

name: Visceral hallucination
definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of internal bodily sensations or processes that do not actually exist.

name: Abnormal perceptual state
definition: Temporary alteration of the awareness of reality or self-perception.

name: Depersonalization
definition: A psychological experience or symptom characterized by a sense of detachment or estrangement from oneself or one's surroundings.

name: Derealization
definition: A subjective experience in which an individual feels a sense of detachment or estrangement from their surroundings, leading to a distorted perception of the external world. It is characterized by a feeling of unreality or unfamiliarity with one's environment, as if things are dreamlike, artificial, or lacking in significance.

name: Decreased facial expression mirroring
definition: Diminished mirroring or reflection of facial expressions in another person during social interactions.
comments: Automatic mirroring of affective gestures and expressions refers to the unconscious imitation of gestures and expressions of other people during conversation. This term refers to the assessment that the affected person does not imitate gestures and expressions as much as typically expected in age-matched children.

name: Diminishment of comfort with casual physical contact
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to accept casual physical contact with others as compared to that person's previous norm.
comments: For instance, an individual may choose to stand farther apart from others in conversations or decline physical contact when offered during social interactions.This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

name: Thought blocking
definition: The experience of sudden cessation of the thought/thinking process, the person often describes the mind going blank and there is frequently a period of silence that is accompanied by a perplexed state, not understanding what transpired. Some may describe the experience as an abrupt emptying of the mind or the belief that an external force removed their thoughts from their head.

name: Maladaptive fear-related cognitions
definition: Threat-based cognitive biases result in a skewed perception, experience, or processing of internal or external stimuli.

name: Hypervigilance
definition: A heightened alertness is characterized by a broad awareness and/or excessive scanning of environmental stimuli.

name: Phobia
definition: Extreme, irrational, and persistent fears of certain objects, situations, activities, or persons can impede functioning in day-to-day life.

name: Anticipatory anxiety
definition: A state characterized by future-oriented worry, accompanied by negative affect and autonomic arousal.

name: Flight of ideas
definition: Successive thoughts and speech are easily diverted by external stimuli or internal superficial associations. Unable to maintain a constant train of thought and lose themselves in side issues, losing the thread and are unable to recover it. Superficial connections appear to drive the subject matter.

name: Recurrent maladaptive behavior
definition: A repeating behavior that is either immediately unproductive or has negative long-term consequences. This includes harmful coping mechanisms such as addictive behavior and failure to control impulses and compulsions.

name: Cognitive distortion
definition: A cognitive distortion is a maladaptive, exaggerated, or irrational thought pattern.
comments: Cognitive distortions are often involved in the onset or perpetuation of psychopathological states, such as depression and anxiety.

name: Abnormal change in social behavior
definition: An alternation in the habits and emotional tendencies of an individual with a change in behavior that is typically noticed by family members or peers.
comments: Changes in behavior may be observed as a disease such as dementia progresses and may manifest in increased or decreased amounts of passivity, depressive affect, anxiety, self-centeredness, wandering, agitation, paranoia, and so on.

name: Abnormal demeanor
definition: An anomaly in demeanor, which refers to the outward behavior, manner, or conduct of a person. It encompasses how an individual presents themselves to others in terms of attitude, posture, and general comportment.
comments: Demeanor can be assessed by observation of an individual's posture, gestures, facial expressions, overall mannerisms, or other behavioral manifestations.

name: Abnormally increased volition
definition: An excessive increase in motivated and goal directed as well as non-goal directed behaviors that are usually accompanied by elevated energy and interest that allows individuals to get started, be energized to perform a sustained and directed action. The increase is often disruptive and typically results in unfavorable consequences.

name: Pressured speech
definition: Speech pattern that is excessive and intense that often imparts a sense of urgency, the individual appears to be driven to communicate with many words that are spoken very quickly and may run into each other. The person is frequently difficult to interrupt and appears to not respond to social cues for the conversational partner(s) to take their turn in speaking.
comments: Pressured speech manifests as an increase in the amount of spontaneous speech, which is generally continuous, rapid, loud, and difficult to interrupt. Pressured speech may sometimes be incoherent and continue even when no one is listening.

name: Leaden paralysis
definition: The sensation of having heavy arms and legs, or feeling a heaviness in the limbs.

name: Grandiosity
definition: Persistently exaggerated feelings and thoughts of an inflated sense of self-importance, superiority, uniqueness, or invulnerability. The affected individual may project arrogance with a dismissive behavioral pattern towards others the individual deems inferior.

name: Hopelessness
definition: Persistent and excessive feelings of despair with an overwhelming lack of hope. While hopelessness is primarily a personal experience, the sense of hopelessness becomes pervasive and affects most aspects of the personal experience in relation to the world. For example the person may communicate a sense of hopelessness for family and friends (who themselves do not experience hopelessness), as well as the world in general.

name: Pathological sadness
definition: A negative emotional state characterized by sadness, unhappiness, or sorrow that is excessive in intensity, duration, or resistance to self-regulation compared with culturally appropriate norms or the individual's usual emotional range. It may arise spontaneously or in response to significant life events, but when reactive, it is disproportionate to or persists beyond what is typically expected for the context. Pathological sadness can be associated with feelings of hopelessness, helplessness, anhedonia, and a pessimistic outlook, but these features are not invariably present. It may also be accompanied by increased tearfulness, low energy, cognitive difficulties such as impaired concentration, and somatic changes including disrupted sleep or appetite.
comments: Sadness, per se, is a basic emotion with negative valence and low arousal. Sadness has significant evolutionary implications from behavioral, cognitive, social and health perspectives. As sadness persists, physical and cognitive symptoms including fatigue, difficulty concentrating, disrupted sleep, and loss of interest or pleasure in activities may become present, when dominant, interfere with personal, social, or occupational functioning. This state is distinct from normative sadness or grief and should be differentiated from the syndromic presentation of Major Depressive Disorder.

name: Decreased need for sleep
definition: There has been a noticeable decrease in the need for sleep, where individuals feel refreshed even with minimal or no sleep.

name: Sleep-related breathing disorders
definition: Conditions of abnormal and difficult respiration during sleep, including chronic snoring and sleep apnea.

name: Recurrent distressing nightmares
definition: Repeated occurrence of nightmares that cause clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning, which are not attributable to the physiological effects of a substance (e.g. drug abuse or medication) and which cannot be adequately explained by coexisting mental and medical disorders.

name: Sleep-related eating behavior
definition: Eating during sleep with limited to no recall of involuntary eating while asleep.
comments: Sleep-related eating may be associated with sleep walking.

name: Microsleep
definition: Sudden onset of extreme drowsiness or falling asleep during the day for a short period of time.

name: Exploding head syndrome
definition: Sleep disorder in which one hears a loud noise or explosive crashing sound in one's head. The sound is not real or heard by anyone else. The episode typically happens suddenly, either when beginning to fall asleep or when waking up during the night.

name: REM sleep behavior disorder
definition: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD) is a chronic sleep condition characterized by dream enactment and loss of REM atonia.

synonyms.text: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
Rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder

comments: Normally during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, the body experiences temporary paralysis (REM atonia) of most of the body's muscles while the brain is active and dreaming.

name: Non-restorative sleep
definition: Sleep that is subjectively reported as unrefreshing even though the duration is adequate.

name: Sleep-wake transition abnormality
definition: A parasomnia that occurs with awareness and recollection during the transition between sleep and and awake states.

synonyms.text: Disturbance during transitions between sleep and wake states

comments: Sleep-wake transition abnormalities include rhythmic movement disorder, sleep starts, sleep talking, and nocturnal leg cramps.

name: Sexsomnia
definition: Unintentional sexual behavior during sleep, such as masturbation, initiation of sex, or making sexual noises, is known as sexsomnia. Sexsomnia predominantly occurs during NREM sleep.

name: Periodic limb movements of sleep
definition: Repetitive, stereotyped limb movements occurring during sleep, typically involving brief flexion of the toes, ankles, knees, or hips. These movements recur at regular intervals, often every 20-40 seconds, and may cause sleep fragmentation or daytime fatigue. PLMS commonly co-occurs with restless legs syndrome but may also occur independently.
comments: Periodic limb movements of sleep often occurs alongside Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS). Treatment for RLS may also help with PLMS.

name: Abnormal transition from sleep to wakefulness
definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from sleeping to wakefulness.

name: Abnormal transition from wakefulness to sleep
definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from wakefulness to sleep.

name: Abnormal sleep architecture
definition: Interruptions during the various stages of sleep.

name: REM parasomnia
definition: Parasomnia occurs during REM sleep.

name: Abnormal movement during sleep
definition: Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, also known as Sleep-Related Myoclonus Syndrome or Nocturnal Myoclonus Syndrome, refers to the periodic and stereotypic movements of the legs or upper limbs during sleep.

name: Short N1 sleep
definition: Decreased duration of phase N1 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
comments: N1 sleep may be delayed or disrupted by a number of sleep disorders, including insomnia, hypersomnia, and movement disorders such as restless legs syndrome.

name: Paradoxical insomnia
definition: Paradoxical insomnia is a condition in which individuals with a normal or near-normal sleep macrostructure tend to severely underestimate the quantity and quality of their sleep.

synonyms.text: Disturbance in perception related to sleep

name: Short N2 sleep
definition: Decreased duration of phase N2 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
comments: In the N2 sleep stage, muscles begin to relax, breathing and heart rate slow, and body temperature drops slightly. During this stage of the sleep cycle, your brain activity also slows down to help maintain sleep.

name: Short N3 sleep
definition: Decreased duration of phase N3 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
comments: On an electroencephalogram (EEG), N3 sleep is characterized by a distinct pattern of synchronized brain waves. These brain waves give N3 the moniker "slow-wave sleep.

name: Diminishment of social interactions
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.

synonyms.text: Reduced, declined or lessened social interactions

comments: This feature may be reported by family members or peers. This feature is distinct from (but may be accompanied by) loneliness, which can be defined as a perceived discrepancy between one's actual and desired social relationships.

name: Amplification of interpersonal communication
definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.

synonyms.text: Heightened, amplified social expression and social connectedness

name: Amplification of relationship seeking
definition: Increased frequency or duration in social outings and interactions as part of relationship-seeking or maintenance compared to the previous norms of an individual. May be considered to be overfamiliar and have a tendency to engage strangers in a presumptive manner.

name: Diminishment of interpersonal communication
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.

synonyms.text: A decline or reduced social expression and social connectedness

comments: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers if the affected person begins to share less information or emotions than previously.

name: Diminishment of relationship seeking
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek new interpersonal relationships or maintain existing relationships.
comments: The affected person may begin to avoid social outings or interactions.

name: Amplification of sexual behavior
definition: An abnormal increase of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a higher frequency of sexual activity compared to from a person's previous norm.
comments: Engaging in riskier sexual practices, experiencing a significant increase in frequency, having multiple sexual partners, or spending excessive time on sexual activities can become disproportionate to other aspects of a person's life.

name: Amplification of emotional expression
definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to express emotions compared to that person's previous norm.
comments: Examples of emotional behaviors include crying, laughing, and smiling.

name: Amplification of emotional responsiveness
definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or emotional empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm. May be considered to be overreactive or over-engaged with interpersonal situations that may take on a persistent preoccupation and would appear to be relatively unrelated to the person, and beyond the expression of normal empathy.
comments: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

name: Amplification of comfort with casual physical contact
definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to be comfortable with physical contact with others compared to that person's previous norm. Often considered to be intrusive and encroaching on personal space of others less known to the person, frequently causing discomfort and may result in argument or altercation.

synonyms.text: Increase in comfort with casual physical contact

name: Diminishment of sexual behavior
definition: A reduction of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a reduction in the frequency of sexual activity , and/or activity compared to the affected individual's previous state.

name: Diminishment of emotional expression
definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to express emotions that is typically noticed as a change in behavior by family members or peers.
comments: Reduced frequency or subdued emotional behaviors like crying, laughter, and smiling, making the individual appear apathetic or disinterested.

name: Problematic alcohol consumption
definition: Impaired ability to stop or control alcohol use despite adverse social, occupational, or health consequences.

name: Suicide behaviors
definition: Suicide attempts or preparations
