definition: A congenital anomaly that appears as an amputation at different levels of the leg, e.g. femur, foreleg, ankle or toe. The limb is missing the terminal (distal) segment(s), with preservation of all the segment(s) proximal to the missing segment.

name: Hemimelia of lower leg
definition: A developmental defect leading to a transverse deficiency with absence of the lower leg (eg tibia and fibula), ankle and foot.

name: Hemimelia of forearm
definition: A developmental defect leading to a transverse deficiency with absence of the forearm (eg ulna and radius), wrist and hand.

name: Sodium glucose transport inhibitor exposure
definition: History of having been treateed with a sodium glucose transport inhibitors such as dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, canagliflozin, sglt-i, SGLT2, bexagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin, jardiance, invokana, forxiga, brenzavvy, steglatro, inpefa.
comments: May be a risk factor for SGLT-2i induced diabetic ketoacidosis.

name: Breath-holding spell
definition: A benign paroxysmal nonepileptic disorder occurring in healthy children 6 to 48 months of age. The episodes start with a provocation such as emotional upset or minor injury, and might progress to breath holding, cyanosis, and syncope.

name: Flared proximal tibial metaphysis
definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the proximal tibia.

name: Delayed toe phalanx ossification
definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of any of the toe phalanges.

name: Sorbitol ingestion
definition: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing sorbitol.

name: Positive peritoneal fluid bacterial culture
definition: Growth of bacteria in a culture dervied from ascites fluid.

name: Ocular cystine crystal deposition
definition: Accumulation of cystine crsytals in the eye. Patients present with crystal accumulation affecting the cornea and conjunctiva, but crystals can also be deposited in the iris, ciliary body, choroid and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and lens capsule. Corneal crystal deposition starts in infancy in the anterior periphery of the cornea, and progresses centrally and posteriorly. The crystals, which have a fine, uniform needle-shaped structure, are diffusely distributed within the corneal tissues.

name: Exuberant granulation tissue
definition: A manifestation of abnormal wound healing in which there is formation of excessive granulation tissue, with the granulation tissue rising above the level of surrounding skin and creating a raised, reddish, moist, and bumpy surface.

name: Oral mucosal papule
definition: A small (less than 5 mm in diameter), elevated, circumscribed, solid, palpable mass located in thte mucosa of the oral cavity.

name: Excessive piloerection
definition: Abnormally increased degree of goose bump formation, that is, of involuntary formation of bumps on a person's skin at the base of body hairs.
comments: Excessive piloerection can be a feature of opioid withdrawal.

name: Scalp edema
definition: A palpable swelling in the scalp caused by an increase in interstitial fluid volume (excess fluid).

name: Serpiginous burrow
definition: A slightly raised and often reddish serpentine or curvilinear path in the skin.
comments: Serpiginous refers to the wavy path of the burrows that is said to resemble the tracks of a snake. These lesions are characteristic of scabies and some other infections.

name: Positive brain-tissue rabies nucleic acid test
definition: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in brain tissue by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

name: Positive respiratory tract Bordetella pertussis nucleic acid test
definition: Detection of Bordetella pertussis PCR nucleic acid in in nasopharyngeal secretions by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

name: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli in wound tissue
definition: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli by microscopic examination of wound tissue. Acid fastness is a physical property that gives a bacterium the ability to resist decolorization by acids during staining procedures.
comments: Bacteria displaying acid fastness include: Mycobacterium leprae, M. tuberculosis, M. smegmatis, M. Avium complex, M. kansasii, Nocardia brasiliensis, N. cyriacigeorgica, N. farcinica, and N. nova.

name: Positive tissue encapsulated budding yeast test
definition: Identification of encapsulated budding yeasts in smears of body fluids, secretions, exudates, or other specimens.
comments: In fixed-tissue specimens, encapsulated yeasts may also be identified and confirmed as cryptococci by positive mucicarmine or Masson-Fontana staining. This finding may suggest a diagnosis of cryptococcosis.

name: Positive tissue coccidioidomycosis culture
definition: Growth of coccidioidomycosis in a culture derived from skin or an organ.

name: Diminished tissue dihydropteridine reductase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of dihydropteridine reductase (EC 1.6.99.7) below the lower limit of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and erythrocytes.

name: Decreased circulating transcobalamin-1 concentration
definition: The concentration of transcobalamin-1 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

synonyms.text: Decreased circulating R vitamin B12 binder protein concentration

name: Decreased circulating cationic trypsinogen concentration
definition: The concentration of cationic trypsinogen in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

synonyms.text: Decreased serine protease 1 level in blood
Reduced serine protease 1 level in blood

comments: Cationic trypsinogen is one of the several isoforms of trypsinogen. Serum cationic trypsinogen when low, is known to be associated with reduced pancreatic exocrine function in a number of disorders, including Shwachman's syndrome and type 1 diabetes mellitus.

name: Diminished circulating hyaluronidase activity
definition: The activity or concentration of hyaluronidase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Diminished sulfotransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Rate of proteoglycan sulfation (sulfotransferase activity) is below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

name: Elevated tissue alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.50) above the upper limit of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts. It is also known as alpha-acetylglucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-glucosaminidase, and alpha-D-2-acetamido-2-deoxyglucosidase.

name: Abnormal tissue alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity
definition: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.50) outside of the limits of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts. It is also known as alpha-acetylglucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-glucosaminidase, and alpha-D-2-acetamido-2-deoxyglucosidase.

name: Elevated circulating trihydroxycholestanoic acid concentration
definition: The concentration of trihydroxycholestanoic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated circulating glyoxylic acid concentration
definition: The concentration of glyoxylic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated CSF sepiapterin concentration
definition: Concentration of sepiapterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

name: Intrahepatic inclusion bodies
definition: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of stainable substances within hepatocytes.

name: Muscle vacuoles
definition: Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. The vacuoles are often associated with cytoplasmic and occasionally intranuclear eosinophilic inclusions.

name: Nonrimmed muscle vacuoles
definition: Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. On histological staining with hematoxylin and eosin, non-rimmed vacuoles lack the prominent dark border (rim) seen in rimmed vacuoles.

name: Reduced hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity
definition: Activity or concentration of glycogen phosphorylase L in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

name: Bone marrow hemophagocytosis
definition: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages observed in the bone marrow.

name: Splenic granulomatosis
definition: Splenic inflammation involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.

name: Immediate detumescence of penis at time of symptom onset
definition: Loss of erection at the time point of pain or other symptom onset.

name: History of aortic valve replacement
definition: History of having received a surgical replacement of the aortic valve.

name: Coved type ST segment elevation
definition: An ST-segment elevation of at least 2 mm in at least one right precordial lead (V1 to V3), followed by an r'-wave and a concave or straight ST segment. The descending ST segment crosses the isoelectric line and is followed by a negative and symmetric T-wave.
comments: This finding is highly suggestive of Brugada syndrome.

name: Saddle-back type ST segment elevation
definition: An ST-segment elevation of at least 0.5 mm (generally at least 2 mm in V2) in at least one right precordial lead (V1 to V3), followed by a convex ST. The r'-wave may or may not overlap the J point, but it has a slow downward slope. The ST segment is followed by a positive T-wave in V2 and is of variable morphology in V1.
comments: ECG anomaly is only suggestive of Brugada syndrome.

name: Substantially elevated circulating ethanol concentration
definition: A blood concentration of ethanol that is consistent with alcohol intoxication, generally assumed to be 0.0800 g/dL or higher.

name: Tortuous appearance of the stomach
definition: Abnormal twisting or winding of the stomach.
comments: This feature can be seen with gastric volvulus and cam imply that it is difficult to reach the pylorus with gastric endoscopy.

name: Cochlear nerve aplasia
definition: A developmental defect causing an absence of the cochlear nerve resulting in sensorineural hearing loss.

name: Slit-like lateral ventricle
definition: Abnormally small lateral ventricle with a slit-like appearance.

name: Fetal methamphetamine exposure
definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy (including during the period of conception) of the mother of a fetus or child to methamphetamine.

name: Elevated circulating 4-hydroxybutyric acid concentration
definition: Concentration of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urinary 2,4-dihydroxybutyric acid level
definition: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxybutyric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Pupillary hypersensitivity to parasympathomimetic agents
definition: A higher than normal tendency of parasympathomimetic agents to induce miosis.
comments: Topical administration of methacholine 2.5% or pilocarpine 0.0625% has no observable effect on the normal pupil but causes miosis after approximately 20 minutes in almost all individuals with familial dysautonomia.

name: Lack of pupillary response to hydroxyamphetamine
definition: 4-hydroxyamphetamine is used in eye drops to dilate the pupil, e.g.., to induce mydriasis for fundus examinations. This term refers to a lack of response of the pupil to topical application of 4-hydroxyamphetamine.

name: Subcortical U fiber lesion
definition: Abnormal morphology of subcortical U fibers, typically as assessed by abnromal intensity on magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.
comments: Subcortical U-fibers are special types of short association fibers located in the superficial white matter (SWM). In contrast to the SWM, the U-fibers only connect the adjacent gyri. Since U-fibers have a rich blood supply from long perforating arteries and short perforating arteries that span the white matter (WM) and adjacent cortex, they are usually unaffected in chronic ischemic WM disease. Anatomically, U-fibers originate from pyramidal neurons of layer 6 of the cerebral cortex and provide local integration of different sites of the same gyrus or immediately adjacent gyri. Developmentally, U-fibers do not fork until the second half of gestation when gyration and sulcation of the cerebral cortex occur. As a result, U-fibers are not readily involved in diseases of myelin metabolism, such as adrenoleukodystrophy and metachromatic leukodystrophy. However, in demyelinating diseases with normal myelin and oligodendrocyte dominance, including multiple sclerosis and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, U-fibers are commonly involved Pathologic processes that involve the white matter typically appear hyperintense on T2/FLAIR images.

name: Intraspinal extradural lipoma
definition: A lipoma (a benign encapsulated mass with lobulated mature adipose tissue enclosed by fibrous tissue) located within the spine but outside of the dura mater.

name: Intranasal mass
definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to the nasal cavity. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

name: Liver rupture
definition: Subcapsular hepatic rupture is characterized by the development of a hematoma, often quite large, beneath the liver capsule. An interval of days or hours may elapse between the time of injury and the first appearance of symptoms. A history of injury may be entirely lacking, or may be so unremarkable that it is elicited only by diligent interrogation. The hematoma tends to increase in size.

name: Elevated urinary mandelic acid
definition: The amount of mandelic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urine malic acid level
definition: The amount of malic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urine 3-hydroxysebacic acid level
definition: The amount of 3-hydroxysebacic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urinary vanillactic acid level
definition: The amount of vanillactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urine 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid level
definition: The amount of 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urine hydroxyphenyllactic acid level
definition: The amount of hydroxyphenyllactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Hydroxyphenyllactic acid or 4-hydroxyphenyllactate (the L-form) is a tyrosine metabolite. The level of L-hydroxyphenyllactic acid is elevated in patients with a deficiency of the enzyme p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate oxidase (EC 1.14.2.2).

name: Positive gastric CMV intranuclear inclusions
definition: Demonstration of the presence of cytomegalovirus in the stomach by means of a method such as in-situ hybridization.

name: Elevated urine dihydroxycholestanoic acid level
definition: The amount of dihydroxycholestanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urinary bile alcohol level
definition: The amount of bile alcohol in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated urine glucose tetrasaccharide level
definition: The amount of glucose tetrasaccharide in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Increased urine 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate level
definition: The amount of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Inability to protrude lips
definition: Lack of ability to purse or pucker the lips.
comments: The anomaly can be related to abnormalities of the muscles, nerves, or structure of the face.

name: Wet voice
definition: Wet voice is a perceptual vocal quality that is gurgly or liquid sounding and is due to the voice being produced through moisture. It is commonly used as an indicator of penetration and/or aspiration in clinical swallowing assessments and bedside screening tests.

name: Erythema marginatum
definition: An erythematous (pink-red, depending on the skin color of the affected individual) macule that spreads peripherally and coalesces to form polycyclic or serpentine patches or plaques. Lesions occur in crops over days to weeks and are evanescent. The rate of migration is 2 to 12 mm over a period of a few hours. Erythema marginatum tends to affect the trunk more than the extremities and to not be accompanied by pruritus.

name: Mechanic's hands
definition: Mechanic's hands are fissured, erythematous, hyperkeratotic eruptions on the hands, resembling the type of occupational dermatosis said to resemble the hands of a manual laborer. The lesions are classically on the lateral edges of the fingers and thumbs, largely sparing the palmar, and dorsal aspects of the digits.
comments: This feature can be observed in antisynthetase syndrome (ASyS), an autoimmune disease clinically manifested most often by interstitial lung disease, myositis, and arthritis.

name: Hiker's feet
definition: Hyperkeratotic scaly fissured plaques on the fingers/palms or soles, generally more evident on the lateral aspect of index fingers.
comments: Hiker's feet is a finding that is analogous to mechanic's hands with similar hyperkeratotic eruptions on the toes and feet, and is a manifestation of antisynthetase syndrome.

name: Anti-HLA-DQ antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against a human leukocyte antigen (HLA-DQ). DQ is one of several antigens involved in antibody-mediated rejection of organ transplants.

name: Inappropriate normal or low erythropoietin
definition: Erythropoietin is produced and released into the blood by the kidneys in response to hypoxemia, and would normally be expected to increase with decreasing hemoglobin levels. This term applies if the increase fails to occur, as may be seen in conditions including chronic kidney disease.

name: Rapid gastric emptying
definition: A condition in which food moves through the stomach into the small intestine at an abnormally fast rate.
comments: Dumping is the effect of alteration in the motor functions of the stomach, including disturbances in the gastric reservoir and transporting function. Anatomic and physiologic changes introduced by gastric surgery result in clinically significant dumping syndrome in approximately 10% of patients. Gastrointestinal hormones play an important role in dumping by mediating responses to surgical resection. Treatment options of dumping syndrome include diet, medications, and surgical revision.

name: Mediastinal lymph node calcification
definition: Abnormal deposition of calcium in mediastinal lymph nodes.
comments: Lymph node calcifications most often result from prior granulomatous infections, especially tuberculosis and histoplasmosis. Other, less common, causes are sarcoidosis, silicosis, amyloidosis, and calcifications secondary to the treatment of lymphomas (radiation therapy or chemotherapy).

name: Eggshell calcification of lymph nodes
definition: Eggshell calcification refers to fine calcification seen at the periphery of a mass and usually relates to lamellar lymph node calcification.
comments: Eggshell calcification, commonly occurs in patients with silicosis and coal-worker's pneumoconiosis. Sarcoidosis, postirradiation Hodgkin disease, blastomycosis, and scleroderma are other reported causes. Eggshell calcification has more rarely been observed in amyloidosis and histoplasmosis.

name: Knee joint effusion
definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid within the knee joint or around the knee. Symptoms maye include, pain, swelling, and stiffness.
comments: Increased intra-articular amount of (synovial) fluid is not specific for a particular disorder, as can occur in a variety of settings but draws attention to the presence of a joint disorder, such as knee osteoarthritis, or rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Subcutaneous emphysema
definition: Skin emphysema/Subcutaneous emphysema occurs when gas or air accumulates and seeps under the skin, where normally no gas should be present. While the presence of air in subcutaneous or mediastinal tissue is not dangerous in itself, prompt recognition of the underlying cause is essential.
comments: Subcutaneous emphysema can be caused by medical procedures and medical conditions that cause the pressure in the alveoli of the lung to be higher than that in the tissues outside of them. Its most common causes are pneumothorax or a chest tube that has become occluded by a blood clot or fibrinous material. It can also occur spontaneously due to rupture of the alveoli, with dramatic presentation. When the condition is caused by surgery it is called surgical emphysema. The term spontaneous subcutaneous emphysema is used when the cause is not clear.

name: Elevated bone scintigraphy uptake
definition: Bone scintigraph is performed with technetium 99m-labeled diphosphonates. The uptake of these radiopharmaceuticals depicts osteoblastic activity and regional blood flow to bone.
comments: Bone scintigraphy is frequently performed as part of the routine staging of patients with a wide variety of primary malignancies. Although it is a sensitive imaging modality, it is relatively nonspecific, and there are many potential causes of increased isotope uptake that can mimic metastatic disease.

name: Diminished long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase (EC 4.2.1.74) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

name: Diminished acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
definition: Concentration or activity of acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.16) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. This enzyme catalyzes the reaction acetyl-CoA + an acyl-CoA = a 3-oxoacyl-CoA + CoA. It is also known as 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase and beta-ketothiolase.

synonyms.text: Reduced 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity in cultured fibroblasts

name: Pathological inclusion body
definition: Pathological inclusion bodies are are composed of glycogen, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, hemosiderin, and calcium, that accumulate as metabolic by-products, catabolic products of macromolecular complexes, or in the context of cell injury.

name: Reduced epidermal collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining
definition: Diminished or absent collagen alpha5(IV) chain staining pattern in the epidermal basement membrane.

name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 3 chain staining
definition: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 3 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 4 chain staining
definition: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 4 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining
definition: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 5 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

name: Cystine nephrolithiasis
definition: A cystine stone is a type of kidney stone that is yellowish brown with a granular surface. They are observed in individuals with Cystinuria and tend to be of early onset, to occur repeatedly, and to be associated with urinary tract infections.

synonyms.text: Yellowish brown character to kidney stone suggestive of cystine

name: Hepatic cystine accumulation
definition: Accumulation of cystine in the liver.
comments: Cystine crystal accumulation activates Kupffer cells and secreted vasoactive substances cause vasoconstriction in microcirculation resulting in portal hypertension

name: Bone marrow cystine accumulation
definition: The presence of cystine crystals in bone marrow cells as demonstrated in a fresh bone marrow aspiration sample.

name: Desmoid tumor
definition: Desmoid tumors are rare, locally aggressive, fibroblastic soft-tissue tumors that are characterized by infiltrative growth and tendency to recur. Desmoid tumors do not metastasize but can arise in any part of the body: extra-abdominal (appear in the head and neck, chest, extremities), and abdominal wall or intra-abdominal (originating in tissue that connects abdominal organs).

name: Tubular jejunal duplication
definition: A segment of the jejunum that runs parallel to the normal jejunum and communicates with the jejunal lumen at one or both ends.

name: Left ventricular rupture
definition: A full thickness tear or breakage of the myocardium of the left ventricle.

name: Punctate pontine perivascular enhancement
definition: Multiple punctate (speckled, patchy spot-like) and/or curvilinear areas of gadolinium enhancement distributed around blood vessels in the pons.
comments: The lesions may extend into adjacent CNS structures, caudally to the medulla oblongata or the cervicothoracal spinal cord, rostrally to the midbrain, and even involve supratentorial regions such as the thalami, capsula interna, basal ganglia, corpus callosum and cerebral white matter. See Figure 1 of PMID:24028073.

name: Intestinal worm
definition: Presence of one or more adult worms in the intestine as demonstrated by sonography or passage of a worm in the stool. On sonography, worms may appear as linear, echogenic structures within the intestines.

name: Scrotal worm
definition: Demonstration of one or more worms in the scrotum. This finding can be appreciated by sonography, where echogenic, linear structures could be seen moving within the scrotum.

name: Small intestinal adenoma
definition: A small bowel tumor with adenomatous epithelium.
comments: Grossly and histologically, adenomas arising in the mucosa of the small intestine are similar to the adenomas found in the colon.

name: Maternal retinal mottling
definition: Mottling (spots or blotches with different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium in the mother of the index patient. Retinal mottling may indicate a mosaic X-linked inactivation state in the mother.

name: Twisted gallbladder pedicle
definition: A stretched conical-shaped structure found at the gallbladder neck with several linear echoes converging towards its tip. This finding is demonstrated by sonography and can indicate gallbladder volvulus.

synonyms.text: Conical structure at the gallbladder neck

name: Cholecyst-enteric fistula
definition: Fistula between the gallbladder and the intestine.

name: Dyschronometria
definition: Impaired ability to accurately measure or estimate time intervals.
comments: Common signs of dyschronometria are often generic to cerebellar ataxia, including a lack of spatial awareness, poor short term memory, and inability to keep track of time. For example, when asked to wait for thirty seconds, or tap every second that has gone by, those affected will be able to perform the task for a short time and then become derailed. This can result from a loss of focus, however, more often than not the individual affected can no longer tell what they are doing and they become disoriented. This often takes form in forgetting basic time keeping unless a timer is set, such as when cooking for example. Dyschronometria does not affect the 24-hour circadian rhythm, which is sustained by a different biological process.

name: History of recent intermittent breastfeeding
definition: History of recently intermittent breastfeeding an infant (i.e., on and off).
comments: Recent on and off breastfeeding can be a risk factor for galactocele and breast abscess.

name: Breast cyst
definition: A benign, fluid-filled sac in the breast.

name: Circumscribed
definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are well-defined and localized to a specific area.

name: Lobulated
definition: Applies to an abnormality that displays multiple indentations and/or elevations producing an irregular surface contour.

name: Spiculated
definition: Applies to an abnormality with irregular, radiating, or spiky edges.
comments: A spiculated mass is a centrally dense lesion seen on mammography with sharp lines radiating from its margin. The spicules can vary greatly in length, from a few millimeters to several centimeters. In malignant lesions, spicules represent a mixture of tumor cells and fibrosis invading the normal tissue surrounding the lesion.

name: Whorled
definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles series of a concentric circles or spirals.

name: Delta brush pattern on EEG
definition: Delta brushes are transient patterns characterised by a slow delta wave with superimposed fast activity.
comments: Delta brushes are the hallmark of the EEG of premature infants.

name: Tibiotalar synostosis
definition: Fusion of the junction between the distal tibia, fibula and the talus.

name: Vertebra plana
definition: he term given when a vertebral body has lost almost its entire height anteriorly and posteriorly, representing a very advanced compression fracture.

name: Intoeing
definition: An abnormal gait caused by a rotational variation anywhere in the lower extremity that causes the foot to point inward, instead of pointing straight ahead or outward, when walking or running.
comments: The three major causes of pediatric in-toeing are metatarsus adductus, internal tibial torsion, and femoral anteversion.

name: Palpable thrill on extremity
definition: A vibration felt upon palpation of a blood vessel over an extremity.
comments: This feature can be due to an arteriovenous malformation.

name: Out-toeing
definition: The feet turn excessively outward when walking, caused by a rotational variation in the leg.

name: Ankle dislocation
definition: An abnormal separation between the talo-tibial joint.

name: Anti-neuronal intermediate filament antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neuronal intermediate filament.

name: Anti-DREBRIN antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against dendritic spine scaffolding protein Drebrin.

name: Anti-lipoprotein lipase autoantibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-lipoprotein lipase.

name: Anti-apolipoprotein CII autoantibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against apoCII.

name: Eosinophilic neuronal inclusion bodies
definition: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neurons that stain with eosin, a red or pink dye.

name: Sweaty foot-like odor
definition: A characteristic smell said to resemble the odor of dirty socks.
comments: This feature is characteristic of isoveleric acidemia.

name: Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against acetylcholine receptor.
comments: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChR) are ligand-gated cation channels that are present throughout the nervous system. The muscle AChR mediates transmission at the neuromuscular junction; antibodies against the muscle AChR are the cause of myasthenia gravis. The ganglionic (alpha 3-type) neuronal AChR mediates fast synaptic transmission in sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric autonomic ganglia. Impaired cholinergic ganglionic synaptic transmission is one important cause of autonomic failure.

name: Hair shaft lesion
definition: Applies to an abnormality that is located on hair shafts.

name: Prolonged use of tightly fitting footwear
definition: History of use of tightly fitting shoes for a long period of time.
comments: This may be a risk factor for tinea pedis.

name: Triggered by high protein intake
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about ingestion of high quantities of protein.
comments: Metabolic triggers for late-onset urea cycle disorders include excessive protein intake.

name: Thickened tricuspid valve cusp
definition: An abnormally increased thickness of a leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

name: Displaced anterior fontanelle
definition: Abnormal shifting of the anterior fontanelle fropm its normal central position.
comments: This feature can be related to an abnormality of the cranial sutures, mostly craniosynostosis.

name: Subdural hygroma
definition: Accumulation of cerebral spinal fluid in the subdural space.

name: Incus ankylosis
definition: Incus ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the incus, which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).

name: Excessive diet restriction
definition: A tendency to reject a variety of foods and/or to eat a restricted range of foods.

name: Left ventricular apical dyskinesis
definition: Dyskinesis is used to describe ventricular muscle segments that bulge outside the left ventricular cavity during systole, as opposed to contracting inwards with the rest of the segments.

name: Longitudinal erythronychia
definition: A longitudinal red band extending from the proximal nail fold or lunula to the distal nail plate.

name: Exacerbated by exposure to sunlight
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by exposure to sunlight.

name: Exacerbated by heat
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by exposure to heat (high ambient temperatures).

name: Exacerbated by excessive sweating
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by excessive sweating.
comments: High temperatures, high humidity, excessive sweating can exacerbate cutaneous wounds.

name: Malignant pleural effusion
definition: The accumulation of a significant amount of exudate in the pleural space, accompanied by the presence of malignant cells or tumour tissue.

name: Inappropriately low urine osmolality following challenge
definition: In diabetes insipidus, affected individuals produce large quantities of dilute urine. In nephrogenic DI, the kidneys do not respond to vasopressin. In a water deprivation test or with administration of exogenous vasopressin, the osmolaltiy of the urine does not increase as normally.

name: Reduced urine tetrahydrocortisol plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone ratio
definition: Abnormally low ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE).
comments: In cortisone reductase deficiency-2, the ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE), which in CORTRD patients is typically less than 0.1 (reference range, 0.7 to 1.2).

name: Elevated urinary 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate level
definition: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Abnormal urine D-xylose test
definition: An abnormal result of the xylose absorption test that is used to assess the ability of the intestines to absorb D-xylose. D-xylose is a five-carbon monosaccharide found in some plants. The patient drinks a solution containing a specific amount of D-xylose and the concentration of xylose is measured in the blood circulation and then in the urine. A low amount of D-xylose indicates reduced small intestinal absorbtion.
comments: The standard 25-g D-xylose test in adults, based on analysis of a 5-h urine collection and a 1-h serum sample, discriminates between normal subjects and patients with proximal small intestinal malabsorption with X5% specificity and sensitivity.

name: Cerebral hemisphere mass lesion
definition: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in a hemisphere of the cerebrum. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

name: T2-hyperintense putaminal rim
definition: Increased signal on T2 magnetic resonance imaging characterized by a linear region of high signal surrounding the lateral aspect of the putamen at 1.5 Tesla.

name: Posterior fossa mass lesion
definition: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in the posterior fossa, affecting the cerebellum or fourth ventricle. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

name: Irregular RR interval
definition: Abnormal increased variability in the timing between consecutive R-waves on an electrocardiogram.
comments: Sinus arrhythmia is a variation of normal sinus rhythm that characteristically presents with an irregular rate in which the change in the R-R interval is greater than 0.12 seconds.

name: Irregular P-P interval
definition: Abnormally increased variability in the timing between consecutive P-waves on an electrocardiogram.

name: Fungal hair infection
definition: Demonstration of fungi growing on hair by a method such as microscopy of hairs mounted on slides with 10% potassium hydroxide.

name: Long hairstyle
definition: A past medical history of having long, full hair.

name: Conjunctival subepithelial fibrosis
definition: fine white linear scars under intact conjunctival epithelium. This scarring appears in areas of previous conjunctival ulceration or pseudomembrane formation, weeks to months after the insult is healed.
comments: Subepithelial fibrosis can be a manifestation of ocular graft-versus-host disease (oGVHD), but can also be found after epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and chemical burns.

name: Conjunctival fornix foreshortening
definition: Abnormal reduction in depth of the fornix of the conjunctiva. The fornix is the area where the conjunctiva folds back upon itself, thereby creating a recessed space.

name: Strong ultraviolet light exposure
definition: History of exposure to ultraviolet light, such as may be encountered with outdoor activities, living near equator, radiation.

name: Exposure to vaginal douching
definition: A history of intravaginal cleansing with a liquid solution for personal hygiene or aesthetic reasons.
comments: Douching represents a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis.

name: Exposure to oily lotions or creams
definition: A history of applying oily lotions or creams to the skin.
comments: This may be a risk factor for tinea versicolor.

name: Elevated circulating pristanic acid concentration following branched-chain fatty acid ingestion
definition: Concentration of pristanic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. This finding can be observed in Zellweger syndrome. Note that branched-chain fatty acid accumulation depends on dietary intake of phytanic acid, which is minimal in formula- and breast-fed infants. Thus, phytanic and pristanic acid levels are normal in a neonate with Zellweger spectrum disorder.

name: Decreased CD4+ T cell ZAP-70 protein expression
definition: Reduction in the level of ZAP-70 protein CD4-positive T cells.

synonyms.text: Decreased T-cell ZAP-70 protein expression in CD4-positive T cells

comments: Testing of CD4+ T cells reveals absence or near absence of ZAP-70 protein in most individuals affected by ZAP70-related combined immunodeficiency.

name: Dorsal flexion contracture of the ankle
definition: A type of contracture in which the dorsal flexion muscles of the ankle are contracted.
comments: Dorsiflexion of the ankle is the movement of the top of the foot towards the leg in an upward motion. With dorsal flexion contracture, the ability to passively or actively move the tip of the toe away from the leg is limited.

name: Metaphyseal undermodelling
definition: Lack of the normal diaphyseal constriction (thinning of long bones toward the midshaft area) giving the submetaphyseal areas an abnormally wide appearance.

name: Iliac vein compression
definition: Compression of the common iliac vein against the spine by the contralateral common iliac artery.
comments: Pulsations of the overriding artery cause shear stress and endothelial changes in the vein, resulting in the formation of fibrous bands or spurs. Over time, the affected area forms a stricture, causing impaired venous return and, in some circumstances, deep venous thrombosis. Common iliac vein compression can be ascertained by Doppler sonography.

name: Positive serum amyloid P scintigraphy
definition: Detection of abnormal amyloid deposits in the body by 123I-labeled serum amyloid P component (SAP) scintigraphy.

name: Crossed brainstem sign
definition: Motor and/or sensory cranial nerve findings ipsilateral to the lesion, and at the same time motor and/or sensory findings on the contralateral side of the body.

name: Inability to puff cheeks
definition: Reduced ability to inflate the cheeks by blowing air into them while keeping the lips closed.
comments: This feature may be related to facial muscle weakness as well as to cranial nerve VII lesions.

name: Entoptic phenomenon
definition: Visual sensations caused by changes within the eye itself, rather than by the normal light stimulation process. Entoptic phenomena are classified in the syndrome as floaters, blue field entoptic phenomenon, photopsia and self-light of the eye.

name: Abnormal vestibulo-spinal reflex
definition: An abnormality of the vestibulospinal (VS) reflexes, which contribute to the control of postural orientation. In this task, they continuously collaborate with reflexes elicited by stimulation of visual and somatosensory receptors. Labyrinthine receptors are sensitive to modifications (i) of the head position with respect to the earth vertical or (ii) of the angular/linear velocity of head motion in space. This information can be used to monitor deviations from the maintained body position.

name: Positive probe-to-bone test
definition: An abnormal result of the probe-to-bone (PTB) test. The PTB test is performed by inserting a sterile, metal surgical probe into the ulcer and is positive if a hard, gritty surface is felt inside. For large wounds, this may require gentle exploration of the wound with the probe.
comments: The basis behind the PTB test is that if a probe can reach bone, so can bacteria.

name: Exposure to repetitive hand impact
definition: A history of exposure to repetitive impact on palm or hand, such as working with a jackhammer.
comments: This history can be a risk factor for carpal tunnel syndrome.

name: Fractured scaphoid bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the scaphoid bone.

name: Local anesthetic ineffectiveness
definition: Resistance to the effects of local anaesthesia, with delayed onset or failure of local anesthetics to incude numbness or relieve pain.
comments: This feature has been reported in individuals with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

name: Palmoplantar location
definition: Applied to lesions whose distribution is confined or restricted to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet.

name: Oral mucosa plaque
definition: A raised, flat-topped lesion with a diameter of one centimeter or more that is located in the mucosa of the mouth.

name: Positive saliva rabies nucleic acid test
definition: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in saliva by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

name: Elevated tissue arylsulfatase A activity
definition: Activity of arylsulfatase A (EC 3.1.6.8) above the upper limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including culutured fibroblasts and leukocytes or in the blood circulation.

name: Elevated circulating methysterol concentration
definition: The concentration of a methysterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: This group of compounds includes thje 4-alpha-monomethyl sterols and 4,4-prime-dimethyl sterols.

name: Elevated urinary adipic acid
definition: The amount of adipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. Adipic acid is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,4-dicarboxy derivative of butane.

name: EEG with temporal slowing
definition: Slow-wave activity observed in the temporal area of the scalp electro-encephalogram (EEG).

synonyms.text: EEG with slow activity in temporal lobes
EEG with slow-wave activity involving the temporal lobes

name: History of high-pressure injection injury of the hand
definition: Medical history of the hand having come into contact with the nozzle of a high-pressure injecting system such as a paint gun or air compressor.

name: Hypertrophic ulnar styloid process
definition: Excessively long styloid process of the ulna.
comments: Ulnar styloid impaction syndrome involves impaction between the tip of the ulnar styloid process and the triquetrum bone. This syndrome is most commonly seen in patients with excessively long or hypertrophic ulnar styloid processes and is not necessarily associated with positive ulnar variance. The ulnar styloid process index (USPI), calculated as the difference between the ulnar styloid length and the ulnar variance divided by the transverse diameter of the ulnar head, is commonly used to assess the size of the ulnar styloid. An excessively long ulnar styloid has a length greater than 6 mm or a USPI more than 0.21. Repetitive friction of the proximal pole of the triquetrum and the ulnar styloid tip leads to chondromalacia, synovitis, and ulnar-sided wrist pain.

name: History of recent peripheral venous catheter
definition: A history of placement of a peripehral venous catheter in the hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint.

name: Purulent drainage from skin
definition: Exudation of a thick, opaque fluid from a wound or skin lesion, typically as a result of infection and draining pus, i.e., dead white blood cells, bacteria, and tissue debris.

name: Occupational history of putting fingers in other people's mouths
definition: A history of exposure of fingers by putting them in other peoples' mouths occupationally, e.g., as a dentist or physician.
comments: This is a risk factor for Herpetic whitlow.

name: Single-finger involvement
definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are limited to or predominantly affect a single finger.

name: Multiple-finger involvement
definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance affect more than one finger.

name: Pain disproportionate to abnormality on physical exam
definition: Exquisite tenderness in a specific region, beyond what one would surmise from examination.
comments: This finding may be observed with several diseases including necrotizing fasciitis and gas gangrene.

name: Sphenoid wing dysplasia
definition: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the greater or lesser wing of the sphenoid bone, typically resulting in widening of the superior orbital fissure, elevation of the [lesser sphenoid wing, and ipsilateral orbital enlargement.
comments: All reported cases of congenital sphenoid wing dysplasia have been attributed to neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Sphenoid bone dysplasia occurs in 3-11 percent of the subjects with neurofibromatosis type 1 NF1 patients. This malformation, a distinctive diagnostic feature for NF1, is characterized by progressive proptosis and facial disfiguration secondary to herniation of meningeal and cerebral structures. Unilateral in most of the cases, sphenoid bone dysplasia associated with plexiform neurofibroma in the territory of the trigeminal nerve in several cases and pooling of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in all cases often described in the past as an arachnoid cyst.

name: Skin laceration
definition: An injury in which skin and underlying tissues are cut or torn.

name: Metacarpal fracture
definition: A partial or complete breakage of a metacarpal bone.

name: Pain at the base of the thumb
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the base of the thumb, over thenar eminence or thumb metacarpal.
comments: The base of the thumb is the fleshy area on the palm side of the hand near where the thumb attaches to the hand.

name: History of recent participation in athletics
definition: Medical history of participation in sports (football, basketball, soccer, skiing) in the hours, days, or weeks prior to the current presenting complaint.

name: Remote trauma history
definition: History of trauma months to years ago, including but not limited to fracture or other orthopedic injury at the symptomatic area.
comments: This feature may suggest scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse, scapholunate advanced collapse, or distal radioulnar joint arthritis.

name: Distal radioulnar joint arthritis
definition: An inflammatory condition of the joint that connects the far ends of the radius and the ulna, known as the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ). DRUJ arthritis may be characterized by widening of the DRUJ interval, volar/dorsal displacement of the distal ulna, radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis at the DRUJ joint including osteophytes, subchondral cysts, subchrondal sclerosis, and joint space narrowing.

synonyms.text: Arthritis of the distal radioulnar joint

comments: Arthritis of the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) between the sigmoid notch of the distal radius and the ulnar head can be caused by traumatic, inflammatory, congenital, and degenerative processes.

name: Radial head fracture
definition: Fracture of the proximal end of the radius involving the radial head.

name: Elbow lateral collateral ligament tear
definition: An injury to the lateral collateral ligament (LCL) of the elbow. The LCL is a complex capsuloligamentous structure critical in stabilizing the ulnohumeral and radiocapitellar articulations. LCL injury can result in elbow instability, allowing the proximal radius and ulna to externally rotate away from the humerus as a supination stress is applied to the forearm.

synonyms.text: Ligamentous tear on the lateral aspect of the elbow

name: Elbow medial collateral ligament tear
definition: An injury to the medial collateral ligament (MCL) of the elbow.

synonyms.text: Ligamentous tear on the medial aspect of the elbow

comments: Elbow medial collateral ligament sprain occurs when the elbow is subjected to a valgus force exceeding the tensile properties of the medial collateral ligament (MCL). This is an injury seen more often in throwing athletes.

name: Coronoid fracture
definition: Fracture of the coronoid process on the proximal ulna.
comments: The coronoid process acts to buttress against the posterior translation of the ulna on the humerus. It is also the attachment site for the anterior elbow capsule, brachialis, and the medial collateral ligament of the elbow. Coronoid fractures are critical injuries and are suggestive of elbow instability.

name: History of spinal cord injury
definition: A medical history of hving had a spinal cord injury prior to the presenting complaint.
comments: Spinal cord injury (SCI) results from direct or indirect spinal cord damage. The most common SCI cause is acute trauma from motor vehicular crashes (MVCs), although the condition may also arise from insidious etiologies such as malignancies and chronic tuberculous infection. Spinal cord lesions may lead to permanent disability, significant morbidity, and even mortality. High spinal injuries often impair cardiorespiratory function, requiring emergent interventions.

name: Femoral nerve distribution
definition: Paresthesias in anterior/medial aspect of the thigh (anterior and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh) and/or medial aspect of the lower leg and foot (saphenous distribution). May be accompanied by weakness in the quadriceps.

name: Triceps tendon rupture
definition: Breakage (tear) of the triceps tendon.

name: Digoxin exposure
definition: History of having been treateed with digoxin.
comments: Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside derived from the foxglove plant (digitalis species). It has inotropic effects and is utilized in the management of systolic dysfunction in patients with congestive heart failure (CHF) and as an atrioventricular nodal blocking agent for managing atrial tachydysrhythmias. Gastrointestinal upset is the most common symptom of digoxin toxicity. Patients also may report visual symptoms, which classically present as a yellow-green discoloration, and cardiovascular symptoms, such as palpitations, dyspnea, and syncope.

name: Upper arm pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the upper arm.
comments: Pain anywhere between the shoulder and elbow. Upper arm pain may be observed with conditions such as ulnar shaft fracture, intersection syndrome of hand tendons, Galeazzi fracture, radial tunnel syndrome, and wrist dislocation.

name: Capitellum fracture
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the capitulum of the humerus, which is a smooth, rounded eminence on the lateral portion of the distal articular surface of the humerus.

name: Anterior shoulder pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the anterior (front) part of the shoulder.
comments: Pain localized to the anterior aspect of the shoulder. Anterior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as proximal biceps tendon tear.

name: Pain at the anterior aspect of the elbow
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the elbow front part of the elbow, that is, on the ventral side of the arm where the arm bends.

name: Posterior fat pad sign of the elbow
definition: Lateral elbow x-ray showing lucent crescent of fat that indicates a joint effusion in the elbow .

name: Pain at the anterior aspect of the knee
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the knee, that is, the side of the knee where the patella is located.

name: Pain at the posterior aspect of the knee
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back part of the knee, that is, opposite to the side of the knee where the patella is located.
comments: Pain at the posterior aspect of the knee may be observed with Baker cyst.

name: Biceps tendonitis
definition: Biceps tendinitis is inflammation of the tendon around the long head of the biceps muscle.
comments: MRI may show increased T2 signal around the biceps tendon or ultrasound showing thickening of the biceps tendon.

name: Increased peripheral nerve cross sectional area
definition: Ultrasonography showing increased cross sectional area (CSA) of a peripheral nerve as it travels through a potential site of compression.
comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar tunnel syndrome, cubital tunnel syndrome, and radial tunnel syndrome.

name: Pain exacerbated by passive flexion at joint
definition: Pain in extremity that worsens with joint is passively flexed.
comments: This feature may be observed in acute compartment syndrome.

name: Positive hook test at the elbow
definition: With forearm fully supinated and elbow flexed to 90 degrees, examiner hooks a finger a bit around the distal biceps tendon at the anterior aspect of the elbow. Test is positive when there is lack of appreciable cord like structure to hook around.
comments: This sign can indicate a distal biceps tendon tear.

name: Positive Speed's test
definition: Manual downward pressure on the arm with the shoulders flexed forward to 90 degrees, elbows fully extended, and palm facing up recreates pain in the anterior shoulder region; named after Dr. Speed.
comments: The Speed's test was recorded as positive if the patient experienced pain in the proximal portion of the shoulder during the application of a downward force applied to the arm. The patient's arm was placed with the forearm in full supination at 90 degrees of shoulder elevation. See Figure 1 of PMID:9848587.

name: Triangular lunate bone
definition: A disruption of the greater and lesser arcs of the lunate bone, with the lunate having a triangular silhouette, know as the piece of pie sign. Often caused by falling on an outstretched hand, patients will have tenderness to palpation over the dorsum of the wrist and may have sensory deficits in the median nerve distribution.

synonyms.text: Piece of pie sign of lunate bone

comments: See Figure 3 of PMID:23616330.

name: Pain exacerbated by wrist deviation
definition: Pain worsens with wrist ulnar or radial deviation.
comments: Ulnar: Triangular fibrocartilage complex tear; Ulnocarpal abutment syndrome Radial: Triangular fibrocartilage complex tear.

name: Pain on the lateral aspect of the foot
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the side of the foot nearest to the little (fifth) toe.

name: Pain at the medial aspect of the knee
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the inner side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces the other knee.
comments: This feature may be observed with medial collateral ligament knee injury.

name: Pain at the lateral aspect of the knee
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the outer side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces away from the other knee.
comments: This feature may be observed with lateral collateral ligament injury.

name: Occupational exposure to frequent kneeling
definition: A history of exposure to frequent squatting/kneeling and/or heavy lifting.
comments: Occupations that require frequent kneeling such as roofing, construction workers, plumbers, electricians, landscapers, gardeners, carpenters, and housekeepers may increase risk of prepatellar bursitis and knee osteoarthritis.

name: Trochanteric pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the structures around the greater trochanter (the bony prominence on the outer part of the femur).

synonyms.text: Pain at the lateral aspect of the hip
Pain on the outside of the hip

name: Pulsatile mass in extremity
definition: A noticeable lump or swelling in the arm or leg that you can feel with you fingers and this lump is beating or pulsating, similar to the feeling of a heartbeat.
comments: This finding may be observed with conditions such as arteriovenous malformation located in the arm or leg or withulnar artery thrombosis.

name: Abnormal R wave
definition: Any anomaly of the R wave of the EKG, which is the first upward deflection after the P wave. The R wave reflects early ventricular depolarisation.

name: Poor R-wave progression
definition: Absence of the normal increase in size of the R wave in the precordial leads when advancing from lead V1 to V6 of the electrocardiogram.
comments: With normal R wave progression, the amplitude of the R wave gradually increased from V1 to V5 and decreases from V5 to V6. Abnormal R wave progression may be observed with myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, right or left ventricular hypertrophy, and other conditions.

name: Prominent V1-V2 R wave
definition: The R wave in leads V1-V2 is normally considerably smaller in amplitude than the S wave in the same leads. Prominent R wave in these leads implies the R wave is larger than the S-wave, which may indicate cardiovascular pathology. This term includes Tall R wave in lead V1, which is defined by a R/S ratio greater than 1.

synonyms.text: High voltage R wave in V1/V2
Prominent R wave in lead V1

comments: This electrocardiographic finding exists as a normal variant in only 1% of patients. Physicians should therefore be familiar with the differential diagnosis for this important QRS configuration. The electrocardiographic entities which can present with this finding include right bundle branch block, left ventricular ectopy, right ventricular hypertrophy, acute right ventricular dilation (acute right heart strain), type a Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, posterior myocardial infarction, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, progressive muscular dystrophy, dextrocardia, misplaced precordial leads, and normal variant.

name: Finger mass
definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a finger.
comments: The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

name: Foot mass
definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a foot.
comments: The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

name: Abnormal retinal vein morphology
definition: A condition characterized by structural abnormalities of the retinal veins, including tortuosity, dilation, narrowing, or irregularities in branching patterns. These changes may be associated with systemic or ocular diseases such as retinal vein occlusion, diabetic retinopathy, or hypertensive retinopathy.

name: Spongiosis
definition: Spongiosis refers to the increased intercellular edema in the epidermis resulting in the pulling away of the keratinocytes from their surrounding desmosomes. Histologically, the spongiotic tissue reaction pattern involves the accumulation of fluid in the intercellular spaces of the epidermis, making the desmosomes junctions more easy to appreciate. Parakeratosis forms above the areas of spongiosis. The foci of spongiosis can be microscopic to grossly identifiable clinically with vesicles or bullae.
comments: Comment: Spongiosis is present in all diseases manifesting clinically as eczema; however, there are diseases with spongiosis that do not belong to the eczema spectrum, e.g., pityriasis rosea, erysipelas or tinea. . Spongiotic dermatoses include a very large list of disorders which are best grouped under neutrophilic, eosinophilic, miliarial, follicular and pityriasiform forms of spongiosis.

name: Discoid adrenal gland
definition: A congenital finding where the adrenal gland does not form it's typical triangular, Y or V shape and is instead discoid, straight or elongated in shape. It is often found incidentally on renal ultrasound and is associated with renal agenesis and other renal congenital anomalies.

name: Abnormal optic disc vasculature morphology
definition: A structural abnormality in the blood vessels of the optic disc, including bleeding, tortuosity, dilation, shunting, or other unusual branching patterns.
comments: May be associated with conditions such as glaucoma, papilledema, leber optic neuropathy, or optic disc drusen, and can contribute to visual field defects or other optic neuropathies.

name: Supraclavicular nerve distribution
definition: Localization of symptoms such as numbness or paresthesias on the skin over the upper chest, specifically above the clavicle and over the lateral aspect of the neck, corresponding to the distribution of the supraclavicular nerve.
comments: May be observed with clavicle shaft fracture.

name: Limited shoulder internal rotation
definition: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm towards the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.
comments: Conditions characterized by this finding include shoulder internal impingement syndrome, pectoralis major rupture, proximal humeral epiphysiolysis, and rotator cuff tear arthropathy.

name: Superior displacement of the humeral head
definition: An anterior posterior (AP) shoulder radiograph shows distance between the the proximal aspect of the humeral head and inferior aspect of the acromion of less than 7 mm.

synonyms.text: Proximal subluxation of the humeral head

comments: Conditions characterized by this finding include rotator cuff tear arthropathy, rotator cuff tear, and shoulder external impingement syndrome.

name: Increased compartment pressure
definition: intracompartmental pressure (ICP) over 30 mmHg. Acute compartment syndrome occurs when there is increased pressure within a closed osteofascial compartment, resulting in impaired local circulation. Acute compartment syndrome is considered a surgical emergency since, without proper treatment, it can lead to ischemia and eventually necrosis. Generally, acute compartment syndrome is considered a clinical diagnosis. However, ICP over 30 mmHg can be used as a threshold to aid in diagnosis.
comments: Fascia is a thin, inelastic sheet of connective tissue that surrounds muscle compartments and limits the capacity for rapid expansion. The earliest objective physical finding is the tense, or wood-like feeling of the involved compartment. Pain is typically severe, out of proportion to the injury. Measurement of intracompartmental pressure is not required but can aid in diagnosis if uncertainty exists. Compartment pressures are often measured with a manometer, a device that detects intracompartmental pressure by measuring the resistance that is present when a saline solution is injected into the compartment. The normal pressure within the compartment is between 0 mmHg to 8 mmHg. An intra-compartmental pressure greater than 30 mmHg indicates compartment syndrome and a need for fasciotomy.

name: Pain at the lateral aspect of the elbow
definition: Pain localized to the radial aspect of the elbow.

name: Pain at the posterior aspect of the elbow
definition: Pain localized to the posterior aspect of the elbow.
comments: The posterior aspect of the elbow refers to the back side of the elbow, which forms the prominent bony tip of the elbow.

name: Pain at the medial aspect of the elbow
definition: Pain localized to the medial aspect of the elbow.
comments: The medial aspect of the elbow refers to the inner side of the elbow. Conditions characterized by this finding include medial epicondylitis.

name: Radial nerve distribution
definition: Applies to the localization of findings corresponding to the distribution of the radial nevrve, such as (i)paresthesias on the dorsoradial aspect of the hand and wrist, including the dorsal thumb, index finger and middle finger and (ii) Weakness in elbow extension, wrist extension, finger extension, thumb extension and/or supination of the forearm.

name: Omovertebral bone
definition: An osseous connection between the superomedial border of the right scapula and C5-C6 spinous processes.
comments: The omovertebral bone is seen in approximately one-third of patients with Sprengel deformity. The clinical presentation of SD varies, ranging from simply limited shoulder abduction and mild cosmetic deformity to severe clinical abnormalities. Nonsurgical management is appropriate for mild cases, while severe deformities require surgery. See Figure 1 of PMID:38908946.

name: Clavicular edema
definition: Swelling on the chest between the neck and the shoulder, above the clavicel (collar bone).
comments: This condition may be observed with diseases including congenital pseudoarthrosis of clavicle and clavicle shaft fracture.

name: Positive CSF anti-measles antibody test
definition: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of measles virus.

synonyms.text: Elevated measles antibody titer in cerebrospinal fluid

comments: This finding may be observed with diseases including subacute sclerosing leukoencephalitis.

name: Vogt striae
definition: Vertical lines in the posterior stroma of the cornea, aligned with Descemet membrane. These lines temporarily disappear with pressure applied to the cornea. Vogt striae are a hallmark feature of keratoconus but have also been observed in healthy eyes. Rare cases of horizontal striae have been reported.

name: Choroid thickening
definition: A condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the thickness of the choroid, which may be associated with various ocular or systemic conditions. Choroid thickening can be measured using imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT).

name: Corneal epithelial edema
definition: A condition characterized by accumulation of fluid within the corneal epithelium, leading to swelling, blurred vision, and discomfort. It is often associated with increased intraocular pressure, endothelial dysfunction, or contact lens overuse. Clinical features may include a hazy cornea and microcystic changes visible on slit-lamp examination.
comments: This finding can be observed in diseases such as Fuchs endothelial dystrophy, acute angle-closure glaucoma, and bullous keratopathy.

name: Retinal shunt vessels
definition: bnormal blood vessels in the retina that form as a response to vascular occlusion, serving as bypass channels to redirect blood flow around obstructed or damaged retinal vessels. Retinal shunt vessels are often associated with conditions like retinal vein occlusion or diabetic retinopathy and may appear as tortuous or dilated vessels on fundoscopic examination.
comments: See Figure 12 of PMID:37238303.

name: Filamentary keratitis
definition: A condition characterized by the formation of filaments composed of degenerated epithelial cells and mucus attached to the corneal surface. It is associated with symptoms such as pain, foreign body sensation, photophobia, and tearing. Filamentary keratitis is often linked to underlying conditions such as dry eye disease, post-surgical ocular surface disorders, or systemic diseases like Sjoegren syndrome.

name: Elevated circulating glucosylsphingosine concentration
definition: Concentration of D-glucosylsphingosine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) is a key biomarker of Gaucher Disease.

name: Optic disc hemorrhage
definition: A condition characterized by bleeding at or near the optic disc, visible as a flame-shaped or splinter hemorrhage on fundoscopic examination.
comments: Optic disc bleeding is a significant clinical marker in glaucoma, particularly normal-tension glaucoma, and is associated with disease progression. It may result from mechanical stress on the lamina cribrosa or vascular dysregulation.

name: Decreased circulating progranulin concentration
definition: The concentration of progranulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
comments: Progranulin, a secreted glycoprotein, maintains cerebrocortical viability. It has been identified as an important factor controlling neural function while also suppressing neuroinflammation and playing roles in neuronal lysosome function. Loss of one allele of GRN, the gene encoding progranulin, leads to the development of frontotemporal dementia, and loss of both alleles leads to the development of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.

name: Preauricular lymphadenopathy
definition: Enlargement of one or more lymph nodes located in front of the ear.

name: Onychoheterotopia
definition: Growth of nail tissue outside the ungual plate, generally in the finger.

name: Abnormal MHC surface expression
definition: A deviation from the normal level of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules expressed at the cell surface. The cell-mediated adaptive immune response is regulated by the MHC, which is called human leukocyte antigen (HLA) in humans. HLA molecules are cell surface glycoproteins whose primary function is to present endogenous and exogenous antigens to T lymphocytes for recognition and response. The HLA molecules that present antigen to T lymphocytes are divided into two main classes: HLA class I and HLA class II molecules.

name: Forward displacement of posterior cervical dura mater on neck flexion
definition: Flexion MRI (imaging with neutral and flexed about 30-40 degrees neck position) reveals an anterior shift of the cervical dural sac from the lamina in the region of C4 to C7.
comments: This finding is characteristic of Monomelic amyotrophy (Hirayama disease) is a rare motor neuron disorder characterized by progressive weakness and atrophy in the distal upper extremities, typically beginning during adolescence. The condition involves asymmetric muscle atrophy in the hand and forearm, sparing the brachioradialis muscle, and is attributed to increased laxity in the dura mater, which causes the spinal cord to shift forward during neck flexion. Increased laxity of the dura mater from its superior anchors on the dorsal surfaces of C2 and C3, harbingering forward cord movement during cervical flexion. Increased laxity allows the spinal cord to shift forward, leading to repeated subclinical trauma and microischemia in the anterior horn during cervical flexion. Trauma and microischemia eventually lead to myelopathy and degeneration, as evidenced by asymmetric lower cervical cord thinning within the C7 and C8.

name: Corneal dellen
definition: A localized area of corneal thinning typically occurring adjacent to an elevated lesion, such as a conjunctival scar, pterygium, or poorly fitting contact lens. Corneal dellen result from tear film instability and localized dehydration. Without timely treatment, they may progress to epithelial defects or corneal ulceration.
comments: Diseases characterized by this finding include corneal pterygium, corneal ulceration, and post-surgical ocular surface disorder.

name: Conjunctival xerosis
definition: A condition characterized by dryness of the conjunctiva, often associated with keratinization of the conjunctival epithelium. Conjunctival xerosis is commonly linked to vitamin A deficiency, severe dry eye disease, or systemic conditions such as Sjogren syndrome. Clinical features may include a dull, rough conjunctival surface and reduced mucosal secretions.
comments: Diseases characterized by this term include vitamin A deficiency, Sjogren syndrome, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

name: Limited shoulder external rotation
definition: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.
comments: Diseases characterized by this finding include rotator cuff tear.

name: Occupational exposure to frequent hand trauma
definition: A history of exposure to repeated hand trauma as observed with occupations in which use of hands is frequent such as construction, food preparation and serving related occupations, and transportation and material moving occupations.

name: Inability to fully extend finger at metacarpophalangeal joint
definition: An inability to fully extend the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of a finger (extension of an MCP joint straightens the finger).

synonyms.text: Inability to fully extend finger at MCP joint
Inability to fully extend finger from base

name: Wrist arthritis
definition: Inflammation of the wrist joint.
comments: Symptoms of arthritis include pain, swelling, redness, stiffness, and loss of motion of the involved joint. Three primary types of arthritis affect the human wrist: osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and post-traumatic arthritis.

name: Scapholunate interval widening
definition: Widening of the space between the scaphoid and lunate on x-ray; scapholunate dissociation.

name: FInger pulp localization
definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution is limited to or predominantly affects the fleshy mass on the volar (palmar) aspect of the digit, distal to the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint (known as the pulp of the finger).

synonyms.text: Symptoms localized to pulp of the finger

name: Ulnar wrist pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the ulnar side of the wrist.
comments: The ulnar side of the wrist is the side of the wrist closest to the little finger (fifth finger, pinky). Conditions characterized by this term include triangular fibrocartilage complex, distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) arthritis, and pisotriquetral (PT) osteoarthritis.

name: Lunotriquetral interval widening
definition: Radiographic widening of the space between the lunate and triquetrum bones.
comments: This finding may be observed with lunotriquetral ligament injury.

name: Ulnar translocation of the carpus
definition: Anteroposterior wrist radiograph showing ulnar translocation of the carpus from the distal radius with widening of the radial styloid-scaphoid space.
comments: This finding may be observed with Carpal instability nondissociative (CIND).

name: Snapping sensation at time of injury
definition: A popping or snapping sensation (noise or feeling) at the time of an injury.
comments: Sudden snapping or popping at the time of an injury can be a sign of significant damage to muscles, tendons, ligaments, or bones.

name: Pagetoid spread
definition: Pagetoid spread connotes the spread of single neoplastic cells, and small nests of them above the basal layer in a variety of melanocytic and nonmelanocytic neoplasms similar to the pattern seen in Paget's and in extramammary Paget disease.
comments: Pagetoid proliferation of single melanocytic cells or small nests of melanocytes may be seen in a variety of melanocytic neoplasms including pagetoid spitz nevi, de novo epithelioid melanocytic dysplasia, and melanoma. Pagetoid melanocytosis may also be a common feature of acral nevi, traumatized nevi, or in nevi after acute sun exposure.

name: Central scarring
definition: Central scarring of skin lesions.

name: Scapholunate ligament tear
definition: A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the scapholunate ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Tear of the scapholunate ligament may lead to carpal instability.
comments: Together with the lunotriquetral interosseous ligament, the scapholunate ligament is one of the two proximal interosseous carpal ligaments of the wrist. It is a C-shaped ligament that binds the scaphoid bone to the lunate bone of the wrist. A scapholunate tear can be partial or complete. Since it is C-shaped, it often is only one limb of the C that is torn.

name: Lunotriquetral ligament tear
definition: A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the lunotriquetral ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Rupture or tear of the the lunotriquetral ligament may lead to carpal instability.
comments: The scapholunate and lunotriquetral interosseous ligaments form the interconnections between the bones of the proximal carpal row and share several anatomic features. Each forms a barrier between the radiocarpal and midcarpal joints, connecting the dorsal, proximal, and palmar edges of the respective joint surfaces.

name: Pisotriquetral arthritis
