definition: Arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint. Radiographic evidence of arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint includes joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral cysts, and/or subchondral sclerosis.

name: Volar intercalated segment instability
definition: A type of carpal instability characterized by volar tilt of the lunate bone.
comments: Lateral wrist radiograph showing volar flexion of the lunate with a scapholunate angle less than 30 degrees. This finding may be observed with conditions such as lunotriquetral ligament injury and carpal instability nondissociative.

name: Inaccurate finger pulse oximetry oxygen saturation measurement
definition: Any substantial discrepancy between the measurement of oxygen saturation with finger probe pulse oximetry as compared to an arterial blood gas, which is considered the gold standard.
comments: Pulse oximetry is an useful, readily available and non-invasive tool of measuring oxygen saturation. It uses light sensors containing two light sources of different wavelengths, that are absorbed by haemoglobin (both oxy and deoxy forms) and transmitted through tissues to a photodetector. Any discrepancy in the light transmission caused either by vascular abnormality of the fingers or anatomical change may lead to inaccurate or absence of reading in the pulse oximeter.

name: Finger pulse oximetry lower than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
definition: Inaccurately reduced oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.
comments: This feature may be observed with conditions such as Raynaud phenomenon and scleroderma, in which peripheral microvasculopathy leads to poor perfusion of the fingers.

name: Finger pulse oximetry higher than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
definition: Inaccurately elevated oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.
comments: This feature may be observed with Carbon monoxide poisoning. Presently available pulse oximeters overestimate arterial oxygenation in patients with severe CO poisoning. An elevated COHb level falsely elevates the SaO2 measurements from pulse oximetry.

name: History of thumb sucking past the age of four years
definition: Thumb sucking is a behavior that ceases spontaneously in most children between 2 and 4 years of age. If thumb sucking continues, negative consequences can occur, such as a deformity of the nail or paronychia. This term refers to a history of habitual thumb sucking past the age of 4 years of life.

name: Cutaneous granulomatosis
definition: Skin inflammatory reaction triggered by a wide variety of stimuli, including infections, foreign bodies, malignancy, metabolites, and chemicals. From a pathogenic point of view, they are divided into non-infectious and infectious granulomas. From a clinical point of view, it is useful to divide cutaneous granulomatosis into localized and more disseminated forms, although this distinction can be sometimes artificial.

name: Ureteric stricture
definition: Obstruction of urine flow through one or both ureters caused by issues such as injury, infection, tumours and surgery.

name: Arteriovenous crossing sign
definition: A retinal vascular abnormality characterized by indentation or compression of a retinal vein at an arteriovenous crossing, leading to changes in venous caliber. AV crossing signs are commonly associated with hypertensive retinopathy and may contribute to retinal vein occlusion. They are indicative of vascular remodeling due to chronic hypertension or other systemic vascular diseases.
comments: This feature may be present in diseases such as hypertensive retinopathy and retinal vein occlusion.

name: Haab striae
definition: Curvilinear or circumferential breaks in Descemet membrane, typically associated with congenital glaucoma. Haab striae result from elevated intraocular pressure during corneal development, leading to the formation of horizontal or arcuate lines that may be visible on slit-lamp examination. They can contribute to corneal astigmatism and visual impairment.

name: Positive Legionella sputum culture
definition: Growth of Legionella bacteria in a sputum culture.

name: Positive Streptococcus pneumoniae sputum culture
definition: Streptococcus pneumoniae growth in sputum culture.

name: Positive Blastomyces dermatitidis sputum fungal stain
definition: Demonstration of Blastomyces dermatitidis by microscopic examination of a stained sputum specimen.

synonyms.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis on sputum fungal stain

comments: Blastomycosis is a fungal infection caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis. It presents as a pulmonary infection after the inhalation of spores, and it may be either asymptomatic or have severe life-threatening complications like acute respiratory distress syndrome.

name: Posterior shoulder pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the posterior (back) part of the shoulder.
comments: Posterior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as shoulder internal impingement syndrome, suprascapular neuropathy, labrum tear, and shoulder dislocation.

name: Superior shoulder pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the superior or proximal aspect of the shoulder over the acromion, distal clavicle, and/or acromioclavicular (AC) joint.
comments: Superior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as acromioclavicular joint injury, acromioclavicular joint osteoarthritis, and distal clavicle osteolysis.

name: Lateral shoulder pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the localized aspect (on the side) of the shoulder.
comments: Lateral shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as proximal humerus fracture, proximal humeral epiphysiolysis, adhesive capsulitis, and suprascapular neuropathy.

name: Shoulder instability
definition: Subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the shoulder with movement, shoulder 'giving way', or sensation of shoulder dislocating.
comments: Shoulder instability may be observed in conditions such as shoulder dislocation, labrum tear, and suprascapular neuropathy.

name: Shoulder labrum tear
definition: A injury with a team (rip, split, or disruption) to the labrum, which is the ring of cartilage that surrounds the socket of the shoulder joint (the glenoid).
comments: Shoulder labral tears can be classified as superior Labral Anterior Posterior tear (SLAP); bankart lesion; anterior labral periosteal sleeve avulsion (ALPSA); and glenoid labral articular defect (GLAD) and may be observed in conditions such as shoulder dislocation, shoulder internal impingement syndrome, and acromioclavicular joint injury.

name: Positive modified dynamic labral shear test
definition: Sensation of a pain with or without clicking or clunking sensation with the following test. Flex patients elbow to 90 degrees and abduct the arm 120 degrees while maximally externally rotating the arm, then examiner lowers the arm to 60 degrees of abduction. A positive test occurs with pain and/or a painful click along the posterior joint line between 120 degrees and 90 degrees of abduction.
comments: This test is frequently positive with labrum tear of the shoulder.

name: Positive O'Brien active compression test
definition: Pain in shoulder reproduced when examiner applies downward pressure on the arm while patient resists pressure in the following position: elbow extended, shoulder forward flexed to 90 degrees and 10-15 degrees adducted with palm facing down. This can be compared to the same position but with the palm facing up which should be less painful.
comments: A positive test may be observed in conditions such as acromioclavicular joint injury, shoulder labrum tear, adhesive capsulitis, and biceps subluxation.

name: Positive shoulder apprehension test
definition: The individual being investigated displays noticeable apprehension (unease) during a test for shoulder instability in which the individual is laying supine with shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 90 degrees, and an external rotation pressure with combined downward pressure is applied on the upper arm.

name: Foamy tear film
definition: A condition characterized by the presence of foam or bubbles within the tear film, often associated with meibomian gland dysfunction or ocular surface diseases.
comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as Meibomian gland dysfunction and blepharitis.

name: Salzmann corneal nodules
definition: The formation of large, bluish, nodular lesions in the superficial corneal stroma, often associated with chronic keratitis or aging. These nodules may lead to visual impairment.

name: Corneal stromal vascularisation
definition: The abnormal growth of blood vessels into the corneal stroma, often associated with ocular herpes, chronic inflammation, infection, or hypoxia. This condition can lead to corneal scarring and vision impairment.
comments: This feature may be observed in herpetic eye disease.

name: Corneal iron line
definition: Linear or arcuate deposition of iron within the corneal epithelium or stroma, typically associated with conditions such as keratoconus, corneal degeneration, or postsurgical corneal changes.

name: Conjunctivochalasis
definition: A condition characterized by redundant, loose conjunctival tissue, typically located between the globe and the lower eyelid, which may cause ocular discomfort, tear film instability, or epiphora.
comments: Conjunctivochalasis can be observed with conditions such as dry eye and floppy eyelid syndrome.

name: Conjunctival hyperpigmentation
definition: Increased pigmentation of the conjunctiva, characterized by brown or black discoloration due to melanocytic proliferation or pigment deposition. It may be associated with benign conditions such as primary acquired melanosis or malignant transformation into conjunctival melanoma.

name: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies
definition: Antibodies against antigens presented by the cell wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
comments: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (ASCAs) have been used as a marker for Crohn disease, Behcet disease, celiac disease, and other conditions.

name: Elevated fraction exhaled nitric oxide
definition: The fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is elevated above the upper limit of normal. FeNO is an endogenous gaseous molecule which can be measured in the human breath test because of airway inflammation. It has been studied extensively as a marker of inflammation and has been incorporated into an algorithm for asthma management.
comments: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a simple, reproducible, and a noninvasive marker of inflammation that may be elevated in diseases such as ssthma, eosinophilic pneumonia, COPD, pulmonary fibrosis, and interstitial lung disease.

name: Iris hyperemia
definition: A condition characterized by increased blood flow and congestion of the iris vasculature, leading to a reddish discoloration of the iris. Iris hyperemia is commonly associated with anterior uveitis, angle-closure glaucoma, or ocular inflammation.

name: Elevated circulating reticulated platelet count
definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

name: Reduced circulating reticulated platelet count
definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

name: Abnormal circulating reticulated platelet count
definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is outside the limits of normal.
comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

name: Flexed posturing of finger
definition: A sign that can be observed in diseases such as Pyogenic or suppurative flexor tenosynovitis in which the affected finger is held in a flexed position. Often, there is pain on any attempt at passive finger extension. This finding is to be distinguished from a contracture of a finger joint in which the flexed positions is fixed.
comments: This finding is one of the four Kanavel signs for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis: (i) flexed posturing of the involved digit; (ii) tenderness to palpation over the tendon sheath; (iii) marked pain with passive extension of the digit; and (iv) fusiform swelling of the digit.

name: Positive synovial fluid alpha-defensin
definition: Elevation of the the alpha-defensin concentration in synovial aspirate is above the upper limit of normal. The alpha-defensin test is a qualitative immunoassay optimized and validated for synovial fluid. The alpha-defensin protein is an antimicrobial peptide that is naturally released by neutrophils responding to a pathogen in the synovial fluid.
comments: The alpha-defensin test has been previously demonstrated to be highly accurate in the diagnosis of prosthetic joint infection.

name: Physeal fracture
definition: Salter-Harris fractures (physeal fractures) refer to fractures through a growth plate (physis) and are, therefore, specifically applied to bone fractures in children.

name: Salter I fracture
definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture line extends through the physis or within the growth plate. Type I fractures are due to the longitudinal force applied through the physis, which splits the epiphysis from the metaphysis.
comments: Beware that a normal radiograph cannot exclude a physis injury in a symptomatic pediatric patient. A radiograph may be normal due to lack of bony involvement, and mild to moderate soft tissue swelling may be noted. Look for the widening of the physis or displacement of the epiphysis, which may suggest a fracture. Diagnosis is based on clinical findings, such as the presence of focal tenderness or swelling surrounding the growth plate.

name: Salter II fracture
definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture extends through both the physis and metaphysis. These are most common and occur away from the joint space. When the small corner of the metaphysis is visible, this is known as a corner sign or Thurston-Holland fragment.

name: Salter III fracture
definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and extends from the physis into the epiphysis.
comments: If the fracture extends the complete length of the physis, this type of fracture may form two epiphyseal segments. Since the epiphysis is involved, damage to the articular cartilage may occur. One example is a Tillaux fracture of the ankle, which is a fracture of the anterolateral aspect of the growth plate and epiphysis.

name: Salter IV fracture
definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and passes through the epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis.
comments: As this fracture involves the epiphysis, the articular cartilage may be damaged. Types III and IV fractures each carry a risk for growth retardation, altered joint mechanics, and functional impairment. Therefore, both require urgent orthopedic evaluation.

name: Salter V fracture
definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture that is due to a crush or compression injury of the growth plate. In type V, the force is transmitted through the epiphysis and physis, potentially disrupting the germinal matrix, hypertrophic region, and vascular supply.
comments: Though Harris-Salter V fractures are very rare, they may be seen in electric shock, frostbite, and irradiation cases. As this fracture pattern tends to result from severe injury, these typically have a poor prognosis leading to bone growth arrest.

name: Nail bed laceration
definition: A cut or injury to the soft tissue under the fingernail or toenail.

name: History of distal radius fracture
definition: Recent or remote history of distal radius fracture of the symptomatic arm.
comments: This finding refers to a medical history of distal radius fracture in the arm that is the focus of current medical attention. This finding may relate to scapholunate advanced collapse, distal radioulnar joint arthritis, and scapholunate ligament injury.

name: History of triangular fibrocartilage complex tear
definition: Recent or remote history of a tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). The TFCC is a load-bearing structure between the lunate, triquetrum, and ulnar head. The function of the TFCC is to act as a stabilizer for the ulnar aspect of the wrist. The TFCC is at risk for either acute or chronic degenerative injury.
comments: Such a history is important for the diagnosis of Distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) arthritis.

name: Reduced plantar creases
definition: The creases (wrinkles) on the soles of the feet are less pronounced than normal, or absent.
comments: This finding may be seen in premature infants and in some conditions such as GFRA1-related Apert syndrome, renal hypodysplasia/aplasia 4, and Atelis syndrome 2.

name: Skin burn
definition: Damage to the skin and underlying tissues caused by an agents such as heat, chemicals, electricity, radiation, or friction, resulting in pain, redness, swelling, and sometimes blisters or charring.
comments: This term does not refer to sunburn.

name: Elevanted carboxysterol concentration in cultured lymphoblasts
definition: The concentration of carboxysterols in lymphoblastoid cells cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium is below the lower limit of normal.
comments: When cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium, lymphoblastoid cells of individuals with CHILD syndrome and CK syndrome have increased levels of methyl- and carboxysterols and slightly decreased levels of cholesterol.

name: Superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
definition: An anomaly that can be ascertained by iron-specific magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences such as gradient-echo (GRE) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system is a chronic condition due to persistent or repeated long-term bleeding into the subarachnoid space, leading to subpial hemosiderin deposition. Hemosiderin deposition on MRI is seen as a T2 hypointensity and preferentially outlines the cerebellum and brainstem surface.
comments: Superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition is a manifestation of superficial siderosis (SS) of the central nervous system (CNS), which is typically due to chronic low-grade extravasation of blood into the subarachnoid space. Hemoglobin in red blood cells in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) breaks down into globin and neurotoxic heme. In response to the presence of neurotoxic heme, neuroglial cells release hemoxygenase and apoferritin. Hemoxygenase breaks heme into free iron and biliverdin, and apoferritin binds free iron to form ferritin and subsequently hemosiderin. This process is likely neuroprotective and prevents free iron mediated neuronal injury. Persistence of blood in the subarachnoid space eventually overwhelms the ferritin production capacity and unbound iron results in free-radical mediated neuronal injury. Hemosiderin deposits in regions of the brain or spinal cord adjacent to CSF. This confluent subpial hemosiderin deposition results in a characteristic marginal and confluent T2-hypointensity on magnetic resonance imaging that is referred to as SS and it is best appreciated on iron-sensitive sequences.

name: Cortical superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
definition: A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that most commonly occurs due to iron deposits in the superficial cortical layers following bleeding from leptomeningeal vessels, most often from cerebral amyloid angiopathy in patients aged 55 or older.

name: Infratentorial superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
definition: A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that involves the cerebellum and brainstem, most commonly the superior vermis, quadrigeminal plate, and basal cerebral surfaces. Cerebellar atrophy, particularly the superior vermis and anterior cerebellar hemispheres, can also be seen on a computed tomography scan of the head. The MRI of the spinal cord may reveal myelomalacia, syringomyelia, owl-eyes, or snake-eyes signs. The most common etiology for classic or primary infratentorial superficial siderosis is spinal dural defects, often dural tears.

name: Pulmonary hyperplasia
definition: Pulmonary Hyperplasia is an absolute increase in the number of alveoli, which are mildly enlarged. Pulmonary hyperplasia has been also referred to as polyalveolar lobe and type 3 cystic adenomatoid malformation.
comments: The pathogenesis and clinical characteristics of pulmonary hyperplasia are related to congenital lobar overinflation/emphysema, but should be distinguished. In the latter condition, the volume increase is due to alveolar enlargement as opposed to an absolute increase in alveoli. Radial alveolar counts can be helpful for distinguishing between these two abnormalities. Pulmonary hyperplasia may be associated with in utero death due to compression of venous return to the heart and/or esophageal compression, resulting in polyhydramnios and fetal hydrops. The therapy for infants with lobar distension causing severe mediastinal shift and normal lung compression is surgical removal of the affected lobe or segment.

name: Positive protozoan parasite CSF wet mount test
definition: Demonstration of protozoan parasites in a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimen by microscopy.

name: Gallbladder polyp
definition: A gallbladder (GB) polyp is a growth that projects from the lining of the inside wall of the gallbladder into the lumen of the GB. GB polyps are a common incidental sonographic finding, the vast majority of which are benign.
comments: Most benign GB polyps are non-neoplastic, including cholesterol pseudopolyps and inflammatory polyps.

name: Gallbladder polyposis
definition: Multiple polyps arising from the gallbladder mucosal wall.

name: Biceps tendon rupture
definition: Discontinuity of the biceps tendon as observed by ultrasound or magnetic resonance (MR) imaging.
comments: Patients suffering from biceps tendon rupture may complain of sudden sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, depending on the site of the rupture. Usually, there is a history of sudden eccentric force to a flexed elbow. They may feel an audible pop in the affected arm at the time of the injury. Pain can persist for weeks to months.

name: Medial epicondyle apophysitis
definition: Medial epicondyle apophysitis (MEA), also known as little league elbow, is an overuse injury prevalent among adolescent athletes whose sport involves repetitive overhand throwing, racket use, or other overhead arm motions. The medial epicondyle is a bony protrusion on the medial elbow with its own ossification center, separate from the main distal humeral physis, known as an apophysis. Medial epicondyle apophysitis occurs due to excessive and repetitive valgus stress placed on the apophysis before its closure. Over time, the repetitive strain results in a traction-type injury and may cause pathologic widening and inflammation of the apophysis or even an avulsion fracture.

name: Thumb carpometacarpal subluxation
definition: A partial (subluxation) loss of alignment at the base of the thumb, where the first metacarpal bone meets the trapezium bone of the wrist. Thumb radiographs showing carpometacarpal (CMC) joint space widening and/or incongruity of the joint space between thumb metacarpal bone and the trapezium bone.

name: Localized to lower eyelid
definition: A descriptor indicating that a condition, lesion, or abnormality is confined to the lower eyelid. This localization may be relevant for various ocular conditions, including infections, structural abnormalities, or dermatological diseases affecting the lower eyelid region.
comments: An anatomical spatial pattern or localization referring to the lower eyelid, the smaller, less mobile fold of skin and tissue positioned below the eye.

name: Localized to eyelid
definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in an eyelid.

name: Halo vision
definition: A visual phenomenon characterized by the perception of bright rings or halos surrounding light sources. Halo vision is often associated with optical irregularities such as corneal edema, cataracts, or intraocular lens complications. It may also occur in conditions affecting the tear film or due to the presence of glare from light scattering within the ocular media.

name: Hematospermia
definition: The presence of blood in the seminal fluid.

name: Choledocholithiasis
definition: Choledocholithiasis is the presence of stones within the common bile duct.
comments: It is estimated that common bile duct stones are present in anywhere from 1-15% of patients with cholelithiasis.

name: Axillary nerve distribution
definition: Paresthesias on the lateral aspect of the shoulder and upper arm. Weakness in shoulder abduction (deltoid) and shoulder external rotation (teres minor).

name: Pelvic ring fracture
definition: X-ray of the pelvis (AP, inlet, and outlet views) showing fracture of the pelvic ring, including iliac wing (ilium), superior or inferior pubic ramus, or ischium, and/or displacement of the pubic symphysis or sacroiliac joints.

name: Scapulothoracic dissociation
definition: An injury consisting of a laterally displaced scapula with separation of the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint, disruption of the ipsilateral subclavian vessels and brachial plexus, and an intact overlying skin.
comments: Scapulothoracic dissociation may be associated with a laterally displaced scapula with an ipsilateral distracted clavicular fracture (most common type), acromioclavicular joint separation or less commonly sternoclavicular joint disruption, without or with concomitant injuries to the ipsilateral subclavian or axillary vessels and the brachial plexus.

name: Pain exacerbated by weight bearing
definition: Refers to pain that is worse when the individual bears weight with the affected body part.
comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as hip fracture, tibial shaft fracture, calcaneus fracture, and ankle sprain.

name: Thumb sign
definition: The distal phalanx of the adducted thumb extends beyond the ulnar border of the palm (The thumb protrudes from the clenched fist).
comments: The Steinberg or the thumb sign is elicited by asking the patient to fold his thumb into the closed fist. If the thumb tip extends from the palm of the hand, the test is positive.

name: Tibialis anterior tendon rupture
definition: Partial or complete breakage (rupture) of the tibialis anterior tendon (TAT). The TAT is the principal dorsiflexor of the ankle joint and secondary invertor of the foot. It has important roles in the different stages of gait; in the swing phase, it concentrically dorsiflex the ankle for foot clearance and during plantarflexion of the ankle in the stance phase, it eccentrically contract to stabilize the ankle and prevent damage to the foot and ankle. Clinically, presentations in acute lacerations or direct trauma cases are straight forward, in chronic and atraumatic cases usually the symptoms at the time of TAT rupture are more subtle. Other manifestations include mild pain, localized mass, palpable gap, loss of strength, instability during gait, gait disturbances with forefoot dropping and stumbling and high stepping gait.

name: Decreased circulating ADAMTS13 activity
definition: Activity of the enzyme von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease (ADAMTS13) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
comments: A severe deficiency of ADAMTS13 (a disintegrin-like and metalloprotease with thrombospondin type 1 repeats) as detected by current assays, less than 5 percent of normal activity, may be specific for Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).

name: Abnormal methacholine challenge test
definition: An abnormal result of the methacholine challenge test, which is a bronchoprovocation technique used to evaluate airway hyperresponsiveness, particularly in patients with suspected asthma.
comments: Methacholine, a derivative of acetylcholine, directly induces bronchoconstriction by stimulating airway smooth muscle receptors. In some cases, hyperresponsiveness may be the only objective sign of asthma, making this test a valuable diagnostic tool. The procedure involves stepwise administration of methacholine, followed by spirometry to measure the forced expiratory volume in 1 second. This process continues until either a 20% reduction in the forced expiratory volume in 1 second or a 35-40% reduction in specific airways conductance is observed. The dose required to cause a 20% reduction is known as the provocation dose (PD20). A PD20 of 200 micrograms, or a provocation concentration (PC20) of 8 mg/mL or less, indicates a positive result (100 microgram or 4 mg/mL for specific airway conductance).

name: Positive stool glutamate dehydrogenase test
definition: Detection of the presence of glutamate dehydrogenase produced by Clostridium difficile in a stool sample.

synonyms.text: Detection of C. difficile glutamate dehydrogenase
Positive C. difficile glutamate dehydrogenase test

comments: Clostridium difficile produces an NAD-specific glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), which converts l-glutamate into alpha-ketoglutarate through an irreversible reaction. The enzyme GDH is detected in the stool samples of patients with C. difficile-associated disease and serves as one of the diagnostic tools to detect C. difficile infection. Clostridium difficile is the leading cause of hospital-acquired diarrhoea, which ranges in severity from mild diarrhoea to fulminant colitis.

name: Retrocorneal membrane
definition: A retrocorneal membrane is an abnormal, fibrous or cellular tissue layer that forms on the posterior surface of the cornea, typically on or adjacent to the Descemet membrane. It may result from trauma, surgery (e.g., penetrating keratoplasty), inflammation, or endothelial cell dysfunction, and can lead to visual impairment depending on its density and extent.

name: Adrenal hemorrhage
definition: Adrenal hemorrhage is bleeding within the capsule of the adrenal gland.
comments: It is challenging to diagnose because it is considered rare and therefore overlooked in the differential diagnosis, while no clinical features or routine laboratory tests can immediately alert to the diagnosis. Most adrenal hemorrhages were unilateral, presenting incidentally or during trauma evaluation, and occurred secondary to postoperative complication or trauma.

name: Optic nerve sheath dilatation
definition: An abnormal increase in the diameter of the optic nerve sheath, typically due to elevated intracranial pressure or local pathology affecting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics. It can be detected via imaging modalities such as ultrasound or MRI and may be associated with papilledema, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, or optic nerve tumors.

synonyms.text: Dilation of the optic nerve sheath

name: Right ventricular thrombus
definition: A blood clot (thrombus) localized in the right ventricle.
comments: Right ventricular thrombus is a rare finding found in 4% of people diagnosed with pulmonary embolism. Although right ventricular thrombi are usually associated with atrial fibrillation, deep venous vein thrombi, or intracardiac procedures, isolated right ventricular thrombi are rare. Right ventricular thrombus has also been reported in patients with right ventricular infarction, as hypokinesis of the right ventricle causes blood stasis and promotes thrombosis as per Virchow's triad.

name: Severe Candida infection
definition: Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Candida. Severe manifestations include invasive candidiasis with hematogenous spread (candidaemia), hepatosplenic candidiasis, renal candidiasis, Candida endophthalmitis, and Candida endocarditis.
comments: Candida species are colonizers of the human skin and gastrointestinal (GI) tract, existing as part of the microbiome in many healthy individuals. The pathophysiology of disseminated candidiasis in immunocompromised patients is poorly understood but thought to be related to chemotherapy-induced mucositis and profound neutropenia. This allows for Candida species to enter the bloodstream where the organisms can translocate into the portal venous system and seed to the liver and spleen, which explains why the lesions are primarily seen in these two organs. Renal, pulmonary, and other organ involvement have also been documented but not as common.

name: Phrenic neuropathy
definition: A functional deficit of the phrenic nerve. Phrenic neuropathy (PhN) is a debilitating condition characterized by impairment of the diaphragm muscle, the primary inspiratory muscle. Diaphragm muscle ultrasound is a noninvasive tool that appears to offer both high sensitivity and specificity for diagnosis. Alternatively, electrodiagnostic studies can assess phrenic nerve health. PhN is commonly diagnosed via diaphragm muscle US or fluoroscopy (sniff test) with paradoxical or significantly decreased diaphragm muscle movement.

name: Glomerular basement membrane subendothelial remodeling
definition: New glomerular basement membrane matrix formation under the endothelial cell.

name: Glomerular endothelium swelling
definition: Enlargement of the glomerular endothelium (the innermost layer of the glomerular filtration barrier) causing capillary lumen narrowing and loss of fenetrations.

name: Medullary collecting duct ectasia
definition: Widening of the lumen of the lumen of the collecting ducts in the renal medulla.

name: Corneal keloid
definition: A raised, opaque, and fibrous lesion on the cornea resembling a dermal keloid, typically composed of disorganized collagen and fibrovascular tissue. Corneal keloids can impair vision and are often secondary to trauma, surgery, or underlying congenital disorders.

name: Podocytic mitochondrial proliferation
definition: An ultrastructural abnormality of the kidney glomeruli characterized by an excessive number or abnormal aggregation of mitochondria in podocytes.
comments: Typically observed by electron microscopy in patients with mitochondrial dysfunction-related nephrotic syndromes.

name: Elevated vitamin D metabolite ratio
definition: The ratio of 24,25(OH)2D to 25(OH)D (also known as vitamin D metabolite ratio or VMR) is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Aggravated by vitamin D supplementation
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment or supplementation with vitamin D.

name: Aggravated by sun exposure
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that becomes worse with exposure to sunlight.
comments: This feature represents a clinically observed pattern of symptom worsening in disorders like CYP24A1-related infantile idiopathic hypercalcemia.

name: Tubular accumulation of uromodulin
definition: Accumulation of uromodulin within renal tubular cells or lumina.
comments: This feature is typically observed in UMOD-related tubulointerstitial kidney disease.

name: Elevated stool reducing substances
definition: Elevated level of reducing substances in the feces. If carbohydrate malabsorption is suspected, a reducing substance should be investigated in the stool using the Benedict or Fehling test. The presence of reducing substances may indicate an abnormality in carbohydrate (e.g., sucrose, lactase) metabolism. The unabsorbed sugars in stool are measured as reducing substances.

name: Osteochondral lesion of talus
definition: Osteochondral lesion of the talus (OLT) is an injury involving the articular cartilage and subchondral bone, defined as any damage involving both articular cartilage and subchondral bone of the talar dome. OLT can cause ankle joint pain and can sometimes lead to instability and manifest as an area of abnormal, damaged cartilage and bone on the top of the talus bone (the lower bone of the ankle joint).

name: Mallet toe
definition: A mallet toe involves the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint [such that] the distal phalanx is flexed on the middle phalanx.
comments: The etiology of mallet toe is varied, and has been attributed to anatomy and toe length, shoewear, trauma, or a factor in systemic neurologic disease. With a fixed mallet toe deformity, patients often complain of pain at the dorsal DIP joint, and/or pain at the tip of the affected toe, where undue pressure from footwear and weight bearing is experienced. Calluses may be found at either of these locations. When symptoms can no longer be tolerated with treatments such as modified shoewear and padding in a patient without underlying systemic disease, surgical intervention may be indicated.

name: Bunionette deformity
definition: The bunionette, or tailor's bunion, is a lateral prominence of the fifth metatarsal head. Most commonly, bunionettes are the result of a widened 4-5 intermetatarsal angle with associated varus of the metatarsophalangeal joint.
comments: Radiologically, foot radiographs showing varus deformity at the 5th metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint as measured by increased 4th-5th intermetatarsal angle (Imore than 8 degrees), increased lateral deviation angle (more that 7 degrees), or increased width of 5th metatarsal head (more than 14mm).

name: Elevated CSF beta chorionic gonadotropin concentration
definition: The concentration of beta chorionic gonadotropin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: CSF is marker for monitoring tumor recurrence or evaluation of treatment results in individuals with malignant germ cell tumor.

name: Pigment epithelium detachment
definition: Separation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) from the underlying Bruch membrane.
comments: Pigment epithelial detachment (PED) is a common feature in patients with exudative age-related macular degeneration. The prevalence of a PED has been reported to be 10-64% in eyes with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy, and 10-22% in eyes with typical exudative AMD with choroidal neovascularization. The natural course is characterised by enlargement of the PED with consecutive regression and atrophy of the RPE and outer retina in avascular PEDs or formation of a disciform scar in vascularized PEDs.

name: Retinal gliosis
definition: A pathological condition characterized by the proliferation of glial cells in the retina, often occurring as a reactive response to injury, inflammation, or degenerative changes, and typically resulting in structural and functional alterations in the retina.

name: Aphakia
definition: Absence of the crystalline lens in the eye, which may be congenital or acquired (e.g., following surgical removal of the lens for cataracts or trauma).

name: Pain on thumb extension
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort that is triggered upon extension (straightening) of the thumb.
comments: Pain on thumb extension may be observed in extensor pollicus longus (EPL) tendonitis.

name: Fractured lunate bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the lunate bone.

name: Fractured triquetrum bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the triquetrum bone.

name: Fractured pisiform bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the pisiform bone.

name: Fractured trapezium bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the trapezium bone.

name: Fractured trapezoid bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the trapezoid bone.

name: Fractured capitate bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the capitate bone.

name: Fractured hamate bone
definition: A partial or complete breakage of the hamate bone.

name: Pulsatile abdominal mass
definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling in the abdomen that pulses or throbs.
comments: Clinical palpation of a pulsating abdominal mass alerts the clinician to the presence of a possible abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA).

name: Nonpulsatile abdominal mass
definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling in the abdomen that does not pulse or throb.

name: Iatrogenic anophthalmos
definition: A form of acquired anophthalmos resulting from surgical removal of the eye (enucleation or evisceration), typically performed due to trauma, intraocular tumors, intractable pain in a blind eye, or severe infection. Unlike congenital anophthalmos, the orbit may have previously developed normally and prosthetic rehabilitation is often pursued.

name: Reduced erythrocyte glutathione peroxidase
definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of glutathione peroxidase (EC 1.11.1.9) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.
comments: Glutathione peroxidase catalzyes the reaction 2 glutathione + H2O2 = glutathione disulfide + 2 H2O.

name: Elevated circulating malonyl carnitine concentration
definition: The concentration of malonylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

synonyms.text: Elevated levels of malonylcarnitine in blood acylcarnitine profile

name: Sertoli cell hypoplasia
definition: Abnormal decrease in the number of Sertoli cells in the testis.

name: Positive talar tilt test
definition: An abnormal result of the talar tilt test. This test assesses ankle ligament integrity, particularly the calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) and the deltoid ligaments. To perform the test, the foot is placed at an angle of 90 degrees with the leg, the calcaneofibular ligament is perpendicular and the anterior talofibular ligament is parallel to the long axis of the talus. Therefore, inversion in this position results in strain on the calcaneofibular ligament.
comments: Post-traumatic laxity is defined as excessive joint range of motion beyond normal physiologic range of motion.

name: Plantar ecchymosis
definition: A purpuric lesion that is larger than 1 cm in diameter and is located on the sole of the foot.
comments: Plantar ecchymosis may be observed in Lisfranc Injury.

name: Prolonged exposure to axillary pressure
definition: History of prolonged compressive pressure in the axillary region.
comments: Prolonged compressive pressure in the axillary region is a risk factor for compressive radial mononeuropathy.

name: Lateral ankle pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the outer side of the ankle.

name: Medial ankle pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the inner side of the ankle.

name: Posterior ankle pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back of the ankle.

name: Anterior ankle pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front of the ankle.

name: Exacerbated by colchicine
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with colchizine.

name: Retinal periphlebitis
definition: A condition characterized by inflammation of the outer walls of retinal veins, often presenting as vascular sheathing or exudates along the venous walls.
comments: Periphlebitis is commonly associated with inflammatory and systemic diseases such as sarcoidosis, multiple sclerosis, or Behcet disease. It may lead to retinal vascular occlusion or neovascularization.

name: Purulent pericardial effusion
definition: Elevated leukocyte count in the pericardial fluid ranging from a a microscopic purulent pericardial effusion to gross pus in the pericardial space.
comments: Bacterial pericarditis occurs by direct infection during trauma, thoracic surgery, or catheter drainage, by spread from an intrathoracic, myocardial, or subdiaphragmatic focus, and by hematogenous dissemination. The frequent causes are Staphylococcus and Streptococcus (rheumatic pancarditis), Haemophilus, and M. tuberculosis.

name: Conjunctival erosion
definition: A condition characterized by the localized loss or breakdown of the conjunctival epithelium, often resulting in exposure of the underlying tissue. Conjunctival erosion may cause symptoms such as redness, irritation, foreign body sensation, and tearing. It can result from trauma, chemical injuries, ocular surface diseases, or prolonged use of contact lenses.

name: Positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis sputum culture
definition: Growth of mycobacterium tuberculosis in a sputum culture.

name: Increased external rotation of shoulder
definition: Increased rotation of the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side).

name: Positive trunk flexion test
definition: The proband is asked to flex the trunk forward with knees straight. The result of the test is considered positive (abnormal) if the palms can be made to rest flat on the floor.

synonyms.text: Abnormal forward flexion of the trunk manoeuvre
Increased forward flexion of the trunk
Trunk flexion with palms on floor

comments: This item is elicited as one of the nine points of the Beighton Score (BS), a set of manoeuvres in a nine-point scoring system, used as the standard method of assessment for Generalised Joint Hypermobility.

name: Tibiotalar arthritis
definition: AP, oblique, or lateral view x-ray of the ankle showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the tibiotalar joint.

name: Anterior ankle osteophyte
definition: Imaging study of the ankle revealing osteophyte (bone spur) formation at the anterior aspect of the ankle (tibial or talar neck).
comments: This finding may be associated with tibiotalar synovitis, capsular thickening, scar, and granulation tissue as well.

name: Midfoot arthritis
definition: AP, oblique, or lateral view x-ray of the foot showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis in the midfoot (tarsometatarsal (TMT) joints, naviculocuneiform joint, intercuneiform joints, and/or metatarsal cuneiform joints), such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the tibiotalar joint.
comments: Midfoot includes Tarso-metatarsal (TMT) joints and naviculo-cuneiform joints (NCJ). Talo-navicular joint (TNJ) and calcaneocuboid joint (CCJ) are considered to be part of hindfoot along with sub-talar joint. Tarso-metatarsal joints are divided into three columns anatomically: the medial column (First Tarsometatarsal joint), the middle column (second and third TMT joints) and the lateral column (Fourth and Fifth TMT or Metatarsocuboid joints). TMT joints are collectively known as Lisfranc joints as well.

name: Decreased circulating reverse T3 concentration
definition: Concentration of reverse T3 (3,3',5'-triiodothyronine or rT3) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Stocking-glove distribution
definition: Distribution of findings in hands and feet with a distal to proximal gradient of severity (being more severe in the more distal locations).
comments: Early peripheral neuropathy may present as sensory alterations that are often progressive, including sensory loss, numbness, pain, or burning sensations in a stocking and glove distribution of the extremities.

name: Hairy kidney sign
definition: A radiological sign related to infiltration of histiocytes into the kidneys and perirenal fat. This infiltration, along with thickening of fibrous bands within the perirenal fat, creates a hairy appearance on cross-sectional imaging studies.
comments: Erdheim-Chester disease is a non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis characterized by the infiltration of foamy histiocytes with fibrosis that can affect many organs, most commonly long bones. Renal involvement commonly manifests in this disease as a histiocytic infiltration into the perirenal fat.

name: White appearance of duodenal mucosa
definition: On a typical diet (e.g., no dietary fat restriction), the intestinal mucosa may have a gelee blanche or white hoar frosting appearance on endoscopy.

synonyms.text: Gelee blanche appearance of duodenal mucosa
White hoar frosting appearance of duodenal mucosa

comments: This finding may be observed in APOB-related familial hypobetalipoproteinemia. Biopsy of the intestinal epithelium may demonstrate lipid-laden epithelial cells.

name: Acromioclavicular joint separation
definition: An acromioclavicular (AC) joint joint separation, often called a shoulder separation, is a dislocation of the clavicle from the acromion. This feature is ascertainable radiographically by AC joint x-ray views including bilateral anteroposterior (AP) view, axillary lateral view, and/or Zanca view showing either superior, posterior, or inferior displacement of the distal clavicle in relation to the acromion at the AC joint.
comments: The AC joint is a diarthrodial joint spanning from the medial articular facet of the acromion to the distal clavicle and links the shoulder girdle to the axial skeleton.

name: Acromioclavicular joint arthritis
definition: Degenerative disease of the acromioclavicular (AC) joint that manifests radiographically as Zanca view X-ray of the AC joint showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the AC joint.

name: Positive shoulder cross-body adduction test
definition: A test used with suspected chronic acromioclavicular joint lesions (which are a common source of pain and disability in the shoulder). The test is considered positive with pain in the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint when patient straightens the affected arm forward and reaches for the contralateral shoulder with extra manual cross body (adduction) pressure on the arm from the examiner.

name: Proximal humeral epiphysiolysis
definition: Proximal humeral epiphysiolysis (Little League shoulder) is a shear or stress injury of the epiphyseal cartilage of the proximal humerus. Anteroposterior (AP) view of the shoulder in external rotation showing widening of the proximal humerus physis in comparison to contralateral shoulder with possible metaphyseal bony irregularity.

name: Positive anterior drawer test
definition: A test for ankle instability in which an anterior pull on the calcaneus with is applied with one hand while stabilizing the end of the tibia/fibula with the other hand. The test is considered positive (abnormal) if it results in more than one cm of anterior translation of the foot compared to the healthy, contralateral ankle.
comments: A positive anterior drawer test indicates possible damage or tearing of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) or the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL).

name: Peroneal tendon tear
definition: Injury to a peroneal tendon, as can be ascertained by an MRI study of the ankle showing partial or complete tear of one or both of the peroneal tendons.

name: Fifth metatarsal apophysitis
definition: Iselin's disease is a traction apophysitis of base of fifth metatarsal. The apophysis is within the peroneus brevis tendon insertion site and appears radiographically at about age 10 in female and age 12 in male and usually fuses by age 11 in female and by age 14 in male. Repetitive microtrauma from the peroneus brevis tendon, as occurs in sports activities is the cause of traction apophysitis. It can be ascertained by oblique foot radiographs showing apophyseal irregularity (enlarged apophysis, disordered ossification, widened chondro-osseous junction) at the base of the fifth metatarsal.

name: Tibial tubercle apophysitis
definition: Lateral knee radiograph showing tibial tuberosity apophysis irregularity and fragmentation; tibial tubercle osteochondrosis; traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle.
comments: The patellar tendon inserts at the tibial tubercle and consists of cartilaginous tissue. This is followed by ossification of the tibial tubercle at ages 10-12 in girls and at ages 12-14 in boys. It is during this stage of bone maturation when Osgood Schlatter disease develops. The prevailing theory is that there is repeated traction over the tubercle leading to microvascular tears, fractures, and inflammation; which then presents as swelling, pain, and tenderness.

name: Enteric anendocrinosis
definition: Near absence of small intestinal and colonic endocrine cells. This feature can be ascertained histopathologically and may also be manifested as a lack of staining for enteroendocrive markers such as synaptophysin.
comments: Enteroendocrine cells (EECs) are gut epithelial hormone-secreting cells, influenced by diet and the microbiome. EECs regulate local gastrointestinal functions and systemic signalling, including communication with the brain, while being linked to various diseases.

name: Metatarsal head osteochondrosis
definition:
Avascular necrosis of a metatarsal head, most commonly involving the second, but also the third or fourth, metatarsal.
Comment: Affected individuals may present with foot pain on weight-bearing, swelling, and tenderness. Radiological features include widening of the metatarsophalangeal joint space and flattening of the affected metatarsal head, at later stages metatarsal head sclerosis, cortical thickening, and intra-articular loose bodies. Osteochondrosis is a condition resulting from an epiphysis injury that alters enchondral ossification and produces irregularity at the joint surface. Freiberg disease is characterized as osteochondrosis of the metatarsal heads (primarily the second).

name: Hallux sesamoiditis
definition: Inflammation of the sesamoid bones of the hallux ( two ovoid-shaped ossicles embedded within the tendons under the big toe). This feature can be ascertained by MRI of the foot, revealing edema within one or both of the hallux sesamoids.

name: Os trigonum
definition: Os trigonum (OT) is one of the most common accessory ossicles in the foot and ankle region. In clinical practice, OT is a considerable factor that may predispose patients to posterior ankle impingement syndrome (PAIS). Lateral ankle x-ray with foot in plantarflexion reveals an accessory ossicle at the posterior aspect of the talus, between the posterior distal tibia and calcaneal tuberosity.

name: Positive heel squeeze test
definition: The squeeze test is the most common examination for diagnosing calcaneal apophysitis (Sever disease) and is conducted by compressing the medial and lateral aspects of the calcaneus. The test is considered positive (abnormal) if squeezing elicits pain.

name: Calcaneal apophysitis
definition: Inflammation of the calcaneal apophysis (bony projection where the Achilles tendon attaches to the heel). Lateral foot x-ray shows increased density in the calcaneal apophysis or fragmentation of the apophysis.

name: Decreased circulating guanidinoacetic acid concentration
definition: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Elevated circulating C-triol concentration
definition: The concentration of cholestane-3beta, 5alpha, 6beta-triol (C-triol) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. C-triol is a diagnostic biomarker for Niemann-Pick disease type C.

name: Germinal vesicle oocyte maturation arrest
definition: A type of oocyte maturation arrest that occurs prior to the breakdown of the germinal vesicle (which is a hallmark of reinitiation of meiosis I and entry into M phase).

name: Metaphase II oocyte maturation arrest
definition: The morphologic classification of MII generally denotes an oocyte that is mature, having arrested in metaphase II and is presumed to be capable of fertilization. However, there are subsets of women who produce oocytes with MII morphology that are not capable of embryo formation even with fertilization. This incongruence between morphologic maturity and capacity could be attributed to either the inclusion within the morphologic classification immature oocytes arrested at any stage between PBI formation and metaphase II, which are not capable of fertilization, or oocytes arrested normally at metaphase II that do not possess the ability to complete meiosis.

name: Mixed oocyte maturation arrest
definition: A type of oocyte maturation failure whereby oocytes arrest at more than one stage of meiosis.

name: Dorsal forearm pain
definition: Pain localized to dorsal (non-palmar) aspect of the forearm.
comments: Dorsal forearm pain can be observed with radial tunnel syndrome.

name: Volar forearm pain
definition: Pain on the volar (palmar) aspect of the forearm.
comments: Volar forearm pain can be observed with conditions such as pronator syndrome.

name: Cholesterol gallbladder polyp
definition: A non-neoplastic gallbladder polyp that is hyperplastic and consists of a lipid deposit. Cholesterol polyps are generally less than 10 mm. often multiple cholesterol polyps are present. They are often associated with vesicular cholesterolosis and are thought to have no malignant potential.

name: Hyperlordotic gait
definition: A gait abnormality characterized by excessive lumbar lordosis (swayback posture, i.e., an inward curvature of the lower spine) and gait pattern with forward tilt of the pelvis and increased lumbar curvature. Hyperlordotic gait is often as a compensatory mechanism for hip extensor weakness, proximal muscle weakness, or hip flexion contracture.
comments: Typically seen in patients with muscular dystrophy due to axial and core muscle weakness.

name: Radioulnar interosseous membrane tear
definition: A tear in the fibrous sheet connecting the radius and ulna bones in the forearm.

name: Fleck sign of elbow
definition: A radiograpzhic sign in which small bone fragments detached from the olecranon are seen on lateral radiographs in cases with avulsion of the tendon.
comments: See Figure 2 of PMID:28461956.

name: Resisted wrist flexion provokes pain
definition: Active wrist flexion against resistance increases pain in the arm.
comments: This sign may be observed with conditions such as medial epicondylitis and lexor carpi radialis tendonitis.

name: Lateral epicondylitis of the elbow
definition: A chronic symptomatic degeneration of the wrist extensor tendons involving their attachment to the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, and is associated clinically with lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow). This term refers to the associated imaging finding. Ultrasound imaging showing extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) tendon thickening and hypoechoic areas with increased vascularity or MRI showing increased signal intensity or tear at the insertion site of the ECRB on the lateral aspect of the elbow.

name: Medial epicondylitis of the elbow
definition: Medial epicondylitis, often referred to as golfer's elbow, is a common pathology. Flexor-pronator tendon degeneration occurs with repetitive forced wrist extension and forearm supination during activities involving wrist flexion and forearm pronation. This term refers to the associated imaging finding. Ultrasound imaging showing ECRB tendon thickening and hypoechoic areas with increased vascularity or MRI showing increased signal intensity or tear at the insertion site of the common flexor tendon.

name: Popeye sign
definition: Exaggerated bulging of the belly of the biceps muscle upon contraction.
comments: The Popeye sign involves hump formation caused by bulging of the biceps muscle because of biceps tendon tear. The bulging is more noticeable with elbow flexion and is said to resemble the biceps muscle of the cartoon character Popeye.

name: Distal biceps tendon rupture
definition: Rupture (tear) of the distal biceps tendon. Ultrasound imaging showing complete discontinuity of the distal biceps tendon or MRI revealing complete distal biceps tendon discontinuity or increased signal intensity in the distal biceps tendon.

name: Proximal biceps tendon rupture
definition: Rupture (tear) of the proximal biceps tendon. MRI reveals a tear of the proximal aspect of the biceps tendon near its site of origin at the supraglenoid tubercle.

name: Positive bursal fluid infectious agent test
definition: Detection of an infectious agent, or evidence thereof, in aspirated bursal fluid using microbiological, molecular, or antigen-based testing methods.

name: Acute retinal necrosis
definition: A condition characterized by the death of retinal tissue due to ischemia, infection, or inflammation.
comments: Retinal necrosis can result from vascular occlusion, viral infections such as varicella-zoster virus (VZV) or cytomegalovirus (CMV), or autoimmune processes. Clinically, acute retinal necrosis presents with retinal whitening, hemorrhages, and potential retinal detachment, often leading to severe visual impairment or blindness if untreated.

name: Cystic changes in greater tuberosity of the humerus
definition: Cystic lesions of the proximal humerus are commonly encountered on routine shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). True cysts are defined as fluid-filled structures or lesions with an epithelial lining, whereas pseudocysts are fluid-filled lesions without epithelial lining. Cystic lesion encompasses both true cysts, pseudocysts and other lesions which could mimic the appearance of a cyst on MRI, with increased signal on fluid sensitive sequences.
comments: Cystic lesions of the humeral head are commonly encountered on routine shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Differential diagnoses include degenerative lesions, calcific tendinitis with osseous involvement, perianchor cysts, abscesses and less often, tumours. Degenerative lesions, including subcortical and subchondral cysts, are the most commonly encountered. These may be associated with rotator cuff disease and degenerative joint diseases or considered part of ageing depending on the location of the cystic lesions.

name: Positive Hawkins test
definition: Manual internal rotation on the forearm with the shoulders flexed forward to 90 degrees, elbows bent to 90 degrees so that the forearm is parallel to the ground, and palm facing down recreates pain in the shoulder region; named after Dr. Hawkins.

name: Hallux weakness
definition: Reduced ability to exert force or power with the hallux (big toe), i.e., reduced strength of the hallux.

name: Hallux dorsiflexion weakness
definition: Reduced ability to lift the big toe (hallux) upward toward the shin.

name: Hallux plantarflexion weakness
definition: Reduced ability to push the big toe (hallux) downward, away from the shin.

name: Forefoot pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized about the metatarsal heads in the front part of the foot.

name: Spur at inferior pole of patella
definition: A bone spur (osteophyte), i.e., de novo bone formation at the lower edge of the patella (knee cap). Radiographically, it is visible as calcification at inferior pole of the patella.
comments: This finding is characteristic of Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease.

name: Urinary ascites
definition: The presence of urine in the peritoneal cavity, an entity that typically results from bladder rupture or damage to the ureters.
comments: Urinary ascites is commonly due to an obstructive uropathy or a neurogenic bladder.

name: Abnormal mixed venous oxygen saturation
definition: Abnormal oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2). SvO2 can be measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery. The SvO2 is dependent on arterial oxygen saturation, hemoglobin concentration, cardiac output, and tissue oxygen demands.
comments: A fall in SvO2 usually implies anemia, arterial oxygen desaturation, and/or decreased cardiac output; however, a normal or high value does not exclude such disturbances. When employed in conjunction with the other indicators of tissue oxygenation available in an intensive care unit, SvO2 can be useful as a guide for both prognosis and urgency of therapy.

name: Elevated circulating lysosphingomyelin concentration
definition: The concentration of lysosphingomyelin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) or Niemann-Pick type A/B is a lysosomal disorder caused by the deficiency of acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) due to pathogenic variants in the SMPD1 gene. Sphingomyelin (SM) is the substrate for ASM that cleaves the phosphorylcholine linkage of SM producing ceramide. SM is a major compound of most cell membranes and coupled with cholesterol constitutes most of the membrane rafts. In the deficiency of ASM, there is primary storage of SM, and the concentration of lysosphingomyelin in dried blood spots and in the blood circulation is typically elevated.

name: Abnormal lens capsule morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of the lens capsule, the smooth, transparent, acellular basement membrane that envelops the lens of the eye and serves as the attachment site for the lens zonules and the lens epithelium.

name: Posterior capsule opacification
definition: Posterior capsule opacification, also known as secondary cataract, is the most frequent complication following manual extracapsular cataract extraction. Secondary cataract results from the proliferation and migration of residual epithelial cells in the posterior region of the lens capsule into the visual axis, leading to thickening and reduction in transparency (opacification), which in turn can cause a decrease in visual acuity.

name: Bronchial stenosis
definition: A narrowing (constriction) of the lumen of a bronchus, which may involve one or more of the major airways branching from the trachea.
comments: Bronchial stenosis may affect the main bronchi, lobar bronchi, or segmental bronchi. Clinical manifestations depend on the location and severity of narrowing and can include wheezing, dyspnea, recurrent pneumonia, or asymmetric lung ventilation on imaging.

name: Skin tenting due to fracture
definition: Skin tenting may occur in the setting of a fracture when a displaced bone fragment pushes on the skin, causing it to bulge outward in a tent-like shape.

name: Follicular conjunctivitis
definition: A type of conjunctivitis characterized by the formation of conjunctival follicles, which appear as raised domes on the are round collections of lymphocytes, and are often most prominent in the inferior fornix (interior part of the lower eyelid).

name: Granulomatous conjunctivitis
definition: A type of conjunctivitis characterized by the formation of conjunctival granulomata, i.e., localized nodular inflammatory lesions of the conjunctiva, characterized histologically by aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes, often with multinucleated giant cells, surrounded by lymphocytes and fibroblasts.

name: Areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation that follow Blaschko lines
definition: Linear streaks of hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation that are distributed according to Blaschko lines, which are V-shaped, S-shaped, or linear patterns on the skin that reflect the embryonic migration pathways of epidermal cells (keratinocytes, melanocytes, etc.) during early development.

name: Retinal drusen
definition: Small focal extracellular deposits underneath the retina, visible ophthalmoscopically as yellow dots.
comments: Drusen are lipid-, mineral-, and protein-containing extracellular deposits that accumulate between the basal lamina of the retinal pigment epithelium and Bruch's membrane of the human eye. They are a defining feature of age-related macular degeneration, a common sight-threatening disease of older adults.

name: Intrauterine amputation
definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of a limb or digit at birth, resulting from interruption of normal limb development in utero.
comments: The two main mechanisms involve amniotic band disruption (constriction of a developing limb or digit by fibrous amniotic bands) and vascular disruption (e.g., thrombosis, hemorrhage, or ischemia).

name: Intrauterine digital amputation
definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of a finger or toe at birth, resulting from interruption of normal development in utero.

name: Intrauterine limb amputation
definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of an arm or leg at birth, resulting from interruption of normal development in utero.

name: Proximal interphalangeal joint arthritis
definition: Inflammation and deterioration of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints. Radiographically, PIP arthritis can be characterized by PIP joint space narrowing, subchondral cysts, and osteophytes.
comments: PIP arthritis manifests clinically with swollen, tender PIP joints, with a more diffuse, swollen appearance and a fusiform joint contour. Joint stiffness is almost always present and often correlates with the degree of swelling.

name: Dorsal intercalated segment instability
definition: A nondissociative form of carpal instability, in which the lunate bone angulates to the dorsal side of the hand.
comments: Carpal instability can be defined as the lack of ligamentous and bony support to maintain a wrist stable to external forces.

name: Disruption of carpal arcs
definition: The arcs of the Gilula are used on PA wrist radiographs as part of assessing the normal alignment of the carpus. The 1st arc (red) outlines the proximal surfaces and the 2nd arc (yellow) the distal surfaces of the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum. The 3rd arc (white) outlines the proximal surfaces of the capitate and hamate. Disruption of carpal arcs (i.e., the arcs appear broken or discontinuous on radiographs) indicates a fracture or ligamentous injury in the wrist.

name: Spilled teacup sign of the wrist
definition: Dislocation of the lunate bone, generally as a result of trauma. Volar displacement of the lunate is said to result a tipped teacup.
comments: Lateral wrist x-ray showing proximal dorsal displacement of the capitate and volar displacement of the dislocated lunate in a flexed position.

name: Positive Finkelstein sign
definition: Finkelstein's test produces severe tenderness and usually pain on the radial aspect of the wrist when the thumb is flexed into the palm and the wrist is ulnar deviated.
comments: The Finkelstein test is a provocative test for diagnosis of De Quervain disease that can easily be performed in an office setting or at the bedside.

name: Forefoot abduction
definition: Outward deviation or turning of the front part of the foot away from the body's midline. An anteroposterior foot x-ray shows increased Simmon angle (angle between the talus and first metatarsal, normal is 7 degrees plus/minus 4 to 5 degrees) or increased talonavicular uncoverage of over 30 to 40 percent. A common clinical observation is the too many toes sign; when viewed from behind, more than two toes will flare out laterally due to the valgus alignment of the foot.

name: Posterior tibial tendon injury
definition: Damage to the posterior tibialis tendon, which runs along the inside of the ankle and foot, supporting the arch of the foot. MRI or ultrasound of the ankle/foot shows posterior tibial tendon degeneration such as tendinosis, tenosynovitis, edema around the tendon, or tendon tear.
comments: The posterior tibialis muscle originates from the posterior proximal tibia, interosseous membrane and proximal fibula; it is in the deep posterior compartment of the leg and turns at the medial malleolus, changing its line of pull from the vertical one to the horizontal one. The myotendinous junction is situated at the distal third of the leg and only the tendinous portion turns at the medial malleolus; anterior subluxation is prevented by a flexor retinaculum which binds the tendon into the shallow groove at the medial malleolus.

name: Plantar pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to palpation of plantar aspect of the foot (the sole).

name: Flexor hallucis longus tendon injury
definition: Damage to the flexor hallucis longus (FHL) tendon. The FHL tendon is a long tendon that runs from the deep calf muscle down through the ankle to the big toe, enabling toe flexion and supporting foot mechanics.. MRI or ultrasound of the ankle/foot shows degenerative changes of the FHL tendon such as fluid around the tendon at the level of the ankle joint, intra-substance tendinous signal, tendon thickening, tendonitis, or tenosynovitis, or tendon rupture.

name: Hallux pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the big toe (hallux).

name: Pain on the medial aspect of the foot
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the side of the foot nearest to the big toe (hallux).

name: Hallux sesamoid injury
definition: Damage affecting one or both of the two small, pea-shaped bones (sesamoids) embedded in the tendons beneath the first metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe. Foot x-ray shows fracture, subluxation, or dislocation of the sesamoid of the hallux.

name: Radial wrist pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the radial side of the wrist.

name: Volar wrist pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the volar side of the wrist (i.e., to the palm side - front - of the wrist).

name: Dorsal wrist pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the dorsal side (back) of the wrist.

name: Peroneal tendon tenderness
definition: Pain elicited with palpation along the course of the peroneal tendons, located posterior to the lateral malleolus and extending distally toward the base of the fifth metatarsal.

name: Peroneal tendon subluxation
definition: Dynamic ultrasound of the lateral ankle showing subluxation or dislocation of one or both of the peroneal tendons out of the peroneal groove.

name: Peroneal tendon injury
definition: Ankle MRI or ultrasound showing edema or thickening of peroneal tendon(s), fluid within peroneal tendon sheath, or a partial or complete tear in one or both of the peroneal tendons.

name: Elevated circulating succinylacetone concentration
definition: The concentration of succinylacetone in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Succinylacetone can be created by the oxidation of glycine, and is a precursor of methylglyoxal. Succinylacetone is an abnormal tyrosine metabolite that arises from defects in the enzyme called fumarylacetoacetase.

name: Flat palate
definition: Reduced height of the palate. A flat palate is present with a palatal index angle below 30 degrees, a normal palate with an angle between 30 and 45 degrees, and a steep palate with an angle above 45 degrees.

name: Elevated circulating C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type1 collagen concentration
definition: The concentration of C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type1 collagen in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type1 collagen is a biomarker of bone resorption.

name: Exacerbated by pulmonary vasodilator exposure
definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with a pulmonary vasodilator medication such as prostacyclin analogs, endothelin receptor antagonists, and phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors.

name: Mercury exposure
definition: History of exposure to mercury.

name: Urinoma
definition: Encapsulated collections of urine around the kidney in the retroperitoneum, most commonly in the perirenal space, as a consequence of renal tract leakage caused by urinary obstruction, trauma, or post-instrumentation.

name: Umbilical discharge
definition: Abnormal fluid draining from the umbilicus (from wounds, surgical sites, or fistulas).
comments: The dischanrge may be serous, purulent, bloody, or foul-smelling.

name: Abnormal biparietal diameter
definition: Abnormal biparietal diameter (BPD) refers to a fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone on an ultrasound image, that lies outside the expected range for a given gestational age. The expected range typically falls between the 10th and 90th percentiles, with microcephaly defined as a BPD below the 3rd percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations below the mean) and macrocephaly defined as a BPD above the 97th percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations above the mean).

name: Abnormal fetal femur length
definition: Femur length is measured between the outer border of one end of the the femoral diaphysis to the other outer border, excluding the epiphysis or other artifact. Abnormal femur length is defined as being more than two standard deviations away from the mean.

name: Pain exacerbated by wrist ulnar deviation
definition: Pain worsens with wrist ulnar deviation (i.e., the pain is exacerbated if the hand is moved towards the side with the fifth finger).

name: Pain exacerbated by wrist radial deviation
definition: Pain worsens with wrist radial deviation (i.e., the pain is exacerbated if the hand is moved towards the side with the thumb).

name: Ulnar positive variance
definition: A phenomenon whereby the distal ulna articular surface is more distal than the distal radius articular surface.
