comments: The triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC) is a well-defined anatomical entity of the wrist joint known as the primary stabilizing structure of the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ). The TFCC provides considerable DRUJ stability. The instability of DRUJ caused by the foveal tear of the TFCC also results in an abnormal anatomic relationship between the radius and ulna. When the foveal attachment of the TFCC is disrupted, the ulnar head is free to sublux dorsally relative to the sigmoid notch of the radius, which is aggravated under the stress of pronation. This change in the anatomic relationship between the radius and ulna can be easily observed on plain radiographs.

name: Negative ulnar variance
definition: Negative ulnar variance is a condition in which the ulna is relatively shorter than the radius at the carpus. AP wrist X-ray shows the distal ulna articular surface more proximal than the distal radius articular surface.
comments: Negative ulnar variance may be observed in Kienbock disease.

name: Flexor carpi radialis tendonitis
definition: Inflammation of the flexor carpi radialis (FCR) tendon, which traverses the carpus through a narrow fibro-osseous tunnel.
comments: Flexor carpi radialis (FCR) tendinitis is an uncommon but important cause of volar radial wrist pain. The FCR tendon may become inflamed primarily or as a sequelae of carpometacarpal arthroplasty, arthritis, or trauma.

name: Transillumination test shows high light transmission
definition: A transillumination test involves shining light through an area of the body or a mass. This term refers to a transillumination test that shows especially high (positive) transillumination, which may be observed when a mass or swelling contains clear fluid rather than solid tissue or blood.
comments: Ganglion cysts may show high transillumination.

name: Hyperleukocytosis
definition: Hyperleukocytosis is commonly defined as a white blood cell (WBC) count of greater than 100,000 luekocytes per microliter.
comments: Hyperleukocytosis can be observed in conditions such as acute myeloid leukemia, which is characterized by the clonal proliferation of hematopoietic stem cells. Hyperleukocytosis is regarded as a hematological emergeny and can lead to complications such as leukostasis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and tumor lysis syndrome.

name: Elbow instability
definition: Impairment of the ability of the elbow joint to maintain proper anatomical alignment and functional mechanics. Elbow instability is a spectrum from subluxation to dislocation, with corresponding clinical and pathologic features and therapeutic implications.

name: Valgus instability of the elbow
definition: A type of elbow instability that arises through injuries to the medial collateral ligament (MCL), specifically the anterior bundle (AMCL). In the valgus stress test, the elbow is placed in 20 to 30 degrees of flexion with the forearm supinated and a valgus stress is applied. The test is positive when no firm end point is palpated, greater than 1 mm of medial joint opening is noted (fluoroscopically), or there is reproduction of the patient's pain.
comments: Medial collateral ligament injuries may occur after trauma, such as an elbow dislocation, or as a repetitive overuse injury, commonly seen in overhead-throwing athletes. The typical history includes a pop and medial elbow pain following throwing activities, or patients may present with recurrent medial elbow pain, classically during the late cocking to early acceleration phase of throwing. Athletes typically complain of a progressive loss of velocity, accuracy, and endurance, which may be exacerbated by glenohumeral internal rotation deficits common to throwing athletes. The physical examination typically elicits tenderness over the MCL.

name: Varus instability of the elbow
definition: A type of elbow insttability characterized by abnormal widening or gapping of the lateral (radial) side of the elbow joint when a varus stress is applied, due to insufficiency of the lateral collateral ligament complex.

name: Limited foot eversion
definition: Decreased foot eversion secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.
comments: This feature is assocaited with a reduced foot range of motion and may be experienced as a stiff foot.

name: Limited foot inversion
definition: Decreased foot inversion secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.
comments: This feature is assocaited with a reduced foot range of motion and may be experienced as a stiff foot.

name: Positive synovial Tropheryma whipplei bacteria microscopy
definition: Demonstration of Tropheryma whipplei bacteria in the synovial (joint) fluid by microscopic analysis.

name: Positive calf squeeze test
definition: An abnormal result of the calf-squeeze test (also known as the Thompson test), which is considered a sign of Achilles tendon rupture. The test is positive (abnormal) if no plantar flexion of the foot occurs at calf squeezing.
comments: With the patient laying prone and feet hanging over the edge of a table, passive squeeze of the calf does not reproduce normal plantarflexion of the foot.

name: Achilles tendon tear
definition: A partial or complete break in the Achilles tendon (the tendon that connects the gastrocnemius and soleus to the calcaneus). This feature can be ascertained by magnetic resonance imaing (MRI) of the foot/ankle showing partial or complete tear of the achilles tendon.

name: Positive bursa fluid gram stain
definition: Demonstration of the presence of bacteria by gram staining of bursa fluid. The sample is generally obtained by bursal fluid aspiration.

name: Abnormal medial epicondyle morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of the medial epicondyle, which is the site of the attachment of various muscles, including the radial and ulnar flexor of the wrist, the superficial flexor of the fingers, the palmaris longus and the pronator teres muscle.

name: Medial humerus epicondyle avulsion fracture
definition: An avulsion fracture of the medial epicondyle of the elbow. Radiological examination in the anteroposterior and lateral projection can be used to make the diagnosis and to determine the degree and direction of the fracture displacement.

name: Hand mass
definition: A swelling or enlargement localized to the hand. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

name: Tenosynovitis
definition: Inflammation of the synovial sheath that surrounds a tendon.
comments: Tenosynovitis can be ascertained as hypoechoic or anechoic thickened tissue with or without fluid within the tendon sheath, which is seen in 2 perpendicular planes and which may exhibit Doppler signal.

name: Tigroid fundus
definition: Enhanced visibility of large choroidal vessels through the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). This reticulated pattern is commonly observed on fundus examination and color fundus photography. Such hypopigmented areas alternate with hyperpigmented zones in a tigroid pattern. Fundus tessellation is often associated with myopia and choroidal thinning.
comments: Tigroid fundus may be a normal variant or an early phenotypic indicator of various retinal or choroidal diseases. In pathological conditions such as high myopia, age-related choroidal atrophy, or inherited retinal dystrophies, FT may reflect underlying structural alterations in the choroid, RPE, or sclera, some of which may predispose to significant visual impairment

name: Decreased myocardial glycogen content
definition: The amount of glycogen in the myocardial tissue of the heart is below the lower limit of normal.

synonyms.text: Glycogen depletion in cardiac muscle tissue

name: CSF anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein.
comments: CSF anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity can be seen in MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), multiple sclerosis, and other neuroimmunological diseases.

name: Spinal cord H sign
definition: The H sign can be ascertained by spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and represents spinal cord myelitis isolated to the gray matter. A longitudinally extensive T2 hyperintense spinal cord lesion from C6 to T10, predominantly involving the gray matter. The appearance of the anomaly is said to resemble the letter H.

synonyms.text: H sign in the spinal cord

comments: The H sign can be observed with Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), multiple sclerosis, and other neuroimmunological diseases.

name: Abnormal testosterone: estradiol ratio
definition: Any deviation from the normal ratio of testosterone and estradiol (the primary sex steroids) to each other. The testosterone:estradiol ratio is derived from total testosterone in ng/dL and total estradiol in pg/mL, and expressed as T:E. Normal ranges are affected by sex, age, and other factors.
comments: There is a natural balance between the major sex steroids, testosterone and estradiol, controlled by gonadal secretion and peripheral conversion by aromatase. This balance is impacted by a variety of inborn and acquired conditions.

name: Abnormal circulating insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration
definition: The concentration of IGFBP-3 (Insulin-like Growth Factor-Binding Protein 3) in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.

name: Decreased circulating insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration
definition: The concentration of insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration (IGF3) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Airway chondritis
definition: Inflammation of the cartilage of the airway, including especially the trachea and bronchi.

name: Costochondritis
definition: inflammation of the costal cartilage (the cartilage that connects the ribs to the sternum). The typical presentation of costochondritis is bilateral parasternal chest wall pain exacerbated by deep breaths, coughing, and stretching. The upper (predominantly second through fifth) costochondral and/or costosternal junctions are most commonly involved. The areas of tenderness are not generally accompanied by heat, erythema, or localized swelling.

synonyms.text: Inflammation of he cartilage that connects the ribs to the sternum (breastbone)

name: History of ocular surgery
definition: Past medical history of surgical procedure on the eye or its surroundings.

name: Increased plantar fascia thickness
definition: Increased thickness of the plantar fascia. This finding can be ascertained by ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging.
comments: The plantar fascia, also called the plantar aponeurosis, is a strong connective tissue structure that helps maintain the longitudinal arch of the foot. The diagnosis of plantar fasciitis generally relies on clinical history and physical examination. The main symptoms include pain and stiffness in the morning, or pain at the beginning of activity after rest. Physical examination reveals tenderness at the origin of the PF and impaired dorsiflexion of the ankle and extension of the toes. MRI or ultrasound of the foot show thickening of the plantar fascia (over 4.5mm) or increased signal within the plantar fascia.

name: Increased mixed venous oxygen saturation
definition: Oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2), as measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: Decreased mixed venous oxygen saturation
definition: Oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2), as measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery, is below the lower limit of normal.

name: Chocolate brown blood
definition: Characteristic chocolate-brown color of circulating blood with an elevated methemoglobin content.

name: Elevated pCO2 gap
definition: The difference between the venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide saturation (Pv-aCO2) is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Central venous-arterial carbon dioxide difference (PCO2 gap) can be a marker of cardiac output adequacy in global metabolic conditions that are less affected by the impairment of oxygen extraction capacity.

name: Putaminal eye sign
definition: An imaging anomly of the putamen that is thought to be pathognomic for MEGDEL syndrome (3-MethylGlutaconic aciduria, Deafness, Encephalopathy, Leigh-like syndrome MIM #614739). In stage 1 of the disease, T2 signal changes of the pallidum are present. In stage 2, swelling of the putamen and caudate nucleus is seen. The dorsal putamen contains an eye that shows no signal alteration and (thus) seems to be spared during this stage of the disease. It later increases, reflecting progressive putaminal involvement. Sparing of the mid dorsal putamen (showing normal signal surrounded by T2 hyperintense signal) is referred to as the putaminal eye.

name: Decreased coracohumeral distance
definition: Axial view on shoulder X-ray or MRI showing decreased distance between posterior border of the coracoid process and anterior border of the humeral head of less than 6 mm; subcoracoid impingement; decreased coracohumeral interval.
comments: Decreased coracohumeral distance can be observed in conditions such as rotator cuff tear and shoulder external impingement syndrome.

name: Abnormal deltoid muscle morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the deltoid muscle, the large triangular intrinsic shoulder muscle, so named because its shape resembles the inverted Greek letter delta.

name: Deltoid muscle tear
definition: An injury of the deltoid muscle of the shoulder or its tendon characterized by partial or complete rupture.

name: Glenohumeral arthritis
definition: Anteropostrior (AP), axillary, or Grashey (true AP) view X-ray of the shoulder showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the glenohumeral joint.

name: Dental root fusion
definition: An anomaly of the roots of a multi-rooted tooth (such as a molar) in which the roots are not physically divided by bone or periodontal ligament space.
comments: Root fusion may be formed either by the combining of roots because of cementum deposition with time or as a result of the failure of the Hertwig epithelial root sheath to develop or fuse in the furcation area, which is frequently found in maxillary and mandibular premolars and molars. In mandibular molars, root fusion usually presents as a C-shaped root, whereas in maxillary molars fused roots may show various root shapes, such as two or more roots being fused partially or completely.

name: Difficulty floating in water
definition: A phenomenon whereby an individual struggles to float, cannot swim despite adequate training, or simply sinks. This phenomenon may be observed in individuals with conditions such as osteopetrosis that are characterized by substantially increased bone mineral density (which implies reduced bouyancy).

name: Aortitis
definition: Aortitis refers to inflammatory changes to the wall of the aorta and incorporates both infectious and non-infectious etiologies.
comments: The term aortitis encompasses inflammatory changes to the aortic wall from varying etiologies that are associated with certain specific histopathological lesions. The inflammatory response may be limited to the aortic wall or accompanied by changes directly adjacent to the vessel (e.g. retroperitoneal fibrosis) or other vessels (e.g., giant cell arteritis). A distinction is made between infectious and non-infectious aortitis. Takayasu arteritis and giant cell arteritis are the most common causes of non-infectious aortitis.

name: Upper extremity claudication
definition: Pain in an arm that is triggered by muscular exertion.
comments: This anomaly is observed in the setting of a patient with axillary or subclavian artery disease.

name: Tongue claudication
definition: Pain in the tongue induced by speaking or chewing.

name: Cerebral perivascular enhancement pattern
definition: Focal, regional or diffuse magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enhancement of intracranial perivascular spaces (PVS). This enhancement pattern is recognizable by its topography that follows PVS distribution, particularly identifiable in regions where PVS predominate (centra semiovalia, basal ganglia and the brachium pontis)15 although it can be found throughout the whole brain. Depending on the perpendicular or parallel orientation of MRI sections to the long axis of PVS, enhanced PVS appear as dots or curvilinear elements respectively. Depending on the causal pathology, PVE may appear more linear or nodular.
comments: Perivascular spaces (PVS) are fluid-filled structures that form the immediate peripheral environment of small cerebral vessels. They are a central component of the glymphatic system, which plays a crucial role in maintaining cerebral homeostasis.

name: Long head of biceps tendon dislocation
definition: Dislocation or subluxation of the long head of the biceps tendon out of the bicipital groove (as documented by magnetic resonance imaging of the shoulder) or dynamic ultrasound of the shoulder showing subluxation or dislocation of the long head of the biceps tendon out of the bicipital groove.
comments: Isolated dislocation of the long head of the biceps is a rare entity. In most cases, dislocation of the biceps tendon out of the bicipital groove is usually associated with tears of the subscapularis tendon or massive rotator cuff tears (or both).

name: Elevated circulating somatostatin concentration
definition: The concentration of somatostatin in the blood corculation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: Somatostatin is a 14 amino acid polypeptide whose principal function is to regulate growth hormone release from the pituitary. Elevated serum and synovial fluid somatostatin levels have been associated with inflammatory responses most notably in rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Lack of attached gingiva
definition: Absence of attached gingiva. The gingiva is subdivided into the nonattached free gingiva (which includes the gingival margin and the papillae) and the attached gingiva. The attached gingiva is tightly and unmovably bound to the periosteum via collagen type I fibers. The gingiva is keratinized and thicker than the mucosa to provide mechanical protection. The border between attached gingiva and mucosa constitutes the mucogingival junction. In vivo, it is sometimes visible as a white line . The oral mucosa is loosely connected to the periosteum and nonkeratinized. It is movable, thin, more fragile, translucent, and blood vessels are visible.

name: Spontaneous diaphragmatic rupture
definition: A full thickness tear of the diaphragm without significant trauma.
comments: Spontaneous diaphragmatic rupture is a rare complication of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in which abnormal collagen synthesis results in tissue fragility and weakness of the diaphragm, predisposing to full-thickness tearing without significant trauma, typically triggered by a sudden increase in intra-abdominal pressure such as coughing, vomiting, or physical exertion, and resulting in herniation of abdominal contents into the thoracic cavity.

name: Elevated alveolar-arterial (A-a) oxygen gradient
definition: An increase in the difference between the oxygen concentration in the alveoli and arterial system above the upper limit of normal.
comments: The A-a gradient, or the alveolar-arterial gradient, measures the difference between the oxygen concentration in the alveoli and arterial system. The A-a gradient has important clinical utility as it can help narrow the differential diagnosis for hypoxemia. The A-a gradient calculation is as follows: A-a Gradient = PAO2 - PaO2. In this equation, PAO2 represents alveolar oxygen pressure and PaO2 representing arterial oxygen pressure. The arterial oxygen pressure (PaO2) can be directly assessed with an arterial blood gas test (ABG) or estimated with a venous blood gas test (VBG). The alveolar oxygen pressure (PAO2) is not easily measured directly; instead, it is estimated using the alveolar gas equation. The A-a gradient may be increased in clinical conditions such as pneumonia, with poor diffusion of oxygen across the alveolar-capillary unit and thus lower oxygen levels in the arterial blood (because of the physical barrier within the alveoli, limiting the diffusion of oxygen into the capillaries).

name: Abnormal concentration of circulating metanephrines
definition: Adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine are degraded by catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) to form their inactive metabolites metanephrine, normetanephrine and 3-methoxytyramine (3-MT). When there is an indication for biochemical testing, such as suspicion of pheochromocytoma, metanephrine and normetanephrine metabolites are measured in plasma or 24-hour urine. This term represents an elevation of the concentration of metanephrine and normetanephrine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: Elevated circulating 3-O-methyldopa concentration
definition: The concentration of 3-O-methyldopa in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: 3-O-methyldopa (3-OMD) is produced by the methylation of L-DOPA by catechol-O-methyltransferase. 3-OMD may be elevated in the plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of Parkinson's disease patients taking L-DOPA and it is also observed to be elevated in individuals with Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency.

name: Elevated CSF 3-O-methyldopa concentration
definition: The concentration of 3-O-methyldopa in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
comments: 3-O-methyldopa (3-OMD) is produced by the methylation of L-DOPA by catechol-O-methyltransferase. 3-OMD may be elevated in the plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of Parkinson's disease patients taking L-DOPA and it is also observed to be elevated in individuals with Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency.

name: Fixed fetal head flexion
definition: An unchanging bending forward of the fetal head in the uterus as visualized by prenatal sonography. This sign can be defined as a lack of change in this position during the 30 min of observation. Additionally, identical head flexion is observable several times at intervals.
comments: This feature has been observed in fetuses with Multiple pterygium syndrome, lethal type.

name: Abnormal rectosigmoid index
definition: The rectosigmoid (R/S) ratio, a measure comparing rectal to sigmoid colon diameter, is below the lower limit of normal on prenatal ultrasound. The rectosigmoid is normally the widest segment of the fetal colon. If the rectosigmoid is narrower than the ascending or transverse colon above it), this is called a reversed rectosigmoid ratio or abnormal rectosigmoid index. The RS ratio is calculated by dividing the transverse rectal diameter by the sigmoid diameter. An R/S ratio of 1 or more is considered normal.
comments: An abnormal rectosigmoid ratio may indicate Hirschsprung disease.

name: Umbilical cord edema
definition: Visible edema (swelling) in a cord with a minimal cross sectional area of 1-3 cm2. This may result from an excessive accumulation of Wharton jelly, resulting in a thick or edematous umbilical cord.

name: Fetal enterolithiasis
definition: Enterolithiasis (concretions or stones forming within the gastrointestinal tract) is a prenatal sonographic sign defined by hyperechogenic foci within the - often distended - fetal bowel.

name: Malignant cells in CSF
definition: The identification of malignant cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), generally by microscopic examination of the CSF.

name: Greek warrior helmet sign
definition: A prenatal sonographic finding characterized by a high forehead, prominent glabella, and a broad, un-tapered nasal bridge that merges directly into the brow line. This appearance is said to resemble a Greek (Corinthian) warrior helmet because the wide, solid vertical column down the center of the face is said to resemble the fixed, protective nose guard of a Corinthian helmet.
comments: This sign is suggestive of the Wolf-Hirschhorn (4p-) syndrome.

name: Somatostatinoma
definition: Somatostatinoma is a rare, functional neuroendocrine tumor (NET) that primarily arises in the pancreas and duodenum, characterized by excessive production of somatostatin.
comments: A somatostatinoma secretes somatostatin, which typically inhibits numerous gastrointestinal and endocrine functions. Clinically, this condition often presents with a classic triad of diabetes mellitus, cholelithiasis, and steatorrhea, resulting from hormonal suppression. On noncontrast CT, somatostatinomas typically appear isodense relative to pancreatic parenchyma. Endoscopic ultrasound is highly sensitive and specific for detecting pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms, including lesions smaller than 5 mm. Somatostatin receptor-based positron emission tomography (PET) using appropriate radiolabeled ligands demonstrates excellent sensitivity and specificity for tumor localization and staging.

name: Erythematous scalp plaque
definition: A circumscribed, palpable, potentially elevated, erythematous lesion > 1 cm in diameter and localized to the scalp. Erythematous plaques exhibiting erythema, i.e., abnormal redness of the skin due to localized dilation and congestion of superficial dermal capillaries, typically as a result of inflammation, irritation, infection, or vasodilation, and usually blanching with pressure.
comments: Erythematous plaque of the scalp may be observed in dermatomyositis and often are pruritic.

name: Positive hair pull test
definition: An abnormal result of the hair pull test, in which the clinician selects 50 to 60 hairs and holds the bundle close to the scalp between the thumb, index finger, and long finger. The clinician then firmly pulls on the bundle using slow traction as the fingers slide down the hair shaft, avoiding a fast and forceful tug. The hair pulls are performed at the vertex, parietal areas, and the occipital area of the scalp. Next, the pulled hairs are counted. Any broken hairs that were extracted from the bundle during the pull are discarded. If more than 10 percent of the hairs in each bundle are removed from a scalp area, the hair pull test is considered positive.
comments: If fewer than 10% are removed, then the hair loss can usually be attributed to normal shedding. If a test is positive in more than one scalp region, the clinician must consider telogen or anagen effluvium. Other hair disorders (ie, alopecia areata) may only have a positive hair pull test in the affected area. The hair pull test is ideally used for monitoring the advancing edge of alopecia areata, acute cases of telogen effluvium, anagen effluvium, and loose anagen syndrome.

name: Loss of acquired purposeful hand skills
definition: A type of neurodevelopmental regression characterized by deterioration or disappearance of previously acquired voluntary, goal-directed hand movements, such as reaching, grasping, manipulating objects, or self-feeding.

name: Loss of acquired spoken language
definition: A type of neurodevelopmental regression characterized by deterioration or disappearance of previously acquired expressive verbal communication, including words, phrases, or sentences the individual had used meaningfully, after these skills had been acquired during development.
comments: Loss of acquired language is based on best acquired spoken language skill, not strictly on the acquisition of distinct words or higher language skills.

name: Postnatal deceleration of headgrowth
definition: Slowing of the rate of head circumference growth occurring after birth, in an individual with normal head circumference at birth, leading to progressive deviation from normal growth curves and, in many cases, acquired (postnatal, secondary) microcephaly.
comments: The human brain undergoes dramatic changes in size and connectivity after birth. From birth to age six years, the brain increases in size by four-fold, reaching 90 percent of adult volume. During normal development, the growth of head circumference is largely driven by growth of underlying brain tissue.

name: Foot small muscle atrophy
definition: Wasting of the small muscles of the foot such as the abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, and the interossei muscles.
comments: This sign may indicate diabetix neuropathy of length-dependent polyneuropathies such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
